cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Gears for intersecting shafts: bevel gears (straight, spiral, zerol). Mitre gears are bevel gears with equal size at 90°.

why.en: Teeth are cut on a cone.

recall_q.en: Gears used when shafts intersect?

explain_simple.en: Cone-shaped gears turn the corner.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Hypoid gears: like spiral bevel but the pinion axis is offset below the crown wheel axis. Used in rear axle differentials.

why.en: The offset lowers the propeller shaft and floor.

recall_q.en: Gears used in most rear axle final drives?

explain_simple.en: Offset bevel gears in the differential.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Hypoid gears need special extreme-pressure (EP) gear oil.

why.en: Teeth slide a lot under heavy pressure.

recall_q.en: Which oil is used for hypoid gears?

explain_simple.en: Special thick oil for heavy-pressure teeth.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Worm and worm wheel: for non-parallel, non-intersecting shafts at 90°. Gives very high speed reduction and is often self-locking.

why.en: One turn of the worm moves the wheel by only one tooth (single start).

example.en: Steering gearboxes (worm and sector).

recall_q.en: Which gear pair gives high reduction and self-locking?

explain_simple.en: A screw turning a wheel slowly.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Rack and pinion turns rotary motion into straight-line motion.

why.en: The rack is a gear with infinite radius (flat).

example.en: Rack and pinion steering in cars.

recall_q.en: Which gear converts rotary motion to linear motion?

explain_simple.en: A round gear moving a flat toothed bar.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Pitch circle: imaginary circle on which two gears roll together without slip. Its diameter is the pitch circle diameter (PCD).

why.en: All gear calculations use it.

recall_q.en: Imaginary circle on which mating gears roll?

explain_simple.en: The rolling circle of a gear.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Module m = pitch circle diameter / number of teeth (D/T), in mm.

why.en: Gears that mesh must have the same module.

recall_q.en: Formula for module?

explain_simple.en: Tooth size number.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Circular pitch p = π D / T = π m. Diametral pitch P = T / D (teeth per inch).

why.en: Circular pitch is the distance from one tooth to the next along the pitch circle.

recall_q.en: Circular pitch in terms of module?

explain_simple.en: Gap between teeth along the circle.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Addendum: tooth height above the pitch circle (= 1 module). Dedendum: depth below it (= 1.25 module).

why.en: Dedendum is larger to give clearance.

recall_q.en: Addendum of a standard gear tooth?

explain_simple.en: Above the circle = addendum; below = dedendum.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Clearance = dedendum − addendum. Backlash = gap between mating teeth on the pitch circle.

why.en: Backlash allows for oil, heat expansion and errors.

recall_q.en: Play between mating teeth is called?

explain_simple.en: A small gap so teeth do not jam.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Pressure angle: angle between the line of action and the common tangent to pitch circles. Standard: 20° (also 14.5°).

why.en: 20° teeth are stronger.

recall_q.en: Standard pressure angle of gears?

explain_simple.en: The angle at which teeth push each other.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Involute tooth profile is most common because centre distance can vary slightly without affecting the velocity ratio.

why.en: Easy to make and tolerant of errors.

recall_q.en: Most common gear tooth profile?

explain_simple.en: The standard curved tooth shape.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Velocity ratio = N₁/N₂ = T₂/T₁ = D₂/D₁.

why.en: Speeds are inversely proportional to tooth numbers.

example.en: A 10-tooth pinion driving a 40-tooth gear: ratio 4:1; output is 4 times slower and 4 times the torque.

recall_q.en: Driver 20 teeth, driven 60 teeth: velocity ratio?

explain_simple.en: Small gear spins fast, big gear spins slow.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Two meshing external gears turn in opposite directions. An idler gear between them makes the driven gear turn the same way as the driver.

why.en: Each mesh reverses direction.

example.en: Reverse gear uses an idler.

recall_q.en: Purpose of an idler gear?

recall_a.en: To change direction of rotation (without changing ratio).

explain_simple.en: An extra gear in the middle flips the direction.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Simple gear train: one gear on each shaft. Compound gear train: two or more gears on the same shaft.

why.en: Compound trains give large ratios in small space.

recall_q.en: Gear train with two gears on one intermediate shaft?

explain_simple.en: Simple = one per shaft. Compound = two on a shaft.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Train value = speed of last gear / speed of first gear = product of driver teeth / product of driven teeth.

why.en: Multiply each stage's ratio.

recall_q.en: Train value of a compound train?

recall_a.en: Product of driver teeth ÷ product of driven teeth.

explain_simple.en: Multiply the ratios of each pair.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Reverted gear train: first and last gears are on the same axis.

why.en: Used in lathes, clocks and car gearboxes (input and output in line).

recall_q.en: Gear train where input and output shafts are co-axial?

explain_simple.en: In and out on the same line.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Epicyclic (planetary) gear train: sun gear, planet gears on a carrier, and an annulus (ring) gear. Some axes move.

why.en: Gives several ratios in a compact unit.

example.en: Automatic gearboxes and differentials use epicyclic trains.

recall_q.en: Three main members of an epicyclic gear train?

recall_a.en: Sun gear, planet carrier (with planets), annulus (ring).

explain_simple.en: Planets spinning around a sun inside a ring.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Gear materials: case-hardened alloy steel for vehicle gears; cast iron for large slow gears; nylon/plastic for light quiet drives.

why.en: Hard surface resists wear; tough core resists shock.

recall_q.en: Why are car gears case-hardened?

recall_a.en: Hard wear-resistant surface with tough core.

explain_simple.en: Hard skin, tough inside.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Interference: tip of one tooth digs into the root of the mating tooth. Happens when the pinion has too few teeth.

why.en: Minimum teeth (about 17 for 20° full-depth) avoids it.

recall_q.en: What causes interference in gears?

recall_a.en: Too few teeth on the pinion.

explain_simple.en: Small pinions' teeth dig into the other gear.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

title.en: Worked example: gear ratio and speed

text.en: Question: A 15-tooth pinion at 1500 rpm drives a 45-tooth gear. Find gear speed.

explain.en: Speed is inversely proportional to teeth.

text.en: Ratio = 45/15 = 3 : 1, so torque is about 3 times.

summary.en: More teeth → slower and more torque.

recall_q.en: Pinion 15 T at 1500 rpm, gear 45 T: gear speed?

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Parallel: spur, helical, herringbone; intersecting: bevel; skew: worm, hypoid.
Module m = D/T; circular pitch = πm.
Addendum 1m, dedendum 1.25m, pressure angle 20°.
VR = T₂/T₁; idler reverses direction.
Simple, compound, reverted, epicyclic trains.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A boiler (steam generator) is a closed vessel that turns water into steam using heat from fuel.

why.en: Steam drives engines and turbines.

recall_q.en: What does a boiler do?

explain_simple.en: A closed pot that makes steam.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Fire tube boiler: hot gases pass through tubes surrounded by water. Water tube boiler: water flows inside tubes surrounded by hot gases.

why.en: Water tube boilers handle higher pressure and make steam faster.

recall_q.en: Boiler where hot gases pass through tubes?

explain_simple.en: Fire in tubes, or water in tubes.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Fire tube boilers: Cochran, Lancashire, Cornish, locomotive, Scotch marine. Water tube boilers: Babcock & Wilcox, Stirling, La Mont, Benson, Loeffler.

why.en: PSC asks to classify named boilers.

recall_q.en: Is Babcock & Wilcox a fire tube or water tube boiler?

explain_simple.en: Cochran, Lancashire, locomotive = fire tube. Babcock & Wilcox = water tube.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Lancashire boiler has two large fire tubes (flues). Cornish boiler has one.

why.en: Two flues give more heating surface.

recall_q.en: How many fire tubes in a Lancashire boiler?

explain_simple.en: Cornish one, Lancashire two.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Cochran boiler is a vertical, multi-tubular fire tube boiler. Locomotive boiler is a horizontal multi-tubular fire tube boiler.

why.en: Both are compact for their output.

recall_q.en: Is a Cochran boiler vertical or horizontal?

explain_simple.en: Cochran stands up.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Benson boiler is a supercritical, drum-less water tube boiler. La Mont is a forced circulation boiler.

why.en: Above critical pressure water turns to steam without boiling.

recall_q.en: Which boiler works above critical pressure and has no drum?

explain_simple.en: Benson = no drum, very high pressure.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Boiler mountings are fittings needed for safe working: safety valve, water level indicator, pressure gauge, fusible plug, steam stop valve, feed check valve, blow-off cock, manhole.

why.en: The law requires them on every boiler.

recall_q.en: Are mountings needed for safety or efficiency?

explain_simple.en: Mountings keep the boiler safe.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Boiler accessories improve efficiency: economiser, superheater, air preheater, feed pump, injector, steam separator.

why.en: They recover waste heat or improve steam.

recall_q.en: Is an economiser a mounting or accessory?

explain_simple.en: Accessories save fuel; mountings save lives.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Safety valve releases steam when pressure goes above the safe limit. Types: dead weight, lever, spring loaded, high-steam low-water.

why.en: Prevents boiler explosion.

recall_q.en: Mounting that prevents excess steam pressure?

explain_simple.en: Lets out steam when pressure is too high.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Fusible plug melts when the water level falls too low, letting steam put out the fire.

why.en: Overheated, dry boiler plates could burst.

recall_q.en: Which mounting protects against low water level by melting?

explain_simple.en: A plug that melts to save a dry boiler.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Economiser heats feed water using exhaust flue gases. Air preheater heats combustion air using flue gases.

why.en: Both recover waste heat.

recall_q.en: Accessory that heats feed water with flue gases?

explain_simple.en: Use waste smoke heat to warm the water.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Superheater heats saturated steam above its saturation temperature, making it dry and superheated.

why.en: Superheated steam gives more work and less turbine erosion.

recall_q.en: Which accessory makes superheated steam?

explain_simple.en: Makes steam extra hot and dry.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Feed check valve lets water into the boiler but stops it flowing back. Blow-off cock removes sludge from the bottom.

why.en: Keeps water in and dirt out.

recall_q.en: Mounting used to remove sediment from a boiler?

explain_simple.en: Drains the mud out.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Steam engine parts: cylinder, piston, piston rod, crosshead, connecting rod, crank, slide valve, eccentric, flywheel, governor.

why.en: Steam pushes the piston; crank turns this into rotation.

recall_q.en: Part connecting piston rod to connecting rod in a steam engine?

explain_simple.en: Piston → piston rod → crosshead → connecting rod → crank.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Steam engine working: the slide valve admits steam alternately to both sides of the piston (double acting), and the exhaust leaves from the other side.

why.en: This gives two power strokes per revolution.

recall_q.en: What admits steam to the cylinder in a simple steam engine?

explain_simple.en: A sliding valve sends steam to each side in turn.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Steam engine is an external combustion, reciprocating engine. Its eccentric works like a small crank to move the slide valve.

why.en: Fuel burns in the boiler, not in the cylinder.

recall_q.en: Is a steam engine internal or external combustion?

explain_simple.en: Fire is outside the cylinder.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Wet steam contains water droplets. Dry saturated steam has no droplets. Dryness fraction = mass of dry steam / total mass.

why.en: Wet steam carries less energy.

recall_q.en: Dryness fraction of dry saturated steam?

explain_simple.en: 1 = fully dry; less than 1 = wet.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Indian Boilers Act 1923 governs boiler registration and inspection in India. Boiler inspection is done by the Factories and Boilers Department.

why.en: Boilers are dangerous pressure vessels.

recall_q.en: Which Act governs boilers in India?

explain_simple.en: Boilers need a licence under the 1923 Act.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Fire tube: Cochran, Lancashire, locomotive. Water tube: Babcock & Wilcox, Benson.
Mountings (safety): safety valve, fusible plug, gauge, water level.
Accessories (efficiency): economiser, superheater, air preheater.
Steam engine: slide valve, eccentric, crosshead.
Dryness fraction 1 = dry steam.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Ferrous metals contain iron (cast iron, steel). Non-ferrous metals do not (aluminium, copper, lead, tin, zinc).

why.en: Iron-based metals are strong but rust; non-ferrous ones are lighter or resist rust.

recall_q.en: Is aluminium ferrous or non-ferrous?

explain_simple.en: Ferrous = has iron.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Pig iron comes from the blast furnace. Cast iron has 2–4.5% carbon. Steel has up to about 2% carbon. Wrought iron is almost pure iron.

why.en: Carbon content decides the type.

recall_q.en: Carbon content of cast iron?

explain_simple.en: More than 2% carbon = cast iron.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Cast iron is brittle, cheap, easy to cast, good in compression, damps vibration and wears well. It is weak in tension.

why.en: Graphite flakes inside act like tiny cracks.

example.en: Cylinder blocks, brake drums, flywheels, manhole covers.

recall_q.en: Is cast iron strong in tension or compression?

explain_simple.en: Cast iron takes squeezing, not pulling.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Grey cast iron: carbon as graphite flakes, grey fracture. Most common; used for engine blocks and brake drums.

why.en: Graphite gives good machinability and damping.

recall_q.en: Cast iron used for cylinder blocks?

explain_simple.en: Grey CI = flakes of graphite.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: White cast iron: carbon as cementite (iron carbide). Very hard and brittle; white fracture. Used for wear parts.

why.en: Fast cooling keeps carbon combined.

recall_q.en: Which cast iron contains cementite and is very hard?

explain_simple.en: White CI = hard and brittle.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Malleable cast iron: made by long heat treatment (annealing) of white cast iron. It is tougher and slightly ductile.

why.en: Carbide changes to rounded graphite clumps.

recall_q.en: Malleable cast iron is made from which iron?

explain_simple.en: Bake white CI to make it less brittle.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Spheroidal graphite (SG) or ductile iron: graphite as spheres, made by adding magnesium or cerium. Strong and ductile.

why.en: Round graphite does not act like cracks.

example.en: Crankshafts, camshafts and steering knuckles.

recall_q.en: Element added to make SG (nodular) cast iron?

explain_simple.en: Round graphite balls make CI tough.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Chilled cast iron: surface cooled fast to make it hard white iron, while the core stays grey. Used for cams and rolls.

why.en: Hard skin, tough inside.

recall_q.en: Cast iron with hard white surface and grey core?

explain_simple.en: Fast-cooled skin is hard.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Steel is an alloy of iron and carbon with carbon up to about 2% (usually less than 1.5%).

why.en: Small carbon makes iron much stronger.

recall_q.en: Maximum carbon in steel?

explain_simple.en: Iron + a little carbon = steel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Plain carbon steels: dead mild (below 0.15% C), mild/low carbon (0.15–0.3%), medium carbon (0.3–0.6%), high carbon (0.6–1.5%).

why.en: More carbon = harder and stronger, but less ductile.

recall_q.en: Carbon range of medium carbon steel?

explain_simple.en: Low, medium, high carbon by percent.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Mild steel uses: chassis frames, body panels, nuts, bolts, rivets, pipes.

why.en: It is ductile, weldable and cheap.

recall_q.en: Steel commonly used for chassis frames and rivets?

explain_simple.en: Mild steel is easy to bend and weld.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Medium carbon steel uses: crankshafts, axles, connecting rods, gears. High carbon steel: springs, cutting tools, files.

why.en: More carbon gives hardness for wear and springiness.

recall_q.en: Which carbon steel is used for leaf springs and tools?

explain_simple.en: High carbon = hard and springy.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Steel designation in India (IS): e.g. C40 means plain carbon steel with 0.40% carbon (older: 40C8).

why.en: The number gives carbon in hundredths of a percent.

recall_q.en: Carbon content in C45 steel?

explain_simple.en: C number ÷ 100 = carbon %.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Iron–carbon diagram phases: ferrite (soft), cementite (hard), pearlite (ferrite + cementite layers), austenite (high-temperature phase), martensite (very hard, from quenching).

why.en: Heat treatment changes these phases.

recall_q.en: Hardest phase formed by quenching steel?

explain_simple.en: Quench it fast and it turns very hard.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Eutectoid steel has 0.8% carbon and is fully pearlite. Below 0.8% = hypo-eutectoid; above = hyper-eutectoid.

why.en: 0.8% is the special point on the iron–carbon diagram (at 723°C).

recall_q.en: Carbon percentage of eutectoid steel?

explain_simple.en: 0.8% carbon = all pearlite.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Heat treatment: heating and cooling a metal in a controlled way to change its properties.

why.en: It can make steel softer, harder or tougher.

recall_q.en: Define heat treatment.

recall_a.en: Controlled heating and cooling to change properties of metal.

explain_simple.en: Cook and cool metal to change how it behaves.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Purposes of heat treatment: relieve stresses, soften for machining, harden for wear, improve toughness, refine grain.

why.en: Each job needs different properties.

recall_q.en: Give two purposes of heat treatment.

recall_a.en: Harden, soften, relieve stress, refine grain, improve toughness.

explain_simple.en: To make metal harder, softer or tougher.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Annealing: heat steel above the critical temperature, hold, then cool very slowly in the furnace. Makes it soft and ductile.

why.en: Slow cooling gives soft, coarse pearlite.

recall_q.en: Heat treatment with very slow furnace cooling?

explain_simple.en: Heat and cool slowly → soft.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Normalising: heat above critical temperature, then cool in still air. Gives fine grain and uniform structure.

why.en: Air cooling is faster than furnace cooling.

recall_q.en: Heat treatment with cooling in still air?

explain_simple.en: Heat and let it cool in air → even grain.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Hardening: heat steel above critical temperature, then quench quickly in water or oil. Makes it very hard but brittle.

why.en: Fast cooling forms martensite.

recall_q.en: Quenching hot steel in water or oil is called?

explain_simple.en: Heat and dunk → hard.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Tempering: reheat hardened steel to a lower temperature (below critical) and cool. Reduces brittleness, adds toughness.

why.en: It relieves stresses from quenching.

recall_q.en: What is done after hardening to reduce brittleness?

explain_simple.en: Warm it again a little to make it less brittle.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Case hardening (surface hardening) makes a hard outer case with a tough core. Methods: carburising, nitriding, cyaniding, carbonitriding, flame hardening, induction hardening.

why.en: Gears and camshafts need wear-resistant skin and shock-resistant core.

recall_q.en: Name two case hardening methods.

explain_simple.en: Hard skin, soft tough heart.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Carburising adds carbon to the surface of low carbon steel at high temperature, then it is hardened.

why.en: Low carbon steel cannot be hardened unless carbon is added.

recall_q.en: Case hardening by adding carbon to the surface?

explain_simple.en: Soak the surface in carbon.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Nitriding adds nitrogen to the surface using ammonia gas at about 500°C. No quenching is needed.

why.en: Nitrides formed are very hard.

recall_q.en: Which case hardening uses ammonia gas?

explain_simple.en: Nitrogen skin, no quench.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Cyaniding adds both carbon and nitrogen using a molten cyanide salt bath.

why.en: Gives a thin, hard case quickly.

recall_q.en: Case hardening in a molten sodium cyanide bath?

explain_simple.en: A salt bath gives carbon and nitrogen.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Induction and flame hardening heat only the surface quickly, then quench. Used for crankshaft journals and gear teeth.

why.en: Only the skin reaches hardening temperature.

recall_q.en: Hardening using high-frequency electric current?

explain_simple.en: Heat just the skin and quench.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Alloy steel contains added elements such as nickel, chromium, manganese, molybdenum, vanadium, tungsten, silicon.

why.en: Each element adds a special property.

recall_q.en: What is alloy steel?

recall_a.en: Steel with extra alloying elements (Ni, Cr, Mo, V…).

explain_simple.en: Steel with added spices.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Nickel: toughness and strength. Chromium: hardness and corrosion resistance. Manganese: strength, hardness, removes sulphur effect.

why.en: Know which element gives which property.

recall_q.en: Which element gives corrosion resistance to steel?

explain_simple.en: Chromium stops rust; nickel adds toughness.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Molybdenum: strength at high temperature. Vanadium: fatigue strength and fine grain. Tungsten: hardness at red heat (tools). Silicon: springiness, magnetic properties.

why.en: PSC often asks element-property pairs.

recall_q.en: Element giving red hardness to high speed steel?

explain_simple.en: Tungsten keeps tools hard when hot.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Stainless steel has at least 10.5% chromium (typical 18% Cr + 8% Ni, '18/8').

why.en: Chromium forms a thin oxide layer that blocks rust.

example.en: Exhaust tail pipes and trims.

recall_q.en: Composition of 18/8 stainless steel?

explain_simple.en: Chromium + nickel = stainless.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: High speed steel (HSS) 18-4-1: 18% tungsten, 4% chromium, 1% vanadium. Used for cutting tools and drills.

why.en: It stays hard at high cutting temperatures.

recall_q.en: Composition of 18-4-1 HSS?

explain_simple.en: Tool steel with lots of tungsten.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Exhaust valve steel: silchrome (silicon-chromium) or austenitic stainless steel (21-4N). Inlet valves: plain chromium or nickel-chrome steel.

why.en: Exhaust valves face red heat and corrosive gases.

recall_q.en: Common steel for exhaust valves?

explain_simple.en: Exhaust valves need heat-proof steel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Nickel-chrome-molybdenum steels are used for crankshafts, connecting rods, axle shafts and highly stressed gears.

why.en: They combine strength, toughness and fatigue resistance.

recall_q.en: Alloy steel group used for crankshafts?

explain_simple.en: Ni-Cr-Mo for heavily loaded shafts.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Invar (36% nickel steel) hardly expands with heat. Used in precision instruments and some piston struts.

why.en: Its expansion coefficient is very low.

recall_q.en: Nickel steel with almost zero thermal expansion?

explain_simple.en: Invar does not grow when hot.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Aluminium: light (density 2.7 g/cm³, one-third of steel), conducts heat well, resists corrosion. Used for pistons, cylinder heads, alloy wheels, radiators.

why.en: Saves weight and removes heat.

recall_q.en: Why are pistons made of aluminium alloy?

recall_a.en: Light weight and good heat conduction.

explain_simple.en: Aluminium is light and cools fast.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Duralumin: aluminium with about 4% copper, plus manganese and magnesium. Strong and light; used in aircraft and vehicle body parts.

why.en: Age hardening gives it high strength.

recall_q.en: Main alloying element in duralumin?

explain_simple.en: Aluminium + copper = duralumin.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Y-alloy: aluminium with copper, nickel and magnesium. Keeps strength at high temperature; used for pistons and cylinder heads.

why.en: Nickel helps strength when hot.

recall_q.en: Aluminium alloy used for pistons with nickel?

explain_simple.en: Y-alloy pistons stay strong when hot.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Brass = copper + zinc. Bronze = copper + tin. Gun metal = copper + tin + zinc.

why.en: PSC asks alloy compositions very often.

recall_q.en: Composition of brass?

explain_simple.en: Brass: Cu + Zn. Bronze: Cu + Sn.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Phosphor bronze (copper + tin + a little phosphorus) is used for bearings, bushes, worm wheels and springs.

why.en: It resists wear and corrosion.

recall_q.en: Alloy used for gudgeon pin bushes and worm wheels?

explain_simple.en: Bronze with phosphorus for bushes.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Babbitt (white metal): tin + antimony + copper (or lead base). Used for bearing linings.

why.en: Soft, low-friction and embeds dirt.

recall_q.en: Main metal in tin-based babbitt?

explain_simple.en: Soft bearing metal.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Solder (soft solder) = tin + lead. Used to join radiator tubes and electrical wires.

why.en: Low melting point.

recall_q.en: Composition of soft solder?

explain_simple.en: Tin + lead melts easily.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Copper: excellent conductor of heat and electricity. Used in wiring, radiator cores, starter and alternator windings.

why.en: Second only to silver in conductivity.

recall_q.en: Metal used for vehicle wiring?

explain_simple.en: Copper carries current best for its cost.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Lead: heavy and soft. Used in batteries (lead-acid plates) and wheel balancing weights.

why.en: Lead reacts with sulphuric acid to store charge.

recall_q.en: Metal used in car battery plates?

explain_simple.en: Lead-acid battery uses lead.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Zinc is used for galvanising — coating steel to prevent rust.

why.en: Zinc corrodes first and protects the steel (sacrificial).

recall_q.en: Coating steel with zinc is called?

explain_simple.en: A zinc coat stops rust.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Magnesium alloys are the lightest structural metals (density about 1.7 g/cm³). Used for gearbox housings and racing wheels.

why.en: Even lighter than aluminium.

recall_q.en: Lightest structural metal used in vehicles?

explain_simple.en: Magnesium is lighter than aluminium.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Effect of sulphur in steel: red shortness (brittleness when hot). Phosphorus: cold shortness (brittle when cold).

why.en: Both are harmful impurities.

recall_q.en: Which impurity causes cold shortness in steel?

explain_simple.en: Sulphur → hot brittle. Phosphorus → cold brittle.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Plastics and composites in vehicles: bumpers (polypropylene), dashboards (ABS, PVC), fuel tanks (HDPE), leaf springs and body panels (FRP).

why.en: They are light, rust-free and easy to mould.

recall_q.en: Plastic commonly used for bumpers?

explain_simple.en: Plastics save weight and never rust.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Thermoplastics soften on heating and can be remoulded (PVC, polythene, nylon). Thermosetting plastics set permanently (Bakelite, epoxy).

why.en: Thermosets form cross-links that do not melt.

recall_q.en: Is Bakelite thermoplastic or thermosetting?

explain_simple.en: Thermoplastic re-melts; thermoset does not.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

points.en: CI 2–4.5% C: grey, white, malleable, SG, chilled.
Steel: mild < 0.3%, medium 0.3–0.6%, high 0.6–1.5% C.
Anneal (slow), normalise (air), harden (quench), temper (reheat).
Case hardening: carburising, nitriding, cyaniding, induction.
Brass Cu+Zn; bronze Cu+Sn; duralumin Al+Cu; 18/8 stainless.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: The cylinder block is the main body of the engine. It holds the cylinders, coolant passages and crankcase.

why.en: Every other engine part is fixed to it.

recall_q.en: What is the main body of an engine called?

explain_simple.en: The engine's backbone.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Single-cylinder engines (motorcycles) often have a separate cylinder barrel. Multi-cylinder engines usually have all cylinders cast in one block (monobloc).

why.en: One-piece casting is rigid and cheaper for many cylinders.

recall_q.en: A block with all cylinders cast together is called?

explain_simple.en: Many cylinders in one casting.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Cylinder blocks are made of grey cast iron or aluminium alloy.

why.en: Cast iron wears well and damps noise; aluminium is light and cools well.

recall_q.en: Two materials for cylinder blocks?

recall_a.en: Grey cast iron and aluminium alloy.

explain_simple.en: Heavy iron or light aluminium.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Aluminium blocks need cast-iron or steel cylinder liners (or special coatings), because aluminium wears quickly against piston rings.

why.en: Aluminium is soft.

recall_q.en: Why do aluminium blocks use liners?

recall_a.en: Aluminium wears fast; liners give a hard wearing surface.

explain_simple.en: A hard sleeve inside a soft block.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A cylinder liner (sleeve) is a replaceable tube fitted into the cylinder bore.

why.en: When worn, only the liner is changed, not the whole block.

recall_q.en: What is a cylinder liner?

recall_a.en: A replaceable sleeve inside the cylinder bore.

explain_simple.en: A replaceable inner tube for the cylinder.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Dry liner: does not touch the coolant; pressed into the block. Wet liner: touches the coolant directly; sealed with rubber rings at the bottom.

why.en: Wet liners cool better and are easier to replace.

recall_q.en: Which liner is in direct contact with coolant?

explain_simple.en: Wet liner = water touches it. Dry liner = water does not.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Dry liners are thin (about 1.5–3 mm). Wet liners are thicker because they must withstand coolant pressure and gas pressure alone.

why.en: A wet liner has no block wall to support it.

recall_q.en: Which liner is thicker: dry or wet?

explain_simple.en: Wet liners stand alone, so they are thicker.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Liners are made of special alloy cast iron (centrifugally cast), sometimes chrome plated.

why.en: Centrifugal casting gives dense, hard metal.

recall_q.en: Usual liner material?

explain_simple.en: Hard cast iron spun into shape.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Cylinder head closes the top of the cylinders and forms the combustion chamber. It holds valves, spark plugs or injectors.

why.en: Gas pressure acts on it every power stroke.

recall_q.en: Part that closes the top of the cylinders?

explain_simple.en: The lid of the engine.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Cylinder heads are made of cast iron or aluminium alloy. Aluminium heads allow higher compression without knocking.

why.en: Aluminium removes heat faster from the combustion chamber.

recall_q.en: Why can aluminium heads allow higher compression ratio?

explain_simple.en: Cooler head, less knock.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Cylinder head gasket seals the joint between block and head, keeping gas, coolant and oil apart.

why.en: Metal surfaces cannot seal perfectly alone.

recall_q.en: What does the head gasket seal?

recall_a.en: Joint between head and block (gas, coolant, oil).

explain_simple.en: A seal sheet between head and block.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Head gasket materials: copper-asbestos (older), steel-asbestos, multi-layer steel (MLS) in modern engines, composite.

why.en: It must survive high heat and pressure.

recall_q.en: Gasket used in modern engines?

explain_simple.en: Layers of thin steel sheet.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Signs of a blown head gasket: white smoke, coolant loss, oil mixed with water (milky oil), overheating, bubbles in radiator.

why.en: Gas and coolant leak between passages.

recall_q.en: Milky oil may show which failure?

explain_simple.en: Water in oil = head gasket problem.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Head bolts are tightened in a set order (from the centre outwards, spiral) and to a set torque with a torque wrench.

why.en: Uneven tightening warps the head and causes leaks.

recall_q.en: In what order are head bolts tightened?

recall_a.en: From centre outwards in a spiral, to specified torque.

explain_simple.en: Middle first, then outwards, evenly.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Crankcase is the lower part of the block that houses the crankshaft. The oil sump (oil pan) is bolted under it.

why.en: The sump stores engine oil.

recall_q.en: Part bolted under the crankcase to hold oil?

explain_simple.en: The oil tray at the bottom.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Core plugs (frost/welch plugs) close holes left in the block from casting. They can pop out if coolant freezes.

why.en: Holes are needed to remove casting sand.

recall_q.en: Purpose of core plugs?

recall_a.en: Seal casting holes (and give some frost protection).

explain_simple.en: Caps on the casting holes.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Combustion chamber shapes (SI): hemispherical, wedge, bath-tub, pent-roof. Hemispherical gives best breathing and less heat loss.

why.en: Shape decides flame travel and valve size.

recall_q.en: Combustion chamber with large valves and best breathing?

explain_simple.en: Dome-shaped chamber breathes best.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Cylinder wear is greatest at the top of the ring travel, just below the ridge, and gives a taper and ovality.

why.en: Heat, pressure and poor oil at the top cause most wear.

recall_q.en: Where is cylinder wear maximum?

recall_a.en: Top of ring travel (top of the bore).

explain_simple.en: The top of the bore wears most.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Reboring: worn cylinders are bored oversize and fitted with oversize pistons. Honing finishes the bore with a cross-hatch pattern.

why.en: Cross-hatch holds oil for the rings.

recall_q.en: Final finishing of a cylinder bore is done by?

explain_simple.en: Honing leaves fine scratches that hold oil.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Cylinder bore wear is measured with a cylinder bore gauge (dial bore gauge).

why.en: Shows taper and ovality.

recall_q.en: Instrument to measure cylinder wear?

explain_simple.en: A dial gauge that goes inside the cylinder.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

title.en: Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket

points.en: Block: cast iron or aluminium; monobloc for multi-cylinder.
Dry liner (no coolant contact, thin) vs wet liner (coolant contact, thick).
Head forms combustion chamber; gasket seals head to block.
MLS gasket; tighten head bolts centre-out with torque wrench.
Wear max at top of bore; rebore and hone.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: The piston moves up and down in the cylinder. It takes the gas force and passes it to the connecting rod.

why.en: It also seals the combustion chamber and carries heat away.

recall_q.en: Main job of a piston?

recall_a.en: Transmit gas force to the connecting rod.

explain_simple.en: The piston gets pushed and pushes the rod.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Piston parts: crown (head), ring grooves and lands, skirt, and gudgeon pin bosses.

why.en: Each part has its own job: crown takes heat, skirt guides, bosses hold the pin.

recall_q.en: The top surface of the piston is called?

explain_simple.en: Crown on top, skirt at the bottom.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Pistons are usually made of aluminium alloy (light, good heat conduction). Heavy diesel engines may use cast iron or steel crowns.

why.en: Light pistons reduce inertia forces at high speed.

recall_q.en: Most common piston material?

explain_simple.en: Pistons are mostly aluminium.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Aluminium pistons expand more than cast iron cylinders, so they need more clearance or special designs.

why.en: Too little clearance makes the hot piston seize.

recall_q.en: Why do aluminium pistons need special design?

recall_a.en: They expand more than the iron cylinder.

explain_simple.en: Hot aluminium grows a lot.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Split-skirt (slotted) piston: a slot in the skirt lets it expand without seizing.

why.en: The slot closes up as the piston heats.

recall_q.en: Purpose of the slot in a split-skirt piston?

explain_simple.en: A gap that closes when hot.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Cam-ground piston: oval when cold, becomes round when hot. The longer axis is at right angles to the gudgeon pin.

why.en: More metal near the pin bosses expands more.

recall_q.en: Shape of a cam-ground piston when cold?

explain_simple.en: Oval when cold, round when hot.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Other piston types: solid skirt, slipper (part skirt cut away), autothermic/invar-strut (steel struts control expansion), tapered.

why.en: All control expansion and reduce weight or noise.

recall_q.en: Piston with steel struts cast in to control expansion?

explain_simple.en: Steel strips stop the piston growing too much.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Piston is tapered: smaller at the crown than the skirt.

why.en: The crown is hottest and expands most.

recall_q.en: Is the crown or skirt of a piston larger when cold?

explain_simple.en: Hotter top is made smaller.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Piston slap: knocking noise when a worn or loose piston rocks and hits the cylinder wall, mostly when cold.

why.en: Too much clearance lets the piston tilt.

recall_q.en: Knock from excess piston clearance is called?

explain_simple.en: Loose piston hits the wall.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Gudgeon (wrist) pin connects the piston to the connecting rod small end.

why.en: It lets the rod swing while the piston moves straight.

recall_q.en: Pin joining piston and connecting rod?

explain_simple.en: The hinge pin of the piston.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Gudgeon pin types: fully floating (free in piston and rod, held by circlips), semi-floating (fixed in rod or piston), fixed.

why.en: Fully floating spreads wear evenly.

recall_q.en: What holds a fully floating gudgeon pin in place?

explain_simple.en: Free pin held by spring clips at the ends.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Gudgeon pins are made of case-hardened steel and are often hollow.

why.en: Hard surface for wear; hollow for less weight.

recall_q.en: Material of gudgeon pins?

explain_simple.en: Hard steel tube.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Gudgeon pin is offset slightly towards the thrust side to reduce piston slap.

why.en: The piston changes sides more gently at TDC.

recall_q.en: Why is the gudgeon pin offset?

explain_simple.en: Moving the pin a bit makes the piston quieter.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Piston rings seal the gap between piston and cylinder, control oil, and carry heat from piston to cylinder wall.

why.en: A piston cannot fit tightly enough on its own.

recall_q.en: Three functions of piston rings?

recall_a.en: Seal gas, control oil, transfer heat.

explain_simple.en: Rings seal, scrape oil and cool.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Two types of rings: compression rings (top) and oil control (scraper) rings (bottom).

why.en: Compression rings stop gas leaking down; oil rings stop oil going up.

recall_q.en: Which ring is at the bottom of the piston?

explain_simple.en: Compression rings on top, oil ring below.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Usual petrol engine: 2 compression rings + 1 oil ring. Diesel engines may have 3–4 compression rings.

why.en: Diesels have higher pressures to seal.

recall_q.en: Typical ring set of a car petrol engine?

explain_simple.en: Two for gas, one for oil.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Oil rings are slotted or have an expander so scraped oil drains back through holes in the piston.

why.en: This stops oil reaching the combustion chamber.

recall_q.en: How does scraped oil return from an oil ring?

recall_a.en: Through slots in the ring and holes in the piston groove.

explain_simple.en: Oil slips back through little holes.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Piston rings are made of fine-grained alloy cast iron; the top ring is often chrome plated.

why.en: Cast iron is springy enough and wears well; chrome resists wear.

recall_q.en: Usual material of piston rings?

recall_a.en: Alloy cast iron (top ring chrome plated).

explain_simple.en: Cast iron rings, chrome on top.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Ring end gap allows for expansion. Ring gaps are staggered around the piston (not in line).

why.en: In-line gaps would let gas blow straight past.

recall_q.en: Why are ring gaps staggered?

explain_simple.en: Spread the gaps so gas cannot slip through.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Worn rings cause blow-by, low compression, high oil consumption and blue exhaust smoke.

why.en: Oil gets past into the chamber and burns.

recall_q.en: Blue exhaust smoke often means?

explain_simple.en: Blue smoke = oil burning.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Compression test with a compression gauge checks ring and valve sealing. A wet test (adding oil) separates ring problems from valve problems.

why.en: Oil seals rings briefly; if compression rises, rings are worn.

recall_q.en: In a wet compression test, compression rises. What is worn?

explain_simple.en: Oil helps worn rings, not bad valves.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: The connecting rod joins the piston to the crankshaft and turns up-down motion into rotation.

why.en: It works with the crank like a pedal and leg.

recall_q.en: What converts reciprocating motion to rotary motion?

explain_simple.en: Rod + crank turn up-down into round.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Connecting rod parts: small end (gudgeon pin end, with bronze bush), shank (I-section), big end (split, with shell bearings, cap and bolts).

why.en: The big end is split so it can fit around the crankpin.

recall_q.en: Which end of the connecting rod is split?

explain_simple.en: Small end at the piston, big split end at the crank.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Connecting rods are made of drop-forged medium carbon or alloy steel; racing engines use aluminium or titanium.

why.en: They need high strength with low weight.

recall_q.en: How are connecting rods usually made?

explain_simple.en: Hammer-forged strong steel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Connecting rod shank has an I-section.

why.en: It gives maximum stiffness against buckling for least weight.

recall_q.en: Cross-section of a connecting rod shank?

explain_simple.en: I-shape is strong and light.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Small end usually has a phosphor bronze bush. Big end uses split shell (thin-wall) bearings.

why.en: The small end only rocks; the big end rotates fully.

recall_q.en: Bearing at the small end of a connecting rod?

explain_simple.en: Bush at small end, shells at big end.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Some connecting rods have an oil hole (squirt hole) that sprays oil onto the cylinder wall or under the piston.

why.en: Extra cooling and lubrication.

recall_q.en: Purpose of the squirt hole in a connecting rod?

recall_a.en: Spray oil onto cylinder wall or piston.

explain_simple.en: A small jet of oil for the cylinder.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Crankshaft turns the reciprocating motion of pistons into rotation and carries the flywheel.

why.en: It is the engine's output shaft.

recall_q.en: Output shaft of an engine?

explain_simple.en: The main spinning shaft.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Crankshaft parts: main journals, crankpins, webs (cheeks), counterweights, oil holes, front end (timing gear, pulley) and rear flange (flywheel).

why.en: Main journals sit in main bearings; crankpins hold big ends.

recall_q.en: Part of the crankshaft where the big end fits?

explain_simple.en: Main journals on the centre line; crankpins offset.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Counterweights on the crank webs balance the rotating weight of crankpins and connecting rods.

why.en: This reduces vibration and bearing load.

recall_q.en: Why are counterweights used on a crankshaft?

recall_a.en: To balance the crankshaft and reduce vibration.

explain_simple.en: Weights opposite the crankpins balance it.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Crankshafts are made of drop-forged steel (carbon or alloy) or SG cast iron. Journals are hardened.

why.en: They face bending and twisting loads.

recall_q.en: Two crankshaft materials?

recall_a.en: Forged steel and SG (nodular) cast iron.

explain_simple.en: Forged steel or tough cast iron.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Crankshaft shapes depend on cylinders: single-throw (1 cylinder), 180° two-throw, four-cylinder flat (throws at 180°), six-cylinder (throws at 120°).

why.en: Throw angle spreads power strokes evenly: 720°/number of cylinders.

recall_q.en: Crank throw spacing for a four-stroke six-cylinder engine?

explain_simple.en: 720° ÷ cylinders = firing interval.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Number of main bearings: a four-cylinder crankshaft usually has 3 or 5 main bearings.

why.en: More mains give a stiffer crank.

recall_q.en: Common number of main bearings in a four-cylinder engine?

explain_simple.en: More bearings, less bending.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Crankshaft end float is controlled by thrust washers or a flanged main bearing.

why.en: Clutch pressure pushes the crank lengthways.

recall_q.en: What controls crankshaft end play?

explain_simple.en: Washers stop the crank sliding back and forth.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Vibration damper (harmonic balancer) on the front of the crankshaft reduces torsional vibration.

why.en: Long crankshafts twist and untwist with each power stroke.

recall_q.en: What reduces torsional vibration of the crankshaft?

explain_simple.en: A rubber-mounted ring stops the crank twisting back and forth.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

title.en: Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft

points.en: Piston: aluminium; split-skirt, cam-ground, invar-strut types.
Rings: 2 compression + 1 oil; staggered gaps; cast iron.
Gudgeon pin: fully floating with circlips; offset reduces slap.
Con rod: I-section, forged steel; small end bush, big end shells.
Crankshaft: journals, crankpins, counterweights; damper at front.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Valves open and close the inlet and exhaust ports at the right time.

why.en: They let fresh charge in and burnt gas out.

recall_q.en: Job of engine valves?

recall_a.en: Control flow of charge in and exhaust out.

explain_simple.en: Doors for gas.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Types of valves: poppet (mushroom) valve, sleeve valve, rotary valve, reed valve. Poppet valves are used in almost all four-stroke engines.

why.en: Poppet valves seal well and are simple.

recall_q.en: Most common type of engine valve?

explain_simple.en: A mushroom-shaped valve.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Poppet valve parts: head, face (usually 45°, sometimes 30°), margin, stem, and grooves for the collets (keepers).

why.en: The angled face seals against the seat.

recall_q.en: Usual valve face angle?

explain_simple.en: The valve's sloping face presses on the seat.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Inlet valve head is larger than exhaust valve head.

why.en: Incoming charge has low pressure and needs a big opening; exhaust leaves under pressure.

recall_q.en: Which valve is bigger: inlet or exhaust?

explain_simple.en: Bigger door for air coming in.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Exhaust valve runs much hotter (up to about 700–800°C) than the inlet valve.

why.en: Hot gases flow over it; the inlet is cooled by fresh charge.

recall_q.en: Which valve runs hotter?

explain_simple.en: Exhaust valve faces hot gas.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Sodium-cooled valve: hollow exhaust valve stem partly filled with sodium. The sodium melts and carries heat from head to stem.

why.en: Liquid sodium splashes up and down, moving heat to the cooler stem and guide.

recall_q.en: Why is sodium filled in some exhaust valves?

recall_a.en: To carry heat away from the valve head (cooling).

explain_simple.en: Melted sodium moves heat away.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Sodium melts at about 98°C, so it is liquid when the engine runs.

why.en: Liquid sodium carries heat well.

recall_q.en: Melting point of sodium used in valves?

explain_simple.en: Sodium is liquid in a running engine.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Valve materials: inlet — chromium or nickel-chromium steel. Exhaust — silchrome or austenitic steel; faces often coated with stellite.

why.en: Exhaust valves need heat and corrosion resistance.

recall_q.en: Hard alloy coated on exhaust valve faces?

explain_simple.en: Exhaust valves get a heat-proof face.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Valve seat inserts of hard alloy are fitted in aluminium heads.

why.en: Aluminium is too soft to act as a seat.

recall_q.en: Why are valve seat inserts used in aluminium heads?

recall_a.en: Aluminium is soft; inserts give a hard wearing seat.

explain_simple.en: A hard ring for the valve to sit on.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Valve guide holds the valve stem in line and carries heat from the stem.

why.en: It keeps the valve centred on its seat.

recall_q.en: What keeps the valve stem aligned?

explain_simple.en: A tube the valve slides in.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Valve stem seals stop oil leaking down the guide into the cylinder.

why.en: Worn seals cause blue smoke on start-up.

recall_q.en: Part that stops oil going down the valve guide?

explain_simple.en: A rubber seal on the valve stem.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Valve spring closes the valve and keeps it on the seat. It is held by a spring retainer and split collets (cotters).

why.en: The cam only opens the valve; the spring closes it.

recall_q.en: What closes the valve?

explain_simple.en: The cam opens, the spring shuts.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Valve float: at very high speed, the valve does not follow the cam and stays partly open.

why.en: The spring cannot close it fast enough.

recall_q.en: Valve not following the cam at high rpm is called?

explain_simple.en: Valve bounces and stays open too long.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Valve rotators turn the valve a little on each opening.

why.en: This spreads wear and stops carbon build-up on the seat.

recall_q.en: Why are valve rotators used?

recall_a.en: Even wear and to prevent carbon deposits on seat.

explain_simple.en: Turning the valve keeps its seat clean.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Valve clearance (tappet clearance) is a small gap in the valve train when the valve is closed.

why.en: It allows for heat expansion so the valve closes fully when hot.

recall_q.en: Why is tappet clearance provided?

recall_a.en: To allow for expansion so valves close fully.

explain_simple.en: A small gap for growth when hot.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Exhaust valve clearance is usually more than inlet valve clearance.

why.en: The exhaust valve gets hotter and expands more.

recall_q.en: Which valve has more tappet clearance?

explain_simple.en: Hotter valve gets a bigger gap.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Too little clearance: valve stays open, burns, and compression is lost. Too much clearance: noisy tapping and less valve lift.

why.en: Clearance changes valve timing.

recall_q.en: Effect of too little tappet clearance?

recall_a.en: Valve does not close fully → burnt valve, low compression.

explain_simple.en: Too tight burns valves; too loose taps loudly.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Hydraulic tappets (lifters) use oil pressure to keep zero clearance automatically.

why.en: No adjustment needed and quiet running.

recall_q.en: Advantage of hydraulic tappets?

recall_a.en: Zero clearance automatically, quiet, no adjustment.

explain_simple.en: Oil-filled lifters adjust themselves.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Valve arrangements: L-head (side valve), I-head (overhead valve), F-head (one over, one side), T-head (inlet and exhaust on opposite sides).

why.en: Older names still asked in exams.

recall_q.en: Engine with both valves in the cylinder head is called?

explain_simple.en: Valve layout is named by letter shapes.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Side camshaft (OHV push-rod) mechanism: camshaft in the block → tappet (follower) → push rod → rocker arm → valve.

why.en: The push rod carries motion up to the head.

recall_q.en: Order of parts in a push-rod valve mechanism?

recall_a.en: Cam → tappet → push rod → rocker arm → valve.

explain_simple.en: Cam pushes tappet, push rod, rocker, valve.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Overhead camshaft (OHC): the camshaft is in the cylinder head and works the valves directly or through rockers/followers.

why.en: Fewer moving parts allows higher engine speeds.

recall_q.en: Advantage of OHC over push-rod design?

recall_a.en: Fewer parts, less inertia, higher rpm.

explain_simple.en: Cam on top = fewer parts, faster engine.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: SOHC: single overhead camshaft. DOHC: two overhead camshafts, one for inlet and one for exhaust valves.

why.en: DOHC allows 4 valves per cylinder and better breathing.

recall_q.en: In DOHC, how many camshafts per cylinder bank?

explain_simple.en: Double OHC: one cam for inlet, one for exhaust.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Multi-valve engines (3, 4 or 5 valves per cylinder) breathe better and allow a central spark plug.

why.en: More, smaller valves give more flow area.

recall_q.en: Why use four valves per cylinder?

recall_a.en: Better breathing, more power, central plug.

explain_simple.en: More doors, more air.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Camshaft opens the valves at the right time. It has one cam (lobe) for each valve and runs at half crankshaft speed in four-stroke engines.

why.en: Each valve opens once per two crank turns.

recall_q.en: Camshaft speed compared to crankshaft?

explain_simple.en: Cam turns once for every two crank turns.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Cam terms: base circle, nose (tip), flank, lift, ramp.

why.en: The nose gives maximum valve opening.

recall_q.en: Highest point of a cam is called?

explain_simple.en: The nose pushes the valve fully open.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Camshafts may also drive the distributor, oil pump and mechanical fuel pump (via an eccentric).

why.en: Older engines used one shaft for many drives.

recall_q.en: What on the camshaft drives a mechanical fuel pump?

explain_simple.en: An off-centre lobe works the fuel pump.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Camshaft drives: gear drive, chain drive (timing chain with tensioner), belt drive (toothed timing belt).

why.en: They keep cam and crank in exact time.

recall_q.en: Three types of camshaft drives?

explain_simple.en: Gears, chain or belt connect crank to cam.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Timing belts are quiet and light but must be replaced at set intervals. Chains last longer but are noisier.

why.en: A broken belt can let pistons hit valves (interference engine).

recall_q.en: Disadvantage of a timing belt?

recall_a.en: Needs periodic replacement; failure can damage valves.

explain_simple.en: Belt is quiet but must be changed on time.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Timing marks on crank and cam sprockets must line up when fitting the chain or belt.

why.en: Wrong timing gives poor running or engine damage.

recall_q.en: What must be lined up when fitting a timing belt?

recall_a.en: Timing marks on crank and cam sprockets.

explain_simple.en: Match the marks before fitting.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Camshafts are made of cast iron (chilled or hardenable) or forged steel; cam lobes are hardened.

why.en: Lobes face heavy sliding wear.

recall_q.en: Material of camshafts?

recall_a.en: Chilled cast iron or forged steel (hardened lobes).

explain_simple.en: Hard-faced iron or steel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Cam followers: flat (mushroom), roller, knife-edge, spherical. Roller followers reduce friction.

why.en: Rolling contact wears less than sliding.

recall_q.en: Which follower has least friction?

explain_simple.en: A small wheel riding on the cam.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Valve grinding (lapping) with grinding paste makes the valve face and seat seal perfectly.

why.en: Removes small pits and makes a gas-tight ring of contact.

recall_q.en: Process of making valve and seat seal with paste?

explain_simple.en: Rub valve and seat together with paste.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Poppet valves, 45° face; inlet bigger, exhaust hotter.
Sodium-cooled exhaust valves; stellite faces; seat inserts.
Tappet clearance: exhaust > inlet; hydraulic lifters = zero.
Push rod: cam → tappet → push rod → rocker → valve. OHC/DOHC.
Cam drive: gear, chain, belt; cam at half crank speed.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Petrol fuel feed, filters and air cleaners; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Petrol fuel system parts: tank, fuel lines, filter, fuel pump, carburettor or injectors.

why.en: Fuel must reach the engine clean and at the right pressure.

recall_q.en: Name the parts of a petrol fuel system.

explain_simple.en: Tank → pump → filter → engine.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Petrol fuel feed, filters and air cleaners; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Fuel feed systems: gravity feed, pressure feed, vacuum feed, pump feed (mechanical or electrical).

why.en: Small vehicles can use gravity; cars need a pump.

recall_q.en: Simplest fuel feed system used in motorcycles?

explain_simple.en: Tank above the engine, fuel just flows down.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Petrol fuel feed, filters and air cleaners; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: AC mechanical fuel pump: a diaphragm pump worked by a rocker arm from an eccentric on the camshaft.

why.en: Engine rotation pumps the fuel.

recall_q.en: What operates the AC mechanical fuel pump?

recall_a.en: Eccentric on the camshaft (via rocker arm).

explain_simple.en: Camshaft moves a lever that flexes a diaphragm.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Petrol fuel feed, filters and air cleaners; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: AC pump parts: diaphragm, rocker arm, return spring, inlet and outlet valves, filter screen, priming lever.

why.en: The diaphragm sucks and pushes fuel through one-way valves.

recall_q.en: Main moving part that pumps fuel in an AC pump?

explain_simple.en: A flexible sheet sucks and pushes petrol.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Petrol fuel feed, filters and air cleaners; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: In the AC pump, the spring pushes fuel out. When the float bowl is full, the diaphragm stays down and the pump idles.

why.en: Delivery pressure is set by the spring, not the cam.

recall_q.en: What decides the delivery pressure of an AC pump?

explain_simple.en: The spring pushes the fuel, so pressure stays safe.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Petrol fuel feed, filters and air cleaners; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: SU electrical fuel pump: a solenoid pulls a diaphragm; contact points switch it off and on.

why.en: Works as soon as the ignition is on, even before cranking.

recall_q.en: What moves the diaphragm in an SU electric pump?

explain_simple.en: Electric magnet flexes the diaphragm.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Petrol fuel feed, filters and air cleaners; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Electric pumps can be fitted near the tank, away from engine heat.

why.en: This reduces vapour lock.

recall_q.en: Advantage of an electric fuel pump?

recall_a.en: Fitted away from heat; fuel at once on switch-on; less vapour lock.

explain_simple.en: Cool location, instant fuel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Petrol fuel feed, filters and air cleaners; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Modern fuel-injected cars use an electric in-tank (submerged) roller-cell or turbine pump.

why.en: Fuel cools the pump and prevents vapour.

recall_q.en: Where is the fuel pump fitted in modern MPFI cars?
