explain_simple.en: Pump sits in the tank.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Petrol fuel feed, filters and air cleaners; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Vapour lock: petrol boils in hot fuel lines and vapour blocks fuel flow.

why.en: Pumps cannot push vapour well.

recall_q.en: Fuel line blocked by petrol vapour is called?

explain_simple.en: Bubbles block the fuel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Petrol fuel feed, filters and air cleaners; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Petrol filters remove dirt and water. Types: in-line paper filter, sediment bowl, gauze strainer in tank and pump.

why.en: Dirt blocks carburettor jets and injectors.

recall_q.en: Why are fuel filters used?

recall_a.en: To remove dirt and water from fuel.

explain_simple.en: Clean fuel, clear jets.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Petrol fuel feed, filters and air cleaners; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Air cleaner removes dust from air entering the engine. It also silences intake noise and acts as a flame arrester.

why.en: Dust wears cylinders and rings fast.

recall_q.en: Give two functions of an air cleaner.

recall_a.en: Filter dust, reduce intake noise (and arrest backfire flame).

explain_simple.en: Cleans air and quiets the intake.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Petrol fuel feed, filters and air cleaners; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Air cleaner types: dry (paper element), wet (oil-wetted mesh), oil bath. Paper dry type is most common in cars.

why.en: Paper elements are efficient and cheap to replace.

recall_q.en: Air cleaner where air passes over oil in a bowl?

explain_simple.en: Paper, oily mesh, or oil bath.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Petrol fuel feed, filters and air cleaners; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Centrifugal (cyclone) pre-cleaners are used on trucks and tractors in dusty conditions.

why.en: They spin out heavy dust before the main filter.

recall_q.en: Pre-cleaner used in dusty conditions?

explain_simple.en: Spins dust out first.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Petrol fuel feed, filters and air cleaners; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A choked air filter makes the mixture rich, raises fuel consumption and causes black smoke.

why.en: Less air for the same fuel.

recall_q.en: Effect of a choked air filter?

recall_a.en: Rich mixture, high fuel consumption, black smoke.

explain_simple.en: Dirty filter = less air = rich mixture.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Petrol fuel feed, filters and air cleaners; standard diploma textbook

title.en: Petrol fuel feed, filters and air cleaners

points.en: Gravity, vacuum, pump feed systems.
AC pump: mechanical, diaphragm, camshaft eccentric.
SU pump: electric solenoid; in-tank pumps in MPFI.
Vapour lock = petrol boiling in lines.
Air cleaners: paper, oil-wetted, oil bath.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A carburettor mixes petrol with air in the correct ratio and supplies it to the engine as a fine spray.

why.en: Petrol must be vapour mixed with air to burn well.

recall_q.en: Function of a carburettor?

recall_a.en: Mix air and petrol in correct proportion.

explain_simple.en: It makes the air–petrol mix.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Carburettor works on the venturi (Bernoulli) principle: air speeds up in the narrow venturi, pressure drops, and petrol is sucked from the jet.

why.en: Fast air = low pressure.

recall_q.en: Principle of the carburettor?

explain_simple.en: Fast air pulls petrol out.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Simple carburettor parts: float chamber with float and needle valve, main jet, discharge nozzle, venturi, throttle valve, choke valve.

why.en: Each part controls fuel level, flow or air.

recall_q.en: Part that keeps a constant fuel level in a carburettor?

explain_simple.en: The float shuts fuel when the bowl is full.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Throttle valve (butterfly) controls the amount of mixture entering the engine and so controls speed and power.

why.en: It is linked to the accelerator pedal.

recall_q.en: Which valve is connected to the accelerator pedal?

explain_simple.en: Pedal opens the throttle.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: The fuel nozzle tip is slightly above the fuel level in the float chamber.

why.en: Prevents fuel dripping out when the engine is stopped.

recall_q.en: Why is the nozzle tip above the float chamber level?

recall_a.en: To stop fuel overflowing when the engine is off.

explain_simple.en: Keeps petrol from dripping out.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A simple carburettor gives a richer mixture as speed rises.

why.en: Fuel flow increases faster than air flow through the venturi.

recall_q.en: What happens to mixture in a simple carburettor at high speed?

explain_simple.en: Simple carb goes rich when fast.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Compensation devices keep mixture correct at all speeds: air bleed jet, compensating jet, emulsion tube, auxiliary air valve, back suction control.

why.en: They correct the richening at high speed.

recall_q.en: Name one compensating device in a carburettor.

recall_a.en: Air bleed jet (or compensating jet, emulsion tube).

explain_simple.en: Extra air or fuel paths keep the mix right.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Chemically correct air-fuel ratio: about 15:1. Rich mixture: less air (e.g. 12:1). Lean (weak) mixture: more air (e.g. 17:1).

why.en: Engine needs different ratios for different conditions.

recall_q.en: Is 12:1 a rich or lean mixture?

explain_simple.en: Less air = rich. More air = lean.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Mixture requirements: cold starting very rich (up to 5:1 or 9:1), idling rich (about 12:1), cruising lean (about 16–17:1), full power/acceleration rich (about 12–13:1).

why.en: Each condition needs different fuel.

recall_q.en: Which condition needs the leanest mixture?

explain_simple.en: Cruise lean, start and power rich.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Best economy mixture is slightly lean (about 16:1). Best power mixture is slightly rich (about 12.5:1).

why.en: Extra fuel ensures all oxygen is used for power.

recall_q.en: Is best power mixture rich or lean?

explain_simple.en: Rich for power, lean for economy.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Modern carburettor circuits: float system, starting (choke) system, idle and slow-speed system, main metering (high speed) system, acceleration pump system, power (economiser) system.

why.en: Each circuit handles a driving condition.

recall_q.en: Name the circuits of a modern carburettor.

recall_a.en: Float, choke, idle, main metering, accelerating pump, power.

explain_simple.en: Six circuits for six jobs.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Idle and slow-speed system supplies fuel through an idle port below the closed throttle, where vacuum is high.

why.en: At idle, venturi air is too slow to lift fuel from the main jet.

recall_q.en: Where does fuel come from at idle?

recall_a.en: Idle port below the throttle valve.

explain_simple.en: A small hole under the throttle feeds idle fuel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Idle mixture screw adjusts idle mixture; idle speed (throttle stop) screw adjusts idle rpm.

why.en: Both are set during tuning.

recall_q.en: Which screw adjusts idle rpm?

explain_simple.en: One screw for mixture, one for speed.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Transfer (progression) ports just above the closed throttle feed extra fuel as the throttle starts to open.

why.en: Prevents a flat spot between idle and main circuits.

recall_q.en: Purpose of transfer ports?

recall_a.en: Smooth change from idle to main circuit.

explain_simple.en: Fill the gap as the throttle starts opening.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Main metering (high speed) system supplies fuel through the main jet and nozzle at cruising and higher speeds.

why.en: Venturi vacuum is strong enough at these speeds.

recall_q.en: Which circuit supplies fuel at cruising speed?

explain_simple.en: Main jet works at normal speeds.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Acceleration pump squirts extra fuel when the throttle is opened suddenly.

why.en: Air speeds up faster than fuel; without it the engine hesitates (flat spot).

recall_q.en: Why is an accelerator pump needed?

recall_a.en: Prevent hesitation (lean mixture) on sudden throttle opening.

explain_simple.en: An extra squirt when you press quickly.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Power (economiser) system gives extra fuel at full throttle, opened by low vacuum or a mechanical link.

why.en: Full load needs a richer mixture.

recall_q.en: Circuit that enriches mixture at full throttle?

explain_simple.en: More fuel at full power.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Choke valve is a butterfly above the venturi. Closing it gives a very rich mixture for cold starting.

why.en: Cold petrol does not vaporise well, so more is needed.

recall_q.en: Which valve gives a rich mixture for cold starting?

explain_simple.en: Choke cuts air for a cold start.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Automatic choke uses a bimetallic spring heated by the engine to open the choke as the engine warms.

why.en: Driver does not need to remember to push it in.

recall_q.en: What operates an automatic choke?

explain_simple.en: A heat-sensitive spring opens it by itself.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Constant vacuum (CV) carburettor: venturi size changes with a piston/slide lifted by vacuum (SU, Stromberg).

why.en: Air speed stays nearly constant, giving good mixture at all loads.

recall_q.en: Name a constant vacuum (variable venturi) carburettor.

explain_simple.en: The venturi grows as needed.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Fixed venturi (constant choke) carburettors: Solex, Zenith, Carter. Variable venturi (constant vacuum): SU, Stromberg.

why.en: PSC asks to classify named carburettors.

recall_q.en: Is Solex a fixed or variable venturi carburettor?

explain_simple.en: Solex/Zenith fixed; SU variable.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Down-draught, up-draught and side-draught carburettors are named by air flow direction. Down-draught is common in cars.

why.en: Gravity helps the mixture flow down.

recall_q.en: Most common carburettor type in cars (by air direction)?

explain_simple.en: Air flows downward into the engine.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Multi-barrel carburettors have two or four throats; the secondary barrels open only at high load.

why.en: Small primary for economy, big secondary for power.

recall_q.en: When does the secondary barrel open?

explain_simple.en: Extra barrels open for more power.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Carburettor faults: flooding (stuck needle valve), lean mixture (blocked jet), rich mixture (choke stuck, high float level), icing.

why.en: Each shows typical symptoms.

recall_q.en: Common cause of carburettor flooding?

recall_a.en: Needle valve stuck open / float punctured.

explain_simple.en: Fuel keeps coming in and overflows.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Carburettor icing: fuel evaporation cools the venturi so much that moisture freezes on it.

why.en: Evaporation takes heat.

recall_q.en: Ice forming in a carburettor venturi is called?

explain_simple.en: Evaporating petrol makes it freezing cold.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Carburettor = venturi principle; float + needle valve keeps level.
Simple carb goes rich at speed → compensation (air bleed).
Start very rich, idle rich, cruise lean, power rich.
Circuits: float, choke, idle, main, accelerator pump, power.
Fixed venturi: Solex, Zenith. Variable: SU, Stromberg.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Inlet (intake) manifold carries air or air–fuel mixture from the carburettor or throttle body to each cylinder.

why.en: Each cylinder must get an equal share.

recall_q.en: What does the inlet manifold do?

explain_simple.en: Pipes that share air to all cylinders.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Inlet manifolds are made of cast aluminium or plastic (nylon composite) in modern engines.

why.en: Light and smooth inside.

recall_q.en: Material of modern inlet manifolds?

explain_simple.en: Light aluminium or plastic.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Hot spot: part of the inlet manifold heated by exhaust or coolant to help petrol vaporise in carburettor engines.

why.en: Liquid petrol drops would cause uneven mixture.

recall_q.en: Purpose of a hot spot in the inlet manifold?

explain_simple.en: Warm spot turns petrol drops to vapour.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Inlet manifold types: single plane, dual plane, log type, individual runners (tuned).

why.en: Shape affects flow, distribution and torque curve.

recall_q.en: Name one type of inlet manifold.

recall_a.en: Single plane, dual plane, log, tuned runners.

explain_simple.en: Different pipe layouts.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Long intake runners give better low-speed torque; short runners give better high-speed power.

why.en: Pressure waves in the runner help filling at certain speeds.

recall_q.en: Which runner length favours low-speed torque?

explain_simple.en: Long pipe for pulling power, short pipe for speed.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Variable intake system (VIS) switches between long and short runners with valves controlled by the ECU.

why.en: Gets good torque at low rpm and power at high rpm.

recall_q.en: Purpose of a variable intake system?

recall_a.en: Change runner length for good torque and power at all speeds.

explain_simple.en: Long pipe at low speed, short at high speed.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: VVT (variable valve timing) changes when the valves open and close depending on engine speed and load.

why.en: Fixed timing is a compromise; VVT gives power, economy and low emissions together.

recall_q.en: What does VVT change?

explain_simple.en: Valves open earlier or later as needed.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: VVT is usually done by a cam phaser on the camshaft sprocket, moved by oil pressure controlled by an ECU solenoid.

why.en: Turning the cam relative to its sprocket shifts timing.

recall_q.en: Device that rotates the camshaft relative to its sprocket?

explain_simple.en: Oil pressure twists the camshaft a little.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: CVVT (continuously variable valve timing) can set any timing within its range, not just two fixed positions.

why.en: Smooth, exact control at every speed.

recall_q.en: Difference between VVT (two-step) and CVVT?

recall_a.en: CVVT adjusts timing continuously, not in steps.

explain_simple.en: CVVT changes timing smoothly all the time.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Brand names: Honda VTEC (also changes lift), Toyota VVT-i, Hyundai CVVT, Maruti VVT.

why.en: VTEC switches cam profiles; VVT-i shifts timing.

recall_q.en: Honda's variable valve system is called?

explain_simple.en: VTEC changes both timing and lift.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Benefits of VVT: more torque at low rpm, more power at high rpm, better fuel economy, smoother idle, lower emissions (internal EGR).

why.en: Overlap can be changed to suit conditions.

recall_q.en: Give two benefits of VVT.

recall_a.en: More power and torque, better economy, lower emissions.

explain_simple.en: Better everything by smart valve timing.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Exhaust manifold collects burnt gases from all cylinders and sends them to the exhaust pipe.

why.en: It must handle very hot gases.

recall_q.en: Function of the exhaust manifold?

explain_simple.en: Pipes that gather smoke from all cylinders.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Exhaust manifolds are made of cast iron or stainless steel tubes (headers).

why.en: They must resist high heat and corrosion.

recall_q.en: Material of exhaust manifolds?

explain_simple.en: Heat-proof metal.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Tuned exhaust headers (e.g. 4-into-1, 4-2-1) use pressure waves to help pull exhaust out (scavenging).

why.en: Less back pressure means more power.

recall_q.en: Why are tuned headers used?

recall_a.en: Better scavenging, less back pressure, more power.

explain_simple.en: Pipe shapes help suck out exhaust.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Exhaust system parts: exhaust manifold, front pipe, catalytic converter, resonator, muffler (silencer), tail pipe.

why.en: Gas is cleaned, then quietened, then released.

recall_q.en: Order of main parts in an exhaust system?

recall_a.en: Manifold → catalytic converter → muffler → tail pipe.

explain_simple.en: Collect, clean, quieten, release.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Catalytic converter changes harmful gases (CO, HC, NOx) into less harmful CO₂, H₂O and N₂ using catalysts.

why.en: Catalysts speed up reactions without being used up.

recall_q.en: Harmful gases treated by a three-way catalytic converter?

explain_simple.en: Turns poison gases into safer ones.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Catalysts used: platinum and palladium (oxidise CO and HC), rhodium (reduces NOx). Coated on a ceramic honeycomb.

why.en: Honeycomb gives a huge surface area.

recall_q.en: Which catalyst reduces NOx?

explain_simple.en: Platinum/palladium for CO and HC; rhodium for NOx.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Two-way converter: oxidises CO and HC only. Three-way converter: also reduces NOx, needs mixture near 14.7:1 (controlled by lambda sensor).

why.en: NOx reduction needs little oxygen; CO/HC oxidation needs some.

recall_q.en: Three-way converter needs mixture close to what ratio?

explain_simple.en: Exactly correct mixture for all three.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Catalytic converter works only when hot (light-off temperature about 250–300°C).

why.en: Catalysts are not active when cold, so cold-start emissions are high.

recall_q.en: Does a catalytic converter work when cold?

explain_simple.en: It must warm up first.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Leaded petrol destroys catalytic converters (lead poisoning of the catalyst).

why.en: Lead coats the catalyst surface.

recall_q.en: Which fuel damages catalytic converters?

explain_simple.en: Lead kills the catalyst.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Diesel engines use a diesel oxidation catalyst (DOC), diesel particulate filter (DPF) and SCR with urea (AdBlue) for NOx.

why.en: Diesel exhaust has lots of oxygen, so three-way converters do not work.

recall_q.en: What fluid is used in SCR systems?

explain_simple.en: Urea spray cleans diesel NOx.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Muffler (silencer) reduces exhaust noise.

why.en: Exhaust leaves in loud pressure pulses.

recall_q.en: Function of a muffler?

explain_simple.en: It makes the exhaust quiet.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Muffler types: baffle type, wave cancellation (Helmholtz/resonator), absorption (straight-through with glass wool), combined.

why.en: Each reduces noise differently.

recall_q.en: Muffler that uses sound-absorbing material around a perforated tube?

explain_simple.en: Baffles, wave cancelling, or soaking up sound.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Wave cancellation muffler splits gas into two paths of different lengths so sound waves meet out of phase and cancel.

why.en: Opposite waves cancel each other.

recall_q.en: How does a wave-cancellation muffler work?

recall_a.en: Sound waves meet out of phase and cancel.

explain_simple.en: Two waves meet and silence each other.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Back pressure: resistance to exhaust flow. Too much back pressure reduces power and raises fuel consumption.

why.en: The engine must push harder to empty the cylinder.

recall_q.en: Effect of high exhaust back pressure?

explain_simple.en: Blocked exhaust chokes the engine.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Removing or modifying silencers is an offence. Noise limits are set under the Central Motor Vehicles Rules.

why.en: Excess noise is pollution; MVD checks during inspection.

recall_q.en: Is removing a vehicle silencer allowed?

recall_a.en: No — it is an offence (noise limits under CMVR).

explain_simple.en: Loud modified silencers are illegal.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

title.en: Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler

points.en: Inlet manifold: aluminium/plastic; hot spot for vaporising.
Variable intake: long runners low rpm, short high rpm.
VVT/CVVT: cam phaser shifts timing; VTEC changes lift too.
Cat converter: Pt, Pd (CO, HC), Rh (NOx); light-off ~250°C.
Muffler: baffle, wave cancellation, absorption.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Diesel fuel system order: tank → feed (lift) pump → primary filter → secondary filter → injection pump → high-pressure pipes → injectors. Leak-off returns to tank.

why.en: Fuel must be very clean and at very high pressure.

recall_q.en: Order of parts in a diesel fuel system?

recall_a.en: Tank, feed pump, filters, injection pump, injectors.

explain_simple.en: Tank → lift pump → filter → injection pump → injector.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Fuel feed (lift / transfer) pump sends fuel from the tank to the injection pump at low pressure (about 1–2 bar).

why.en: The injection pump needs a steady, bubble-free supply.

recall_q.en: Job of the fuel feed pump?

recall_a.en: Supply fuel from tank to injection pump at low pressure.

explain_simple.en: It lifts diesel to the main pump.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Hand priming pump on the feed pump is used to fill the system and bleed out air after filter change.

why.en: Air in diesel lines stops the engine.

recall_q.en: Why is a hand primer used?

recall_a.en: To fill the fuel system and bleed air.

explain_simple.en: Pump by hand to push air out.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Air lock in diesel lines prevents injection; the system is bled at filter and pump bleed screws.

why.en: Air compresses, so pressure cannot build.

recall_q.en: What must be done after running out of diesel?

recall_a.en: Bleed the fuel system to remove air.

explain_simple.en: Push out the air bubbles.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Diesel filters: primary (coarse, often with water separator) and secondary (fine, paper element).

why.en: Injection parts have very fine clearances; dirt and water ruin them.

recall_q.en: Why do diesel systems need fine filters?

recall_a.en: Injection pump and injectors have very fine clearances.

explain_simple.en: Tiny parts need very clean fuel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Water separator (sedimenter) collects water at the bottom of the filter bowl; it must be drained regularly.

why.en: Water corrodes pump and injector parts.

recall_q.en: Purpose of a water separator in diesel filter?

explain_simple.en: Catches water before it reaches the pump.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Fuel injection pump (FIP) supplies exact, metered fuel at very high pressure to each injector at the right time.

why.en: Diesel must be sprayed finely into very hot compressed air.

recall_q.en: Job of the fuel injection pump?

recall_a.en: Meter and pressurise fuel, deliver at right time.

explain_simple.en: The heart of the diesel system.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Types of injection pumps: in-line (jerk) pump with one element per cylinder, distributor (rotary) pump with one element for all cylinders, unit injector, and common rail.

why.en: Different engine sizes and eras use different types.

recall_q.en: Pump with one element per cylinder in a row?

explain_simple.en: In-line = one plunger per cylinder.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: In-line (Bosch) pump: each element has a plunger with a helix; rotating the plunger with a control rack changes fuel quantity.

why.en: The helix uncovers the spill port earlier or later.

recall_q.en: In an in-line pump, what changes fuel quantity?

recall_a.en: Rotating the plunger (helix) via control rack.

explain_simple.en: Turn the plunger to change fuel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Delivery valve in each pump element stops back-flow and gives sharp end of injection (prevents dribbling).

why.en: It drops line pressure quickly after injection.

recall_q.en: Purpose of the delivery valve?

explain_simple.en: Shuts the line quickly after each squirt.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Distributor (rotary) type pump (e.g. Bosch VE, CAV DPA): one pumping element and a rotor distribute fuel to all cylinders in turn.

why.en: Smaller, lighter and cheaper than in-line pumps.

recall_q.en: Pump that uses one element and a rotor for all cylinders?

explain_simple.en: One pump shared by all cylinders.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Distributor pumps suit small, high-speed diesel engines in cars and light vehicles.

why.en: They are compact and self-lubricated by diesel.

recall_q.en: Which pump type suits small car diesels?

explain_simple.en: Compact pumps for small diesels.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Distributor pumps are lubricated by diesel itself, so diesel quality (lubricity) matters.

why.en: Poor fuel can wear the pump.

recall_q.en: What lubricates a distributor pump?

explain_simple.en: Diesel oils the pump.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Fuel injector (nozzle) sprays diesel as a fine mist into the cylinder.

why.en: Fine drops mix and burn quickly.

recall_q.en: Job of a diesel injector?

recall_a.en: Atomise and spray fuel into the cylinder.

explain_simple.en: It sprays fine diesel mist.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Mechanical injector: a spring holds the needle closed; fuel pressure lifts it at the opening pressure (about 150–250 bar in older engines).

why.en: Below that pressure, the spray would be poor.

recall_q.en: What lifts the injector needle?

explain_simple.en: High pressure pushes the needle open.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Nozzle types: single-hole, multi-hole (direct injection), pintle and pintaux (indirect injection).

why.en: Each gives a different spray shape for its chamber.

recall_q.en: Which nozzle is used in direct injection engines?

explain_simple.en: Many holes for direct injection; pintle for side chambers.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Injector testing checks opening pressure, spray pattern, leakage and chatter on an injector tester.

why.en: Bad spray causes smoke and power loss.

recall_q.en: Name one injector test.

recall_a.en: Opening pressure, spray pattern, leak-back, chatter.

explain_simple.en: Check pressure and spray on a tester.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Leak-off pipes return extra fuel (used to lubricate and cool the injector needle) to the tank.

why.en: A little fuel always seeps past the needle.

recall_q.en: Purpose of injector leak-off pipes?

recall_a.en: Return excess fuel to the tank.

explain_simple.en: Pipes that send spare diesel back.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Unit injector combines the pump and injector in one unit at each cylinder, driven by a camshaft.

why.en: No high-pressure pipes, so very high pressures possible.

recall_q.en: Pump and injector combined in one unit is called?

explain_simple.en: Pump and nozzle in one body.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Diesel injection timing is advanced at higher speeds by an automatic timer (advance unit) in the pump.

why.en: Fuel needs the same time to burn, which is more crank degrees at high speed.

recall_q.en: What advances injection timing with speed?

recall_a.en: Automatic timing (advance) device in the pump.

explain_simple.en: Inject earlier when faster.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Diesel smoke colours: black = too much fuel or too little air; blue = oil burning; white = unburnt fuel (cold, retarded timing) or water.

why.en: Smoke colour helps diagnosis.

recall_q.en: Black smoke from a diesel engine means?

recall_a.en: Over-fuelling or not enough air (choked filter, bad injector).

explain_simple.en: Black = too much fuel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Turbocharger uses exhaust gas to spin a turbine, which drives a compressor that forces more air into the engine.

why.en: More air allows more fuel to burn, giving more power from the same engine size.

recall_q.en: What drives a turbocharger?

explain_simple.en: Waste exhaust spins a fan that blows in more air.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Turbocharger parts: turbine wheel (exhaust side), compressor wheel (intake side), common shaft, centre bearing housing (oil-lubricated), wastegate.

why.en: Turbine and compressor are on one shaft.

recall_q.en: What joins the turbine and compressor in a turbocharger?

explain_simple.en: Two fans on one shaft.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Turbochargers spin very fast (up to about 1–2 lakh rpm) and are lubricated by engine oil.

why.en: Very high speed needs a constant oil film.

recall_q.en: How is a turbocharger shaft lubricated?

explain_simple.en: Engine oil keeps the turbo shaft alive.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Let a turbo engine idle for a short time before switching off.

why.en: Stopping a hot turbo cuts oil flow and cooks the oil in the bearings.

recall_q.en: Why should a turbo engine idle before shut-down?

recall_a.en: To let the turbo slow down and cool with oil flowing.

explain_simple.en: Let the turbo cool before switching off.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Wastegate is a valve that lets some exhaust bypass the turbine to limit boost pressure.

why.en: Too much boost can damage the engine.

recall_q.en: What limits turbo boost pressure?

explain_simple.en: A bypass door that stops over-boost.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Intercooler (charge air cooler) cools the compressed air from the turbo before it enters the engine.

why.en: Cooler air is denser, gives more power and reduces knock and NOx.

recall_q.en: Why is an intercooler used with a turbo?

recall_a.en: Cool compressed air to make it denser.

explain_simple.en: Cold air packs more oxygen.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Turbo lag is the delay between pressing the accelerator and the turbo giving boost.

why.en: The turbine needs time to speed up from exhaust flow.

recall_q.en: Delay before turbo boost builds up is called?

explain_simple.en: Waiting for the turbo to spin up.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Turbo lag is reduced by small/light turbines, twin-scroll or twin turbos, ball-bearing turbos and variable geometry turbos (VGT).

why.en: They spin up faster at low exhaust flow.

recall_q.en: Name one way to reduce turbo lag.

recall_a.en: VGT, twin-scroll, smaller turbo, twin turbos.

explain_simple.en: Lighter, smarter turbos react faster.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Variable geometry turbocharger (VGT/VNT) has movable vanes around the turbine that change the gas flow angle.

why.en: Narrow vanes speed up gas at low rpm; open vanes at high rpm.

recall_q.en: Turbo with movable vanes around the turbine?

explain_simple.en: Vanes adjust to give boost at all speeds.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Turbocharger types: single, twin (parallel or sequential), twin-scroll, VGT, electric-assisted.

why.en: PSC may ask types.

recall_q.en: Two turbos where one works at low rpm and both at high rpm?

explain_simple.en: Small turbo first, big one later.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Supercharger vs turbocharger: supercharger is belt-driven by the engine (no lag, uses engine power); turbo uses waste exhaust (efficient, but lag).

why.en: Drive source decides the trade-off.

recall_q.en: Which has no lag: supercharger or turbocharger?

explain_simple.en: Belt-driven blower reacts at once.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Tank → feed pump (hand primer) → filters → FIP → injectors.
In-line pump (helix, rack); distributor/rotary pump for small engines.
Delivery valve gives sharp cut-off; multi-hole nozzle for DI.
Turbo: exhaust turbine + compressor on one shaft, oil-cooled.
Wastegate limits boost; intercooler cools air; turbo lag → VGT.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Engine lubrication reduces friction and wear, cools parts, seals piston rings, cleans and protects from rust.

why.en: Metal-to-metal contact would quickly destroy the engine.

recall_q.en: Give three functions of engine oil.

recall_a.en: Reduce friction, cool, seal, clean, prevent rust.

explain_simple.en: Oil makes parts slide, keeps them cool and clean.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Lubrication systems: petroil (two-stroke), splash, pressure feed (forced), semi-pressure (combined), dry sump.

why.en: Each suits a different engine.

recall_q.en: System where all bearings get oil from a pump under pressure?

explain_simple.en: Splash, pump pressure, or both.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Splash lubrication: dippers on the connecting rod big ends dip into oil troughs and splash oil around.

why.en: Simple, but oil supply is uneven; used in small engines.

recall_q.en: In splash lubrication, what throws the oil?

explain_simple.en: The rod scoops and splashes oil.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Pressure feed: oil pump sends oil through a filter and main gallery to main bearings, big ends (via drilled crankshaft), camshaft bearings and valve gear.

why.en: Gives positive, steady supply to all bearings.

recall_q.en: How does oil reach big-end bearings in pressure feed?

recall_a.en: Through drilled passages in the crankshaft.

explain_simple.en: Oil goes through holes inside the crankshaft.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Wet sump: oil is stored in the sump under the crankcase. Most cars use wet sump.

why.en: Simple and cheap.

recall_q.en: In a wet sump system, where is oil stored?

recall_a.en: In the sump under the crankcase.

explain_simple.en: Oil lives at the bottom of the engine.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Dry sump: oil is pumped out of the sump by a scavenge pump to a separate tank, and a pressure pump feeds the engine from it.

why.en: No oil surge on hard corners; engine can sit lower; better cooling.

recall_q.en: How many pumps does a dry sump system have?

explain_simple.en: Oil kept in a separate tank.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Dry sump is used in racing cars, aircraft, some motorcycles and off-road vehicles.

why.en: Oil supply stays steady at steep angles and high g-forces.

recall_q.en: Where is dry sump lubrication used?

recall_a.en: Racing cars, aircraft, some bikes and off-road vehicles.

explain_simple.en: For vehicles that tilt or corner hard.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Oil pump types: gear pump (external gears), rotor (gerotor) pump, vane pump, plunger pump.

why.en: All are positive displacement pumps.

recall_q.en: Two common types of engine oil pumps?

explain_simple.en: Gears or rotors push the oil.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Rotor (gerotor) pump: an inner rotor with one lobe less than the outer rotor turns inside it, trapping and pushing oil.

why.en: Compact and smooth flow.

recall_q.en: In a rotor pump, how many lobes does the inner rotor have compared to outer?

explain_simple.en: Inner star turns inside outer star.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Oil strainer (pick-up screen) at the pump inlet stops large particles entering the pump.

why.en: Protects the pump.

recall_q.en: What protects the oil pump inlet?

explain_simple.en: A mesh at the pump's mouth.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Pressure relief valve limits maximum oil pressure by returning excess oil to the sump.

why.en: Cold thick oil could build dangerous pressure.

recall_q.en: Purpose of the oil pressure relief valve?

explain_simple.en: Lets extra oil escape back to the sump.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Oil pressure indicator: a warning light (pressure switch) or gauge on the dashboard. The light comes on when pressure is too low.

why.en: Low pressure can destroy bearings in seconds.

recall_q.en: Oil warning light comes on while driving. What should the driver do?

recall_a.en: Stop the engine at once and check oil.

explain_simple.en: Oil light on = stop now.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Oil filtration systems: full-flow (all oil passes the filter before bearings) and bypass (only part of the oil is filtered).

why.en: Full-flow is most common in cars.

recall_q.en: Filter system where all oil is filtered before reaching bearings?

explain_simple.en: Full-flow cleans all the oil every time.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Full-flow filters have a bypass valve that opens if the filter gets blocked.

why.en: Dirty oil is better than no oil.

recall_q.en: Why does a full-flow filter have a bypass valve?

recall_a.en: To keep oil flowing if the filter clogs.

explain_simple.en: If the filter blocks, oil goes around it.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Oil filter types: cartridge (replaceable element) and spin-on (throw-away). Elements: paper, cloth, felt; centrifugal filters in some diesels.

why.en: Spin-on filters are quick to change.

recall_q.en: Throw-away screwed filter is called?

explain_simple.en: Screw on, screw off, throw away.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Oil cooler: a small radiator for engine oil, cooled by air or coolant.

why.en: Hot oil thins and breaks down.

recall_q.en: Why is an oil cooler used?

recall_a.en: Keep oil temperature in safe range.

explain_simple.en: A mini radiator for oil.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Oil seals (lip seals) stop oil leaking where shafts come out of the engine, e.g. front and rear crankshaft seals.

why.en: A spring-loaded rubber lip presses on the shaft.

recall_q.en: Seal used where the crankshaft leaves the block?

explain_simple.en: A rubber lip hugs the shaft.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Crankcase ventilation removes blow-by gases (unburnt fuel, water vapour, acids) from the crankcase.

why.en: These gases dilute oil and form sludge.

recall_q.en: Why is crankcase ventilation needed?

recall_a.en: Remove blow-by gases that contaminate oil.

explain_simple.en: Let leaked gases out of the oil area.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Old open (road draught) ventilation vented gases to air. Modern PCV (positive crankcase ventilation) sends them into the intake to be burnt.

why.en: PCV cuts pollution.

recall_q.en: Where does a PCV system send crankcase gases?

recall_a.en: Into the intake manifold to be burnt.

explain_simple.en: Burn the leaked gases instead of releasing them.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Oil level is checked with the dipstick, engine off and on level ground. Keep it between MIN and MAX marks.

why.en: Too low starves bearings; too high causes foaming.

recall_q.en: How is engine oil level checked?

recall_a.en: With the dipstick, on level ground, engine off.

explain_simple.en: Pull the stick, wipe, dip, read.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Oil grades: SAE (viscosity, e.g. 15W-40), API service (S for petrol, C for diesel, e.g. API SN, CK-4).

why.en: Use the grade the maker specifies.

recall_q.en: In API classification, C stands for?

explain_simple.en: S = spark (petrol), C = compression (diesel).

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Oil additives: detergent-dispersants, anti-wear (ZDDP), anti-oxidants, viscosity index improvers, pour point depressants, anti-foam, corrosion inhibitors.

why.en: Base oil alone cannot do all jobs.

recall_q.en: Additive that keeps dirt in suspension?

explain_simple.en: Additives give oil extra powers.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Low oil pressure causes: low oil level, worn bearings, worn pump, blocked strainer, thin oil, stuck relief valve.

why.en: Each lets pressure fall.

recall_q.en: Name one cause of low oil pressure.

recall_a.en: Low oil level, worn bearings or pump, thin oil.

explain_simple.en: Too little oil or too much leak-away.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Splash (dippers), pressure feed (pump), combined.
Wet sump (cars) vs dry sump (racing, 2 pumps).
Gear or rotor pump; relief valve limits pressure.
Full-flow filter with bypass valve; oil cooler; lip seals.
PCV burns blow-by gases; SAE and API grades.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: The cooling system removes extra heat from the engine and keeps it at the best working temperature (about 80–95°C).

why.en: Too hot: parts seize and oil fails. Too cold: poor efficiency and wear.

recall_q.en: Why does an engine need a cooling system?

recall_a.en: Remove excess heat and keep correct temperature.

explain_simple.en: Keep the engine not too hot, not too cold.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: About 30% of fuel heat is removed by the cooling system.

why.en: Part of the heat balance.

recall_q.en: Roughly what share of fuel heat goes to coolant?

explain_simple.en: About one-third goes to cooling.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Two types of cooling: air cooling and water (liquid) cooling.

why.en: Small engines use air; most cars use liquid.

recall_q.en: Two types of engine cooling?

explain_simple.en: Air or water.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Air cooling uses fins on the cylinder and head to give off heat to air. Fans and cowls (shrouds) help in scooters and some engines.

why.en: Fins increase area for heat loss.

example.en: Motorcycles, scooters, older autorickshaws.

recall_q.en: What helps an air-cooled engine lose heat?

explain_simple.en: Fins let air carry heat away.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Air cooling: light, simple, no leaks or freezing; but noisy, uneven cooling and limited to small engines.

why.en: Air carries much less heat than water.

recall_q.en: Give one disadvantage of air cooling.

recall_a.en: Uneven cooling / noisy / only for small engines.

explain_simple.en: Simple but weak for big engines.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Water cooling parts: water jackets, water pump, radiator, pressure cap, thermostat, fan, hoses, coolant reservoir.

why.en: Coolant carries heat from engine to radiator.

recall_q.en: Name the main parts of a water cooling system.

recall_a.en: Jackets, pump, radiator, cap, thermostat, fan, hoses.

explain_simple.en: Pump moves water from engine to radiator and back.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Thermo-syphon cooling: water circulates by itself because hot water rises and cool water sinks. No pump is used.

why.en: Density difference drives the flow.

recall_q.en: Cooling system that works without a water pump?

explain_simple.en: Hot water rises, cold sinks, no pump.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Thermo-syphon is slow; the radiator must be above the engine and water level kept high. Used in old and small stationary engines.

why.en: Natural circulation is weak.

recall_q.en: Main drawback of thermo-syphon cooling?

recall_a.en: Slow circulation; radiator must be high; level critical.

explain_simple.en: Too slow for modern engines.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Pump circulation (forced) system: a centrifugal water pump driven by belt circulates coolant quickly.

why.en: Fast, steady flow for high-output engines.

recall_q.en: Type of water pump used in cars?

explain_simple.en: A belt-driven spinning pump moves the water.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Water pump is driven by the fan belt or timing belt from the crankshaft. It has an impeller, seal and bearing.

why.en: Seal failure causes leaks from the weep hole.

recall_q.en: What drives the water pump?

explain_simple.en: The engine turns the pump with a belt.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Thermostat is a valve between engine and radiator. It stays closed when cold and opens at about 80–90°C.

why.en: It helps the engine warm up quickly and keeps it at the right temperature.

recall_q.en: Function of the thermostat?

recall_a.en: Quick warm-up and control engine temperature.

explain_simple.en: Shut when cold, open when hot.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Thermostat types: wax pellet (most common), bellows (with volatile liquid like alcohol), bimetallic.

why.en: Wax expands when it melts and pushes the valve open.

recall_q.en: Most common type of thermostat?

explain_simple.en: Melting wax opens the valve.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Thermostat stuck closed → overheating. Stuck open → engine runs cold, heater weak, more fuel use.

why.en: Coolant cannot reach the radiator, or goes there too early.

recall_q.en: Effect of a thermostat stuck closed?

explain_simple.en: Closed = too hot. Open = too cold.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Bypass passage lets coolant circulate within the engine while the thermostat is closed.

why.en: Prevents hot spots and pressure rise during warm-up.

recall_q.en: Purpose of the bypass passage in cooling system?

recall_a.en: Circulate coolant in engine when thermostat is closed.

explain_simple.en: A short path for water while warming up.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Radiator is a heat exchanger that cools hot coolant using air flowing through its core.

why.en: Thin tubes and fins give a large cooling area.

recall_q.en: Main job of the radiator?

recall_a.en: Transfer heat from coolant to air.

explain_simple.en: Radiator cools the water with air.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Radiator parts: upper tank (inlet), core, lower tank (outlet), filler neck with pressure cap, drain cock.

why.en: Hot water enters the top and cooled water leaves the bottom.

recall_q.en: Where does hot coolant enter the radiator?

explain_simple.en: Hot in at top, cool out at bottom.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Radiator core types: tubular (fin and tube) and cellular (honeycomb). Flow types: down-flow and cross-flow.

why.en: Cross-flow radiators are lower and fit under sloping bonnets.

recall_q.en: Radiator with coolant flowing sideways between side tanks?

explain_simple.en: Down-flow top to bottom; cross-flow side to side.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Radiators are made of copper-brass (older) or aluminium core with plastic tanks (modern).

why.en: Good heat conductors; aluminium is lighter.

recall_q.en: Material of modern radiators?

explain_simple.en: Light aluminium and plastic.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Pressure cap raises the system pressure (about 0.9–1.1 bar extra), which raises the boiling point of coolant to about 120°C.

why.en: Boiling point rises with pressure, like a pressure cooker.

recall_q.en: Why is a pressure cap used on the radiator?

explain_simple.en: Pressure stops water boiling early.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Pressure cap has two valves: a pressure valve (opens to the overflow when pressure is high) and a vacuum valve (lets coolant back in when cooling down).

why.en: Prevents bursting hoses and collapsing hoses.

recall_q.en: Two valves in a radiator pressure cap?

explain_simple.en: One lets out, one lets back in.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Never open a hot radiator cap.

why.en: Pressurised hot coolant can spray out and scald.

recall_q.en: Is it safe to open a hot radiator cap?

explain_simple.en: Hot cap = danger of burns.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Coolant = water + antifreeze (ethylene glycol or propylene glycol) + corrosion inhibitors. Usually 50:50 mix.

why.en: Lowers freezing point, raises boiling point and stops corrosion.

recall_q.en: Common antifreeze chemical?

explain_simple.en: Water plus glycol protects in heat and cold.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Antifreeze is used even in hot places like Kerala because it prevents rust and scale and raises boiling point.

why.en: Plain water corrodes metal and leaves deposits.

recall_q.en: Why use coolant with antifreeze in hot climates?

recall_a.en: Corrosion protection and higher boiling point.

explain_simple.en: Coolant protects metal, not just from cold.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Other antifreeze materials: methanol, ethanol (wood alcohol, alcohol), glycerine. Ethylene glycol is preferred.

why.en: Alcohols evaporate easily.

recall_q.en: Why is alcohol less preferred as antifreeze?

explain_simple.en: Alcohol boils away.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Expansion (overflow) tank stores coolant pushed out when hot and returns it when cold.

why.en: Keeps the radiator always full.

recall_q.en: Purpose of the coolant expansion tank?

recall_a.en: Store expanding coolant and return it when cool.

explain_simple.en: A side bottle for extra coolant.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Cooling fan types: belt-driven fixed fan, viscous (fluid) coupling fan, thermostatically controlled electric fan.

why.en: Fan only needed at low speed or in traffic.

recall_q.en: Fan type that switches on only when coolant is hot?

explain_simple.en: Electric fan runs only when needed.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Viscous fan coupling uses silicone fluid; it slips when cool and locks up when the air behind the radiator is hot.

why.en: Saves power and reduces noise.

recall_q.en: Fluid used in a viscous fan coupling?

explain_simple.en: Thick fluid connects the fan only when hot.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Fan shroud directs air through the whole radiator core.

why.en: Without it, air leaks around the fan edges.

recall_q.en: Purpose of a fan shroud?

recall_a.en: Direct air through the radiator core.

explain_simple.en: A cover that guides air.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Overheating causes: low coolant, leaks, loose or broken fan belt, stuck thermostat, blocked radiator, faulty pump, fan failure, head gasket leak.

why.en: Any break in heat removal causes it.

recall_q.en: Name two causes of engine overheating.

recall_a.en: Low coolant, broken belt, stuck thermostat, blocked radiator, fan failure.

explain_simple.en: Not enough water, flow or air.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Temperature gauge sender is a thermistor in the coolant passage; resistance falls as temperature rises.

why.en: The gauge reads the change in current.

recall_q.en: Sensor used for coolant temperature gauge?

explain_simple.en: Its resistance changes with heat.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Air cooling (fins) vs water cooling.
Thermo-syphon (no pump) vs pump circulation.
Thermostat (wax) opens ~85°C; bypass for warm-up.
Pressure cap raises boiling point; pressure + vacuum valves.
Coolant = water + ethylene glycol; electric/viscous fans.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Chassis means the whole vehicle without the body: frame, engine, transmission, suspension, steering, brakes and wheels.

why.en: It is everything needed to make the vehicle move.

recall_q.en: What is a chassis?

recall_a.en: The vehicle without its body (frame + running gear).

explain_simple.en: The running vehicle without the body shell.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: The frame is the backbone of the chassis. It supports the body, engine and all other units.

why.en: It must carry loads and resist bending and twisting.

recall_q.en: Main job of the frame?

recall_a.en: Support all parts and carry loads.

explain_simple.en: The skeleton of the vehicle.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Loads on a frame: weight of vehicle and passengers (bending), road twisting (torsion), braking and acceleration (longitudinal), cornering (side), and impacts.

why.en: The frame must handle all of these together.

recall_q.en: Name two loads acting on a vehicle frame.

recall_a.en: Bending, torsion, braking, side and impact loads.

explain_simple.en: Weight, twist, push, pull and knocks.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Conventional (ladder) frame: two long side members joined by cross members, like a ladder. Used in trucks, buses and SUVs.

why.en: Strong, simple and easy to repair.

recall_q.en: Frame used in trucks and buses?

explain_simple.en: Two long rails with cross bars, like a ladder.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Frameless (integral / unitary / monocoque) construction: body and frame are one welded shell. Used in most cars.

why.en: Lighter and stiffer, with lower floor.

recall_q.en: Construction where body and frame are a single unit?

explain_simple.en: The body itself is the frame.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Semi-integral frame: a light frame is joined to the body through rubber mounts, sharing some loads.

why.en: Combines parts of both designs.

recall_q.en: Frame between conventional and integral types?

explain_simple.en: Half frame, half body.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Other frame types: backbone (central tube), X-frame, perimeter frame, space frame (tube cage, racing cars).

why.en: Each balances stiffness and weight.

recall_q.en: Frame made of many small tubes forming a cage?

explain_simple.en: A cage of tubes.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Frame sections used for side members: channel (C) section (most common), box section, tubular section, I-section.

why.en: Channel is easy to make and good in bending; box resists twisting.

recall_q.en: Most common section for frame side members?

explain_simple.en: C-shaped steel rails.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Box section is best against torsion (twisting). Channel section is best in bending for its weight.

why.en: A closed section resists twist much better.

recall_q.en: Which section best resists twisting?

explain_simple.en: Closed box = hard to twist.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Frame side members are deeper in the middle (between axles) where bending moment is greatest.

why.en: More depth gives more strength where needed.

recall_q.en: Why is a frame deeper at the centre?

explain_simple.en: Make it strongest where it bends most.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Frame is narrow at the front (kick-up / narrowed) to allow wheels to turn for steering, and upswept at the rear over the axle.

why.en: Front wheels need room to turn; rear axle needs room to move.

recall_q.en: Why is the frame upswept at the rear?

recall_a.en: To give room for rear axle movement.

explain_simple.en: Bent up over the axle for clearance.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Frame material: mild steel or low-alloy steel sheet, pressed and riveted or welded. Some cars use aluminium.

why.en: Steel is strong, cheap and repairable.

recall_q.en: Common material for vehicle frames?

explain_simple.en: Pressed steel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Sub-frame: a smaller separate frame carrying the engine, suspension or axle, bolted to the main body through rubber mounts.

why.en: It isolates vibration and makes assembly easier.

recall_q.en: What is a sub-frame?

recall_a.en: A small frame carrying engine/suspension, mounted to the body.

explain_simple.en: A mini frame for the engine or suspension.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Bumpers absorb small impacts and protect the body. Modern bumpers are plastic covers over energy-absorbing foam and a steel or aluminium beam.

why.en: They soak up low-speed crash energy.

recall_q.en: Function of a bumper?

explain_simple.en: A cushion at the front and back.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Fitting bull bars (crash guards) on cars is banned in India.

why.en: They make crashes worse for pedestrians and stop airbag sensors working properly.

recall_q.en: Are bull bars allowed on cars in India?

explain_simple.en: Metal guards on cars are not allowed.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Crumple zones: front and rear parts of the body designed to crush in a crash, absorbing energy. The passenger cell stays rigid.

why.en: Slower deceleration means less injury.

recall_q.en: Purpose of crumple zones?

recall_a.en: Absorb crash energy so the cabin stays safe.

explain_simple.en: The ends crush so people do not.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Frame defects: cracks, bending, sagging, twisting and loose rivets. Alignment is checked with diagonal measurements.

why.en: Equal diagonals show the frame is square.

recall_q.en: How is frame alignment checked simply?

explain_simple.en: Cross measurements must match.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Chassis layouts: front engine rear drive, front engine front drive, rear engine rear drive, mid engine, four-wheel drive.

why.en: Layout affects space, traction and handling.

recall_q.en: Most common layout in Indian small cars?

explain_simple.en: Engine and drive both at the front.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Chassis = vehicle without body; frame = backbone.
Ladder frame (trucks) vs integral/monocoque (cars), semi-integral.
Channel section common; box best for torsion.
Narrowed front, upswept rear, deeper middle.
Sub-frames, bumpers, crumple zones.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Front axle and stub axle; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Dead axle carries only weight; it does not drive the wheels. Live axle carries weight and also drives the wheels.

why.en: Live axles have shafts inside to transmit power.

recall_q.en: An axle that carries load but does not transmit power is?

explain_simple.en: Dead = just holds. Live = holds and drives.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Front axle and stub axle; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Front axle of a rear-wheel-drive vehicle is a dead axle. Front axle of a front-wheel-drive vehicle is a live axle.

why.en: It depends on which wheels are driven.

recall_q.en: Front axle of a rear-wheel-drive truck is dead or live?

explain_simple.en: Truck front axle just steers and carries.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Front axle and stub axle; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Front axle beam has an I-section in the middle and round or elliptical section near the ends.

why.en: I-section resists bending; round ends resist twisting from braking.

recall_q.en: Cross section of a front axle beam in the middle?

explain_simple.en: I-shape for strength in the middle.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Front axle and stub axle; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Front axle beam is dropped (bent down) in the middle.

why.en: This lowers the chassis and engine for stability.

recall_q.en: Why is the front axle beam dropped at the centre?

explain_simple.en: Bent down to sit the vehicle lower.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Front axle and stub axle; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Front axle is made of drop-forged medium carbon steel or nickel steel.

why.en: It needs high strength and toughness.

recall_q.en: Front axle material?

recall_a.en: Drop-forged medium carbon or alloy steel.

explain_simple.en: Forged strong steel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Front axle and stub axle; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Stub axle carries the front wheel and turns on a kingpin for steering.

why.en: It lets the wheel steer while the axle beam stays still.

recall_q.en: The short axle on which the front wheel turns for steering?

explain_simple.en: The small axle that pivots to steer.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Front axle and stub axle; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Stub axle types: Elliott, reversed Elliott, Lemoine, reversed Lemoine.

why.en: They differ in how the stub axle and beam end fit together.

recall_q.en: Name the four types of stub axle.

recall_a.en: Elliott, reversed Elliott, Lemoine, reversed Lemoine.

explain_simple.en: Four ways to join stub axle and beam.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Front axle and stub axle; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Elliott type: the axle beam end fits between the forked (yoke) stub axle. Reversed Elliott: the beam end is forked and the stub axle fits inside.

why.en: Reversed Elliott is the most common.

recall_q.en: Most common stub axle arrangement?

explain_simple.en: In reversed Elliott, the beam has the fork.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Front axle and stub axle; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Lemoine type: an L-shaped stub axle fits under the beam end (no fork). Reversed Lemoine fits above.

why.en: Used where height is limited.

recall_q.en: Stub axle with L-shaped spindle and no fork?

explain_simple.en: Lemoine = L-shape, no yoke.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Front axle and stub axle; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Kingpin (swivel pin) joins the stub axle to the axle beam and lets it swing for steering.

why.en: It is the steering pivot.

recall_q.en: Pin on which the stub axle swivels?

explain_simple.en: The hinge pin for steering.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Front axle and stub axle; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Modern cars with independent suspension use ball joints instead of kingpins.

why.en: Ball joints allow both steering and suspension movement.

recall_q.en: What replaces kingpins in independent front suspension?

explain_simple.en: Ball joints swivel in all directions.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Front axle and stub axle; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Thrust bearing between the stub axle and the beam carries the vehicle weight while letting the stub axle turn.

why.en: Makes steering light.

recall_q.en: Bearing that takes vehicle weight at the kingpin?

explain_simple.en: A bearing under the pivot for easy steering.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Front axle and stub axle; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Steering knuckle is the part carrying the stub axle, steering arm and brake parts.

why.en: It joins steering, suspension and wheel.

recall_q.en: Part that carries the stub axle and steering arm?

explain_simple.en: The joint that holds the wheel and turns.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Front axle and stub axle; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Dead axle carries load; live axle also drives.
Front beam: I-section middle, dropped centre, forged steel.
Stub axle types: Elliott, reversed Elliott (common), Lemoine, reversed Lemoine.
Kingpin pivot; ball joints in independent suspension.
Thrust bearing carries weight at kingpin.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Suspension connects wheels to the frame and absorbs road shocks.

why.en: It gives comfort, keeps tyres on the road and protects the vehicle.

recall_q.en: Main job of suspension?

recall_a.en: Absorb road shocks and keep wheels on road.

explain_simple.en: It makes the ride smooth and safe.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Functions of suspension: comfort, road holding, stability on turns and braking, protect load and parts, carry weight.

why.en: Each is needed for safe driving.

recall_q.en: Name two functions of suspension.

recall_a.en: Comfort, road holding, stability, carry load.

explain_simple.en: Comfort and grip.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Sprung weight: parts supported by springs (body, frame, engine). Unsprung weight: parts not supported by springs (wheels, tyres, axles, brakes).

why.en: Low unsprung weight gives better ride and grip.

recall_q.en: Is the wheel sprung or unsprung weight?

explain_simple.en: Above springs = sprung. Below = unsprung.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Rigid axle (dependent) suspension: both wheels are on one axle, so a bump on one wheel affects the other.

why.en: The axle is a single beam.

recall_q.en: Suspension where a bump on one wheel affects the other?

explain_simple.en: Both wheels joined by one bar.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Independent suspension: each wheel moves up and down separately.

why.en: Better comfort and road grip.

recall_q.en: Main advantage of independent suspension?

recall_a.en: One wheel's bump does not affect the other; better ride.

explain_simple.en: Each wheel moves on its own.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Independent front suspension types: MacPherson strut, double wishbone, trailing link, swinging axle.

why.en: MacPherson is the most common in cars.

recall_q.en: Most common front suspension in cars?

explain_simple.en: MacPherson strut for most cars.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: MacPherson strut: a shock absorber and coil spring in one unit, which also acts as the steering pivot, with one lower arm.

why.en: Simple, compact and leaves room for engine.

recall_q.en: In a MacPherson strut, what acts as the steering pivot?

recall_a.en: The strut itself (top mount and lower ball joint).

explain_simple.en: Spring + shock in one tube that also steers.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Double wishbone: upper and lower A-shaped arms hold the wheel. Gives good control of camber.

why.en: Used in SUVs, sports cars and premium cars.

recall_q.en: Suspension with upper and lower A-arms?

explain_simple.en: Two triangle arms, one above, one below.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Two-wheeler front suspension: telescopic fork (most common), leading link, trailing link. Rear: swing arm with twin shocks or mono-shock.

why.en: Telescopic forks are simple and strong.

recall_q.en: Most common motorcycle front suspension?

explain_simple.en: Two sliding tubes with springs inside.
