cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Three-wheeler (autorickshaw) front: single trailing/leading link with coil spring or torsion bar and shock absorber. Rear: swing arms with coil springs.

why.en: One front wheel needs a single-arm design.

recall_q.en: Front suspension of an autorickshaw is usually?

recall_a.en: Single link (trailing/leading) with spring and shock absorber.

explain_simple.en: One arm for the single front wheel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Rear suspension types: rigid axle with leaf springs (trucks, buses), rigid axle with coil springs and links, twist beam (small FWD cars), independent multi-link.

why.en: Load capacity and cost decide the choice.

recall_q.en: Rear suspension in most small front-wheel-drive cars?

explain_simple.en: A bendy beam linking the rear wheels.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Spring types used: leaf (laminated), coil, torsion bar, rubber, air (pneumatic), hydro-pneumatic.

why.en: Each stores energy in a different way.

recall_q.en: Spring that twists to give springing action?

explain_simple.en: Leaf, coil, twist bar, rubber, air.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Leaf spring types: semi-elliptic (most common), quarter-elliptic, three-quarter elliptic, full elliptic, transverse.

why.en: Semi-elliptic suits trucks and buses.

recall_q.en: Most common leaf spring type?

explain_simple.en: A curved stack of steel strips.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Leaf spring parts: master leaf with eyes, other leaves, centre bolt, rebound clips, U-bolts, spring seat, shackle.

why.en: Rebound clips keep leaves together on rebound.

recall_q.en: What holds leaves together and stops them spreading on rebound?

explain_simple.en: Clips hold the stack together.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Leaves are of graded length so the spring has nearly uniform strength along its length.

why.en: Bending moment is highest at the centre.

recall_q.en: Why do leaves have different lengths?

recall_a.en: To give uniform strength (more leaves at centre).

explain_simple.en: Thickest where bending is most.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Leaf springs also locate the axle and transmit driving and braking forces (Hotchkiss drive).

why.en: No extra links needed.

recall_q.en: Besides springing, what else do leaf springs do?

recall_a.en: Locate the axle and carry drive/brake forces.

explain_simple.en: They spring and hold the axle in place.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Interleaf friction in a leaf spring damps vibration, but makes the ride harsher. Leaves are greased or have plastic inserts.

why.en: Too much friction stiffens the spring.

recall_q.en: Why are leaf springs lubricated?

recall_a.en: To reduce interleaf friction and noise.

explain_simple.en: Grease stops the leaves squeaking and sticking.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Spring shackle: a swinging link at one end of the leaf spring that allows the spring length to change as it flexes.

why.en: A bent spring gets longer when it straightens.

recall_q.en: Why is a shackle fitted at one end of a leaf spring?

recall_a.en: To allow change in spring length during flexing.

explain_simple.en: A swinging link lets the spring stretch.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Shackle pin connects the shackle to the spring eye and frame. Eyes have bushes (bronze or rubber).

why.en: Pins and bushes wear and need greasing.

recall_q.en: Pin joining the shackle and spring eye?

explain_simple.en: The pin through the spring eye.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Front end of a leaf spring is usually fixed to the frame by a bracket; the rear end has the shackle.

why.en: Fixed front end keeps the axle located during braking.

recall_q.en: Which end of a leaf spring usually has the shackle?

explain_simple.en: Front fixed, rear swinging.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Helper spring: an extra small leaf spring above the main spring that works only under heavy load.

why.en: Soft ride when empty, strong support when loaded.

example.en: Pick-up trucks and lorries.

recall_q.en: What is a helper spring?

recall_a.en: An extra spring that acts only under heavy load.

explain_simple.en: A backup spring for heavy loads.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Coil springs: light, compact, need no lubrication, but cannot locate the axle, so links or arms are needed.

why.en: They only take vertical load.

recall_q.en: Drawback of coil springs compared to leaf springs?

recall_a.en: Cannot locate axle/carry side or drive forces; need links.

explain_simple.en: Coils only push up; arms are needed to hold the axle.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Coil spring arrangements: around the shock absorber (coil-over), between lower arm and body, on rigid axle with links (four-link, Panhard rod).

why.en: Layout depends on suspension design.

recall_q.en: A rod that stops sideways movement of a rigid axle?

explain_simple.en: A side rod to keep the axle centred.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Air suspension uses rubber air bags (bellows) with compressed air. A levelling valve keeps ride height constant with load.

why.en: Same ride height empty or full.

example.en: Volvo and Scania buses in KSRTC use air suspension.

recall_q.en: Advantage of air suspension in buses?

recall_a.en: Constant height and soft ride at any load.

explain_simple.en: Air bags adjust to the load.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Anti-roll bar (stabiliser bar) links left and right suspension to reduce body roll on turns.

why.en: It twists when one side moves more than the other.

recall_q.en: Purpose of an anti-roll bar?

explain_simple.en: Stops the car leaning too much.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A shock absorber (damper) controls spring oscillations. It turns movement energy into heat in oil.

why.en: Without it, the car would keep bouncing after a bump.

recall_q.en: Main function of a shock absorber?

explain_simple.en: It stops the bouncing.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Springs absorb shocks; shock absorbers do not absorb shocks — they damp (calm) the spring movement.

why.en: Common PSC trap.

recall_q.en: Do shock absorbers absorb road shocks?

recall_a.en: No — springs absorb, dampers control the bounce.

explain_simple.en: Spring takes the hit; damper stops the bounce.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Telescopic shock absorber: piston with small valves moves in an oil-filled cylinder. Oil forced through valves resists motion.

why.en: Small holes slow the oil flow.

recall_q.en: Most common type of shock absorber?

explain_simple.en: A piston pushing oil through tiny holes.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Telescopic damper parts: inner pressure tube, outer reservoir tube, piston with valves, piston rod, foot (base) valve, seal and dust cover.

why.en: Twin-tube design keeps extra oil in the reservoir.

recall_q.en: Tube that stores reserve oil in a twin-tube damper?

explain_simple.en: Inner tube works, outer tube stores oil.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Shock absorbers usually resist more on rebound (extension) than on bump (compression).

why.en: Soft bump for comfort, firm rebound to control bounce.

recall_q.en: Is damping usually stronger on bump or rebound?

explain_simple.en: Easy going down, slow coming up.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Single-acting damper works only on rebound. Double-acting works on both bump and rebound. Most are double-acting.

why.en: Control in both directions is better.

recall_q.en: Damper that works in both directions is called?

explain_simple.en: Double-acting controls up and down.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Gas-charged (monotube) shock absorbers have nitrogen gas under pressure to stop oil foaming (aeration).

why.en: Foamed oil gives weak damping.

recall_q.en: Why is nitrogen filled in gas shock absorbers?

explain_simple.en: Gas keeps the oil from bubbling.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Other damper types: lever arm (older), friction (old), adjustable and electronically controlled (adaptive) dampers.

why.en: Adaptive dampers change stiffness as needed.

recall_q.en: Old type of damper using rubbing plates?

explain_simple.en: Old dampers rubbed; new ones use oil.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Worn shock absorbers: car keeps bouncing, nose dives on braking, poor grip, uneven (cupped) tyre wear, oil leaks.

why.en: Damping is lost.

recall_q.en: How can you check a shock absorber quickly?

recall_a.en: Bounce test: push down and see if it bounces more than once or twice.

explain_simple.en: Push the car; it should settle quickly.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Rubber bump stops (bumpers) prevent metal-to-metal contact at full suspension travel.

why.en: They cushion the last bit of movement.

recall_q.en: Purpose of bump stops?

recall_a.en: Prevent metal contact at full compression.

explain_simple.en: Rubber blocks at the end of travel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Sprung vs unsprung weight; rigid vs independent.
Front: MacPherson, double wishbone; bikes: telescopic fork.
Leaf spring: master leaf, rebound clips, U-bolts, shackle at rear.
Helper spring for heavy loads; anti-roll bar cuts roll.
Springs absorb; telescopic dampers damp, stronger on rebound.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Steering system lets the driver turn the front wheels to change direction.

why.en: It must be light, precise and safe.

recall_q.en: Main function of steering system?

recall_a.en: Turn the wheels to control direction.

explain_simple.en: It points the wheels where you want to go.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Requirements of steering: easy to turn, self-centring after a turn, stable straight running, little road shock to the wheel, correct turning geometry.

why.en: Good steering keeps the driver in control.

recall_q.en: Name one requirement of a good steering system.

explain_simple.en: Easy, steady and returns straight.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: For true rolling on a turn, all wheels must turn about one common centre (instantaneous centre).

why.en: Otherwise tyres slip and wear.

recall_q.en: Condition for correct steering?

recall_a.en: All wheels turn about a common centre.

explain_simple.en: Every wheel circles the same point.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: On a turn, the inner front wheel turns more sharply than the outer wheel.

why.en: The inner wheel follows a smaller circle.

recall_q.en: Which front wheel turns more on a turn: inner or outer?

explain_simple.en: Inside wheel turns tighter.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Condition for correct steering: cot φ − cot θ = c / b. (φ outer angle, θ inner angle, c = distance between kingpin centres, b = wheelbase).

why.en: This gives true rolling of all wheels.

recall_q.en: Write the condition for correct steering.

explain_simple.en: Formula linking inner and outer wheel angles.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Ackermann steering mechanism uses a trapezium linkage (steering arms angled inward) and has only turning pairs.

why.en: It is simple and used in almost all vehicles.

recall_q.en: Steering mechanism used in most vehicles?

explain_simple.en: A four-bar trapezium linkage.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Ackermann gives correct steering in only three positions: straight ahead and one position each to left and right.

why.en: In between, there is a small error.

recall_q.en: In how many positions does Ackermann give exact steering?

explain_simple.en: Exact at three points, close elsewhere.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Davis steering gear uses sliding pairs and gives correct steering in all positions. It is not used much because sliding parts wear.

why.en: Sliding pairs have more friction and wear.

recall_q.en: Which mechanism is theoretically correct in all positions?

explain_simple.en: Davis is perfect but wears fast.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Ackermann has turning pairs only; Davis has sliding pairs.

why.en: This is the main difference asked in exams.

recall_q.en: Which steering mechanism has sliding pairs?

explain_simple.en: Davis slides; Ackermann turns.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Fifth wheel steering: the whole front axle turns about a central pivot. Used in horse carts and trailers (fifth wheel coupling).

why.en: Simple but unstable for fast vehicles.

recall_q.en: Steering where the whole axle turns on a centre pivot?

explain_simple.en: Whole axle swivels like a bullock cart.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Steering linkage parts (rigid axle): steering wheel → column → gearbox → drop arm (pitman arm) → drag link → steering arm → stub axle; track rod joins both stub axles.

why.en: Each part passes motion to the wheels.

recall_q.en: Rod connecting the two steering arms?

explain_simple.en: Wheel → box → drop arm → drag link → wheels.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Drop arm (pitman arm) is attached to the steering gearbox output shaft; it swings and moves the drag link.

why.en: Turns gearbox rotation into a push-pull motion.

recall_q.en: Arm fixed to the steering gearbox output shaft?

explain_simple.en: The arm hanging from the steering box.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Tie rod ends and drag link ends use ball joints so they can move in all directions.

why.en: Suspension movement and steering happen together.

recall_q.en: Joints used at tie rod ends?

explain_simple.en: Ball joints let the rods move freely.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Independent front suspension uses a divided (split) track rod with an idler arm or rack and pinion.

why.en: A single track rod would upset steering when one wheel moves.

recall_q.en: Why is the track rod split in independent suspension?

recall_a.en: So each wheel can move up and down without bump steer.

explain_simple.en: Two rods so each wheel moves on its own.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Steering gearbox reduces the effort needed and changes the direction of motion. Steering gear ratio is usually 12:1 to 24:1.

why.en: Many turns of the wheel give a small turn of the road wheels.

recall_q.en: Typical steering gear ratio range?

explain_simple.en: Turn more, push less.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Steering gearbox types: worm and sector, worm and roller, worm and nut, recirculating ball, cam and lever, rack and pinion.

why.en: PSC asks to list types.

recall_q.en: Name three steering gearbox types.

recall_a.en: Worm & sector, worm & roller, recirculating ball, rack & pinion.

explain_simple.en: Many shapes of gears do the same job.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Worm and sector: a worm on the column turns a toothed sector on the drop arm shaft.

why.en: Simple and strong, but has more friction.

recall_q.en: In worm and sector steering, what does the worm drive?

recall_a.en: A toothed sector (part of a gear).

explain_simple.en: A screw turns a slice of a gear.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Worm and roller: a roller on the sector shaft engages an hourglass worm, giving rolling contact and less friction.

why.en: Rolling instead of sliding.

recall_q.en: Advantage of worm and roller over worm and sector?

explain_simple.en: A roller instead of teeth slides easier.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Recirculating ball: steel balls roll between the worm and a nut; the nut moves a sector. Very low friction.

why.en: Balls recirculate through a return tube.

example.en: Used in trucks, buses and older SUVs.

recall_q.en: Steering gear in which balls run between worm and nut?

explain_simple.en: Rolling balls make steering light.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Rack and pinion: a pinion on the steering column moves a toothed rack sideways, which moves the tie rods.

why.en: Simple, light, direct and precise.

example.en: Used in almost all modern cars.

recall_q.en: Steering gear used in most modern cars?

explain_simple.en: Round gear moves a straight toothed bar.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Reversible steering: road shocks are felt at the steering wheel. Irreversible: road shocks are not passed back. Most are semi-reversible.

why.en: Some feedback helps self-centring and road feel.

recall_q.en: Steering that passes road shocks back to the wheel?

explain_simple.en: Some feel of the road is good.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Power steering uses hydraulic or electric power to reduce the driver's effort.

why.en: Heavy vehicles and wide tyres are hard to steer.

recall_q.en: Purpose of power steering?

explain_simple.en: A helper makes steering light.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Hydraulic power steering parts: engine-driven pump (vane type), reservoir, control valve, power cylinder, hoses.

why.en: Oil pressure pushes the piston to help the driver.

recall_q.en: Type of pump used in hydraulic power steering?

explain_simple.en: Engine pump pushes oil to help steer.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Integral power steering: control valve and power cylinder are built into the steering gearbox.

why.en: Compact; common in trucks with recirculating-ball boxes.

recall_q.en: Power steering with valve and cylinder inside the gearbox?

explain_simple.en: Everything inside the steering box.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Linkage type power steering: control valve and power cylinder are separate and act on the steering linkage.

why.en: Can be added to an existing manual system.

recall_q.en: Power steering with separate cylinder acting on linkage?

explain_simple.en: Helper cylinder pushes the linkage.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Electric power steering (EPS) uses an electric motor on the column or rack, controlled by a torque sensor and ECU.

why.en: Saves fuel; works only when steering.

recall_q.en: What senses driver effort in EPS?

explain_simple.en: Electric motor helps when you turn.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Power steering is fail-safe: if power fails, the driver can still steer manually with more effort.

why.en: Mechanical link stays connected.

recall_q.en: Can a car be steered if power steering fails?

recall_a.en: Yes, manually but with more effort.

explain_simple.en: Heavier, but still works.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Collapsible steering column collapses on impact to protect the driver's chest. Types: mesh/lattice, telescopic (sliding), shear capsule, convoluted tube.

why.en: Prevents the column spearing the driver in a crash.

recall_q.en: Purpose of a collapsible steering column?

recall_a.en: Collapse in a crash to protect the driver.

explain_simple.en: The column folds instead of hitting you.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Wheel alignment angles: camber, caster, kingpin inclination (KPI / SAI), toe-in/toe-out, toe-out on turns.

why.en: Correct angles give stability, light steering and less tyre wear.

recall_q.en: Name four wheel alignment factors.

explain_simple.en: Angles at which wheels are set.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Camber: tilt of the wheel inward or outward at the top, seen from the front. Positive camber: top tilts out.

why.en: Small camber spreads load and eases steering.

recall_q.en: Wheel top tilted outward is which camber?

explain_simple.en: Camber = wheel leaning in or out.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Excess camber causes tyre wear on one shoulder (positive camber wears the outer edge) and pulling to one side.

why.en: The tyre rides on its edge.

recall_q.en: Too much positive camber wears which edge of the tyre?

explain_simple.en: Leaning wheel wears one side.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Caster: backward tilt of the kingpin/steering axis seen from the side. Positive caster: top tilts towards the rear.

why.en: It gives directional stability and self-centring.

example.en: Like a shopping trolley wheel that trails behind its pivot.

recall_q.en: Which angle gives self-centring and directional stability?

explain_simple.en: Caster makes wheels want to go straight.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Too much caster makes steering heavy; too little makes the vehicle wander. Unequal caster makes it pull to one side.

why.en: Caster sets the self-aligning force.

recall_q.en: Effect of too much positive caster?

explain_simple.en: Too much = heavy. Too little = wandering.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Kingpin inclination (KPI / steering axis inclination): inward tilt of the kingpin at the top, seen from the front. Usually 7–8°.

why.en: Reduces steering effort and helps self-centring (the vehicle lifts slightly when wheels are turned).

recall_q.en: Purpose of kingpin inclination?

recall_a.en: Reduce steering effort and give self-centring.

explain_simple.en: Tilted pivot brings the wheels back straight.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Scrub radius (offset): distance on the road between the tyre centre and the point where the steering axis meets the ground.

why.en: KPI and camber reduce the scrub radius and steering effort.

recall_q.en: Distance at the road between tyre centre and steering axis?

explain_simple.en: How far the wheel sits from its pivot line.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Toe-in: front of wheels closer than the rear (seen from above). Toe-out: front further apart. Usually 2–4 mm toe-in for RWD.

why.en: Toe-in balances the wheels' tendency to splay out when rolling (positive camber, rolling resistance).

recall_q.en: Front of the wheels closer together than the rear is called?

explain_simple.en: Wheels pointing slightly inward.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Front-wheel-drive cars often have zero or slight toe-out.

why.en: Driving force pulls the front of the wheels inward.

recall_q.en: Do FWD cars usually have toe-in or slight toe-out?

explain_simple.en: Pulling wheels toe in by themselves.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Wrong toe causes feather-edge (saw-tooth) tyre wear.

why.en: Tyres scrub sideways as they roll.

recall_q.en: Feather-edge tyre wear indicates wrong what?

explain_simple.en: Saw-tooth wear = toe problem.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Toe-out on turns: on a turn the inner wheel turns more than the outer, giving toe-out. Provided by the Ackermann layout.

why.en: Needed for true rolling about a common centre.

recall_q.en: Toe-out on turns is achieved by?

explain_simple.en: On turns the wheels point slightly apart.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Factors affecting wheel alignment: worn kingpins, ball joints and tie rod ends, bent parts, sagging springs, wrong tyre pressure, accidents, potholes.

why.en: Any wear or bend changes the angles.

recall_q.en: Name two factors that disturb wheel alignment.

recall_a.en: Worn joints, bent parts, weak springs, accidents, tyre pressure.

explain_simple.en: Wear, bends and knocks spoil alignment.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Steering geometry faults: wheel wobble/shimmy, wander, pull to one side, hard steering, poor return after turns.

why.en: Each points to a different cause.

recall_q.en: Shaking of front wheels at speed is called?

explain_simple.en: Shaking steering wheel = shimmy.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Turning radius: radius of the circle traced by the outer front wheel at full lock. Smaller is more manoeuvrable.

why.en: Small cars have about 4.5–5 m.

recall_q.en: Turning radius is measured on which wheel?

recall_a.en: Outer front wheel at full lock.

explain_simple.en: How tight the vehicle can turn.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Over-steer: vehicle turns more than the driver wants (rear slides out). Under-steer: turns less (front pushes wide).

why.en: Caused by grip difference between front and rear tyres.

recall_q.en: Rear sliding out on a turn is called?

explain_simple.en: Over = too much turn. Under = not enough.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

points.en: True rolling: common centre; inner wheel turns more.
Ackermann (turning pairs, 3 exact positions) vs Davis (sliding pairs).
Gearboxes: worm & sector/roller, recirculating ball, rack & pinion.
Power steering: integral, linkage, EPS; collapsible column.
Camber, caster (self-centring), KPI, toe-in, toe-out on turns.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Brakes slow down or stop a vehicle by turning its kinetic energy into heat through friction.

why.en: Energy cannot vanish; it becomes heat.

recall_q.en: Brakes convert kinetic energy into what?

explain_simple.en: Brakes turn speed into heat.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Classification of brakes: by purpose (service, parking), by location (wheel, transmission), by construction (drum, disc), by actuation (mechanical, hydraulic, air, vacuum servo, electric).

why.en: PSC asks classification often.

recall_q.en: Name three types of brakes by method of actuation.

explain_simple.en: Brakes are worked by rods, oil, air or vacuum.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Service brake (foot brake) is used during driving. Parking brake (hand brake) holds the parked vehicle and is usually mechanical on rear wheels.

why.en: Parking brake must work without hydraulic pressure.

recall_q.en: Hand brake is usually which type?

explain_simple.en: Foot brake for driving, hand brake for parking.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Mechanical brakes use rods, cables and levers to push the brake shoes.

why.en: Simple, but uneven braking and more effort.

example.en: Bicycles, many two-wheelers and parking brakes.

recall_q.en: Main drawback of mechanical brakes?

explain_simple.en: Rods and cables, but hard to balance.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Drum brake: shoes press outward against a rotating drum (internal expanding).

why.en: The drum turns with the wheel; friction slows it.

recall_q.en: In a drum brake, what presses against the drum?

explain_simple.en: Shoes push out on the drum.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Internal expanding brake: shoes inside the drum expand outward. External contracting brake: a band outside the drum tightens around it.

why.en: Internal expanding is used on vehicle wheels; external contracting on some transmissions and winches.

recall_q.en: Which brake type is used in vehicle wheel drums?

explain_simple.en: Inside pushing out, or outside squeezing in.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Drum brake parts: back plate, two shoes with linings, wheel cylinder or cam, retracting springs, anchor pin, adjuster, drum.

why.en: Springs pull the shoes back when brakes are released.

recall_q.en: What pulls brake shoes back after releasing the brake?

explain_simple.en: Springs pull the shoes off the drum.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Leading shoe: drum rotation helps press it harder (self-energising). Trailing shoe: drum rotation pushes it away.

why.en: Friction drags the leading shoe into the drum.

recall_q.en: Which shoe is self-energising?

explain_simple.en: Leading shoe gets pulled in; trailing shoe is pushed away.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Brake shoes are made of pressed steel or cast iron, lined with friction material (riveted or bonded).

why.en: Linings wear and are replaced.

recall_q.en: How are brake linings fixed to shoes?

explain_simple.en: Friction lining glued or riveted to the shoe.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Brake lining materials: asbestos-free organic, semi-metallic, ceramic, sintered metal. Asbestos is banned due to health risk.

why.en: Asbestos dust causes lung disease.

recall_q.en: Why is asbestos no longer used in brake linings?

explain_simple.en: Asbestos dust is poisonous.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Brake fade: loss of braking when brakes get very hot from repeated use, for example on long downhill roads.

why.en: Hot linings lose friction; hot fluid may boil.

example.en: Coming down the Thamarassery ghat road using brakes continuously.

recall_q.en: Loss of brake power due to overheating is called?

explain_simple.en: Hot brakes grip less.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Use engine braking (lower gear) on long descents to avoid brake fade.

why.en: The engine holds speed, so brakes stay cool.

recall_q.en: How to avoid brake fade on a long downhill?

explain_simple.en: Let the engine slow you down.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Disc brake: a disc (rotor) turns with the wheel; a caliper squeezes friction pads on both sides of it.

why.en: Disc is open to air, so it cools fast.

recall_q.en: In a disc brake, what squeezes the pads?

explain_simple.en: Pads pinch a spinning disc.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Disc brake advantages: better cooling, less fade, self-cleaning (throws off water), easy pad change, even braking.

why.en: The disc is exposed to air.

recall_q.en: Main advantage of disc brakes over drum brakes?

explain_simple.en: Discs stay cool and work in rain.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Disc brakes are not self-energising, so they need more pedal force; a brake booster is usually fitted.

why.en: Pads press straight, without wedging.

recall_q.en: Are disc brakes self-energising?

explain_simple.en: Discs need a helper (booster).

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Caliper types: fixed caliper (pistons on both sides) and floating/sliding caliper (piston on one side; caliper slides).

why.en: Floating calipers are cheaper and common in cars.

recall_q.en: Caliper with piston on one side only that slides?

explain_simple.en: Fixed has pistons both sides; floating slides.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Ventilated discs have air passages between two faces for better cooling. Discs are made of grey cast iron.

why.en: More cooling surface.

recall_q.en: Material of brake discs?

explain_simple.en: Cast iron discs, sometimes with air vents.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Hydraulic brakes work on Pascal's law: pedal force builds pressure in the master cylinder, which is passed equally to all wheel cylinders.

why.en: Equal pressure gives equal braking.

recall_q.en: Hydraulic brakes work on which law?

explain_simple.en: Push oil at one end; every wheel gets the same push.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Hydraulic brake parts: brake pedal, master cylinder, reservoir, brake lines (pipes and hoses), wheel cylinders or calipers, brake fluid.

why.en: Fluid carries the force.

recall_q.en: Name the parts of a hydraulic brake system.

recall_a.en: Pedal, master cylinder, lines, wheel cylinders/calipers, fluid.

explain_simple.en: Pedal → master cylinder → pipes → wheels.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Master cylinder converts pedal force into hydraulic pressure. Parts: reservoir, piston, primary and secondary cups, return spring, check valve, compensating port, inlet port.

why.en: Pedal pushes the piston which pressurises fluid.

recall_q.en: Which component converts pedal force to hydraulic pressure?

explain_simple.en: Pedal pushes a piston to build pressure.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Compensating port lets fluid flow between reservoir and cylinder when brakes are off, making up for expansion, contraction and lining wear.

why.en: Keeps the system full with no trapped pressure.

recall_q.en: Purpose of the compensating port in master cylinder?

recall_a.en: Allow fluid to expand/return to reservoir; compensate wear.

explain_simple.en: A small hole that balances the fluid.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Check valve in a master cylinder keeps a small residual pressure in the lines (in drum systems).

why.en: Keeps wheel cylinder cups sealed and stops air entering.

recall_q.en: Why is residual pressure kept in brake lines?

recall_a.en: To keep cups sealed and prevent air entry.

explain_simple.en: A little pressure keeps air out.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Tandem master cylinder has two pistons one behind the other, feeding two separate circuits (dual circuit).

why.en: If one circuit leaks, the other still brakes the vehicle.

recall_q.en: Why is a tandem master cylinder used?

explain_simple.en: Two systems in one, so one can fail safely.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Dual circuit splits: front/rear (vertical split) or diagonal (each circuit has one front and the opposite rear wheel).

why.en: Diagonal split keeps balanced braking if one fails.

recall_q.en: Which dual circuit split gives one front and one opposite rear wheel per circuit?

explain_simple.en: Criss-cross split keeps the car straight.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Wheel cylinder: fluid pressure pushes its two pistons outward to expand the brake shoes against the drum.

why.en: It converts hydraulic pressure back to force.

recall_q.en: Function of a wheel cylinder?

recall_a.en: Push brake shoes outward using fluid pressure.

explain_simple.en: Oil pushes small pistons that spread the shoes.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Wheel cylinder types: double-piston (both shoes), single-piston (one shoe), stepped (different piston sizes).

why.en: Stepped cylinders give more force to the leading shoe.

recall_q.en: Wheel cylinder with different piston diameters is called?

explain_simple.en: Bigger piston pushes harder.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Brake bleeding removes air from hydraulic brake lines.

why.en: Air compresses, giving a soft, spongy pedal.

recall_q.en: Why are brakes bled?

recall_a.en: To remove air from the system.

explain_simple.en: Push out air bubbles from the brake pipes.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Bleeding is done at each wheel's bleed screw, usually starting from the wheel farthest from the master cylinder.

why.en: Air is pushed out of the longest line first.

recall_q.en: Bleeding usually starts from which wheel?

recall_a.en: The one farthest from the master cylinder.

explain_simple.en: Start far, finish near.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Spongy pedal: air in the lines. Pedal goes to floor slowly: leaking cups. Hard pedal: booster failure.

why.en: Each symptom points to a cause.

recall_q.en: Spongy brake pedal indicates?

explain_simple.en: Soft pedal = air inside.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Servo (power-assisted) brake uses an outside power source to add to the driver's pedal force.

why.en: Reduces driver effort.

recall_q.en: What is a servo brake?

recall_a.en: Brake assisted by vacuum, air or hydraulic power.

explain_simple.en: A helper multiplies pedal force.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Servo brake types: vacuum servo (most cars), air servo, hydraulic servo, mechanical self-servo (leading shoe).

why.en: Vacuum is freely available from petrol engines.

recall_q.en: Most common servo in cars?

explain_simple.en: Engine vacuum helps push.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Vacuum booster: a large diaphragm with engine vacuum on both sides. Pressing the pedal lets air into one side; the pressure difference pushes the master cylinder.

why.en: Atmospheric pressure on a big area gives a big force.

recall_q.en: Working of a vacuum booster in one line?

recall_a.en: Air on one side, vacuum on the other pushes the diaphragm to help the pedal.

explain_simple.en: Air pushes a big diaphragm toward the vacuum.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Diesel engines have little manifold vacuum, so they use an engine-driven vacuum pump (exhauster) for the booster.

why.en: Diesel engines run without a throttle.

recall_q.en: How do diesel cars get vacuum for the brake booster?

explain_simple.en: A pump makes the vacuum.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Suspended vacuum type: vacuum on both sides of the diaphragm at rest. Atmospheric suspended: air on both sides at rest. Most boosters are vacuum-suspended.

why.en: Vacuum-suspended reacts faster.

recall_q.en: Most boosters are which type?

explain_simple.en: Vacuum waits on both sides.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Air (pneumatic) brakes use compressed air to apply the brakes. Used in heavy vehicles like trucks and buses.

why.en: Gives large braking force with little pedal effort.

recall_q.en: Which vehicles use air brakes?

explain_simple.en: Big vehicles brake with air.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Air brake parts: compressor, governor/unloader, air dryer, reservoir (tanks), foot (brake) valve, brake chambers, slack adjusters, S-cam, relay and quick release valves, pressure gauge.

why.en: Each stores, controls or applies air.

recall_q.en: Valve operated by the driver's foot in an air brake system?

explain_simple.en: Compressor fills tanks; foot valve sends air to wheels.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Air brake working: compressor fills reservoirs (about 7–8 bar). Pressing the foot valve sends air to brake chambers, whose push rods turn the slack adjuster and S-cam, spreading the shoes.

why.en: Air pressure becomes a mechanical push.

recall_q.en: In an air brake, what spreads the brake shoes?

explain_simple.en: Air pushes a rod that twists a cam.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Brake chamber converts air pressure into mechanical force using a diaphragm and push rod.

why.en: It is the 'muscle' at each wheel.

recall_q.en: Part that converts air pressure into push-rod force?

explain_simple.en: Air bag that pushes a rod.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Slack adjuster joins the brake chamber push rod to the S-cam shaft and adjusts for lining wear.

why.en: Keeps the shoe-to-drum clearance correct.

recall_q.en: Function of slack adjuster?

recall_a.en: Link push rod to cam and adjust for lining wear.

explain_simple.en: Keeps brakes adjusted as linings wear.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Quick release valve lets air out of the brake chambers quickly when brakes are released. Relay valve applies air quickly to far-away chambers.

why.en: Long pipes would slow down action.

recall_q.en: Valve that speeds up brake release in air brakes?

explain_simple.en: Lets air out fast.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Spring brakes (parking/emergency) in heavy vehicles: strong springs apply the brakes, and air pressure holds them off.

why.en: If air is lost, brakes come on automatically (fail-safe).

recall_q.en: In spring brakes, what applies the brake?

explain_simple.en: No air = brakes on.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Low air pressure warning (buzzer/light) tells the driver when tank pressure falls below safe level (about 4–5 bar).

why.en: Driving with low air is dangerous.

recall_q.en: What warns the driver of low air brake pressure?

explain_simple.en: An alarm when air is low.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Air dryer and drain cocks remove moisture from compressed air.

why.en: Water in air lines can freeze or rust valves.

recall_q.en: Why are air tanks drained daily?

explain_simple.en: Drain water from air tanks.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Air brakes: advantages—large force, unlimited air, no fluid leaks dangerous, trailer brakes easy. Disadvantages—costly, compressor needed, slower response.

why.en: Trade-offs suited to heavy vehicles.

recall_q.en: Give one advantage of air brakes.

recall_a.en: Large braking force with little effort; easy trailer coupling.

explain_simple.en: Strong and easy for big vehicles.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Air-over-hydraulic brakes: air pressure works a hydraulic master cylinder (booster) for each circuit. Used in medium trucks.

why.en: Combines air force with hydraulic precision.

recall_q.en: Brake system using air to operate hydraulic master cylinders?

explain_simple.en: Air helps oil brakes.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Exhaust brake (retarder) closes the exhaust pipe with a valve so the engine slows the vehicle. Electric (eddy current) retarders are also used in buses.

why.en: Saves service brakes on long descents.

recall_q.en: Device that slows a truck by blocking the exhaust?

explain_simple.en: Choke the exhaust to slow down.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Brake efficiency is tested on a roller brake tester or by a decelerometer. Efficiency = (retardation / g) × 100.

why.en: MVD tests brakes during fitness certification.

recall_q.en: Formula for brake efficiency?

explain_simple.en: Deceleration compared with g.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Stopping distance = reaction distance + braking distance. Braking distance = v² / (2μg).

why.en: Double the speed gives four times braking distance.

recall_q.en: If speed doubles, braking distance becomes?

explain_simple.en: Twice as fast needs four times the room to stop.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Weight transfer during braking loads the front wheels more, so front brakes are made stronger (often discs).

why.en: The vehicle pitches forward.

recall_q.en: Why are front brakes made stronger?

recall_a.en: Weight shifts to the front under braking.

explain_simple.en: Front wheels carry more load when braking.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Proportioning (load-sensing) valve reduces pressure to rear brakes to prevent rear wheel lock-up.

why.en: Rear wheels lose load under braking and can lock.

recall_q.en: Valve that prevents rear wheel lock?

explain_simple.en: Less pressure for the lighter rear.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

text.en: Question: A car at 20 m/s brakes with μ = 0.5. Find braking distance (g = 10 m/s²).

explain.en: At 40 m/s it would be 160 m — four times.

recall_q.en: Braking distance at 20 m/s with μ = 0.5?

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Drum (internal expanding, leading shoe self-energising) vs disc (cooler, less fade).
Hydraulic brakes: Pascal's law, tandem master cylinder, bleeding removes air.
Vacuum servo booster; diesel uses exhauster pump.
Air brakes: compressor, foot valve, brake chamber, slack adjuster, S-cam.
Spring brakes fail-safe; braking distance ∝ v².

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A clutch connects and disconnects the engine from the gearbox.

why.en: We must disconnect the engine to start, stop and change gears smoothly.

recall_q.en: Main function of a clutch?

recall_a.en: Engage and disengage engine power to the gearbox.

explain_simple.en: It joins and separates engine and gearbox.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Friction clutch principle: two friction surfaces pressed together by springs turn together; separated, they turn freely.

why.en: Friction passes the torque.

recall_q.en: Principle of a friction clutch?

recall_a.en: Friction between surfaces pressed together transmits torque.

explain_simple.en: Pressed plates grip and turn together.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Torque transmitted by a clutch T = μ W R n (μ friction coefficient, W spring force, R mean radius, n number of friction faces).

why.en: More pressure, more radius or more faces give more torque.

recall_q.en: Factors affecting clutch torque capacity?

recall_a.en: μ, spring force, mean radius, number of friction surfaces.

explain_simple.en: Grip × push × size × faces.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Requirements of a clutch: smooth engagement, quick disengagement, enough torque capacity, good heat dissipation, low inertia of driven parts, light pedal.

why.en: Each makes gear changes easy and long-lasting.

recall_q.en: Why should the clutch plate have low inertia?

recall_a.en: So it stops quickly for easy gear changes.

explain_simple.en: Light plate stops fast.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Single plate dry clutch parts: flywheel, clutch (friction) plate, pressure plate, clutch springs, cover, release levers, release (thrust) bearing, clutch shaft.

why.en: The friction plate is clamped between flywheel and pressure plate.

recall_q.en: The clutch plate is clamped between which two parts?

explain_simple.en: The plate is a sandwich filling.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Clutch plate is splined to the gearbox input (clutch) shaft, so it can slide but must turn with it.

why.en: It slides to engage and disengage.

recall_q.en: How is the clutch plate fixed to the clutch shaft?

explain_simple.en: Grooves let it slide but not spin alone.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Clutch plate has friction linings on both sides, torsional (damper) springs in the hub and cushion springs (wavy segments) between the linings.

why.en: Damper springs absorb shocks; cushion springs give smooth take-up.

recall_q.en: Purpose of torsional springs in the clutch plate hub?

explain_simple.en: Little springs cushion jerks.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: When the pedal is pressed, the release bearing pushes the levers (or diaphragm fingers), pulling the pressure plate back so the clutch plate is free.

why.en: Spring force is removed from the plate.

recall_q.en: What happens when the clutch pedal is pressed?

recall_a.en: Pressure plate moves back; clutch disengages.

explain_simple.en: Pedal down = plates apart.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Coil spring clutch uses several coil springs around the pressure plate.

why.en: Older design; springs weaken at high speed due to centrifugal force.

recall_q.en: Clutch using several coil springs around the pressure plate?

explain_simple.en: Many springs push the plate.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Diaphragm clutch uses one dish-shaped steel diaphragm spring instead of coil springs. Its fingers act as release levers.

why.en: Lighter, fewer parts, even pressure, lower pedal effort.

recall_q.en: What replaces coil springs in a diaphragm clutch?

explain_simple.en: One dish-shaped spring does it all.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Diaphragm clutch advantages: compact, balanced, less pedal effort, pressure does not drop much as lining wears, not affected by centrifugal force.

why.en: It is used in almost all modern cars.

recall_q.en: Clutch used in most modern cars?

explain_simple.en: Simple and light to press.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Multi-plate clutch has several driving and driven plates stacked together.

why.en: More friction faces give more torque in a small diameter.

example.en: Motorcycles, scooters with gears, heavy vehicles and automatic gearboxes.

recall_q.en: Why is a multi-plate clutch used in motorcycles?

explain_simple.en: Many small plates instead of one big one.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Wet clutch runs in oil; dry clutch runs without oil. Motorcycle multi-plate clutches are usually wet.

why.en: Oil cools and smooths engagement, but lowers friction (more plates needed).

recall_q.en: Do most motorcycle clutches run wet or dry?

explain_simple.en: Wet clutch sits in oil.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Cone clutch: friction surfaces are cone-shaped. The wedge action gives high torque for little spring force.

why.en: Pressure on a cone multiplies normal force.

recall_q.en: Clutch with conical friction surfaces?

explain_simple.en: A cone pushed into a cup.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Cone clutch drawbacks: tends to stick (grab) and is hard to disengage; used now mostly in synchromesh units.

why.en: Small cone angle makes it jam.

recall_q.en: Where is the cone clutch principle used today?

explain_simple.en: Cone clutches live inside synchros.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Centrifugal clutch engages automatically as engine speed rises: weights fly out and press the shoes on a drum.

why.en: No clutch pedal needed.

example.en: Gearless scooters, mopeds, chain saws.

recall_q.en: Which clutch engages automatically with engine speed?

explain_simple.en: Spin faster and it grips by itself.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Semi-centrifugal clutch uses both springs and centrifugal weights. Springs carry normal torque; weights add pressure at high speed.

why.en: Lighter springs give a lighter pedal at low speed.

recall_q.en: Clutch using both springs and centrifugal force?

explain_simple.en: Springs plus flying weights.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Vacuum clutch uses engine manifold vacuum to operate the clutch through a vacuum cylinder, often triggered by a switch on the gear lever.

why.en: No clutch pedal effort for the driver.

recall_q.en: What power operates a vacuum clutch?

explain_simple.en: Vacuum pulls the clutch apart.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Hydraulic clutch uses a master cylinder at the pedal and a slave cylinder at the clutch to operate the release fork.

why.en: Smooth, self-adjusting and easy to route.

recall_q.en: Two cylinders in a hydraulic clutch?

explain_simple.en: Oil carries pedal push to the clutch.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Electromagnetic clutch: an electromagnet pulls the plates together when current flows.

why.en: Can be switched electrically.

example.en: Car AC compressor clutch.

recall_q.en: Where is an electromagnetic clutch used in a car?

explain_simple.en: Electric magnet grabs the plate.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Fluid flywheel (fluid coupling): a driving impeller (pump) and a driven turbine (runner) face each other in oil. Oil thrown by the pump drives the turbine.

why.en: Power passes through oil with no mechanical contact.

recall_q.en: Two main members of a fluid flywheel?

explain_simple.en: One fan throws oil to spin another.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Fluid coupling cannot multiply torque. Output torque = input torque; there is always some slip (about 2%).

why.en: There is no reaction member (stator).

recall_q.en: Can a fluid coupling increase torque?

explain_simple.en: Same torque out, a little slip.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Fluid flywheel advantages: smooth start, no wear, absorbs shocks, engine does not stall when vehicle stops.

why.en: Slip at idle lets the engine keep running.

recall_q.en: Advantage of a fluid flywheel?

recall_a.en: Smooth take-up, no wear, shock absorption.

explain_simple.en: Smooth and never wears out.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Clutch linings: organic (non-asbestos), ceramic, sintered metal (cerametallic), Kevlar.

why.en: Need high friction, heat and wear resistance.

recall_q.en: Name one clutch lining material.

explain_simple.en: Grippy, heat-proof material.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Clutch pedal free play: small pedal movement before the release bearing touches the levers (about 20–25 mm).

why.en: Without it, the clutch slips and the bearing wears.

recall_q.en: Effect of no clutch pedal free play?

recall_a.en: Clutch slip and release bearing wear.

explain_simple.en: A little slack keeps the clutch fully engaged.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Clutch slip: engine speed rises but vehicle does not speed up. Causes: worn or oily linings, weak springs, no free play.

why.en: Not enough grip.

recall_q.en: Engine revs rise without vehicle speeding up — what is the fault?

explain_simple.en: Engine roars, car does not go.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Clutch drag: clutch does not fully disengage, so gears grind. Causes: too much free play, warped plate, air in hydraulic clutch.

why.en: Plate keeps spinning.

recall_q.en: Gears grind when changing even with clutch pressed — what fault?

explain_simple.en: Clutch never fully lets go.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Clutch judder (grabbing): jerky take-up. Causes: oily or glazed linings, worn mountings, warped plates.

why.en: Grip comes on unevenly.

recall_q.en: Jerky clutch take-up is called?

explain_simple.en: Shaky start = judder.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Friction clutch: T = μWRn.
Single plate (coil springs), diaphragm (cars), multi-plate wet (bikes).
Cone, centrifugal (scooters), semi-centrifugal, vacuum, hydraulic, electromagnetic (AC).
Fluid flywheel: impeller + turbine, no torque multiplication.
Faults: slip, drag, judder; keep pedal free play.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A gearbox (transmission) changes the torque and speed from the engine to suit the road, and gives reverse and neutral.

why.en: Engine torque is limited; starting and climbing need more.

recall_q.en: Why is a gearbox needed?

recall_a.en: Vary torque and speed, give reverse and neutral.

explain_simple.en: Low gear for pulling, high gear for speed.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Resistances to vehicle motion: rolling resistance, air resistance, gradient resistance.

why.en: Total resistance changes, so the needed torque changes.

recall_q.en: Three resistances acting on a moving vehicle?

explain_simple.en: Road, wind and hill.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Air resistance increases with the square of speed.

why.en: Faster air hits harder and more often.

recall_q.en: Air resistance varies with speed how?

explain_simple.en: Twice as fast = four times wind drag.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Low gear: high torque, low speed. High gear: low torque, high speed. Top gear is often direct (1:1); overdrive is less than 1:1.

why.en: Gear ratio trades speed for torque.

recall_q.en: Gear ratio of an overdrive?

explain_simple.en: Overdrive spins the output faster than the engine.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Gearbox types: sliding mesh, constant mesh, synchromesh, epicyclic, automatic, CVT.

why.en: Each improved ease of shifting.

recall_q.en: Name three types of manual gearbox.

explain_simple.en: Old to new: sliding, constant, synchro.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Sliding mesh gearbox: gears on the main shaft slide along splines to mesh with gears on the countershaft (lay shaft).

why.en: Simplest design.

recall_q.en: In which gearbox do the gears themselves slide to mesh?

explain_simple.en: Gears move to bite each other.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Sliding mesh gearboxes use spur gears and need double de-clutching to change gears quietly.

why.en: Gear speeds must match before meshing.

recall_q.en: Shifting technique needed in a sliding mesh gearbox?

explain_simple.en: Clutch twice to match speeds.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Gearbox shafts: primary (input/clutch) shaft, lay shaft (countershaft), main (output) shaft, reverse idler shaft.

why.en: Lay shaft is driven by the input and drives main shaft gears.

recall_q.en: Shaft parallel to the main shaft carrying cluster gears?

explain_simple.en: Input → lay shaft → output.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Reverse gear uses an idler gear between lay shaft and main shaft to reverse direction.

why.en: An extra gear flips rotation.

recall_q.en: What gives reverse in a manual gearbox?

explain_simple.en: One extra gear makes it go backward.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Constant mesh gearbox: all gears are always in mesh. Main shaft gears spin freely; dog clutches lock the selected gear to the shaft.

why.en: Teeth are not damaged during shifting, and helical gears can be used.

recall_q.en: In a constant mesh gearbox, what locks the gear to the shaft?

explain_simple.en: Gears always mesh; a dog clutch picks one.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Constant mesh gearboxes are quieter and allow helical gears, but still need double de-clutching.

why.en: Dog clutches have no speed-matching.

recall_q.en: Advantage of constant mesh over sliding mesh?

recall_a.en: Quieter, helical gears, less tooth damage.

explain_simple.en: Quieter, but still not easy shifting.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Synchromesh gearbox: like constant mesh, but has synchronisers (cone clutches) that match gear speeds before the dog teeth engage.

why.en: No double de-clutching; quiet, easy shifts.

recall_q.en: Device that equalises gear speeds before engagement?

explain_simple.en: A small cone clutch matches speeds first.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Synchroniser types: constant load (pin type) and inertia lock (baulk ring type). Baulk ring is common.

why.en: Baulk ring prevents engagement until speeds are equal.

recall_q.en: Most common synchroniser type?

explain_simple.en: Baulk ring blocks until speeds match.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Synchromesh is used in all modern manual cars. Reverse gear is often not synchronised.

why.en: Reverse is engaged only when stopped.

recall_q.en: Which gear often has no synchromesh?

explain_simple.en: Stop fully before selecting reverse.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Progressive gearbox: gears must be changed in order (1-2-3-4), one after another, as in motorcycles.

why.en: A rotating drum selects gears in sequence.

example.en: Motorcycles: one down, rest up (1-N-2-3-4-5).

recall_q.en: Gearbox where gears are changed one after another in sequence?

explain_simple.en: Step by step, no skipping.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Selective gearbox: any gear can be selected directly from neutral (H-pattern in cars).

why.en: Gear lever moves in a gate.

recall_q.en: Car gearboxes with H-pattern are which type?

explain_simple.en: Pick any gear directly.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Epicyclic gearbox: uses planetary gear sets (sun, planets, carrier, annulus). Holding one member with a brake band or clutch gives different ratios.

why.en: Gears always in mesh; shifting without breaking power.

example.en: Wilson pre-selector gearbox; automatic transmissions.

recall_q.en: How are ratios obtained in an epicyclic gearbox?

recall_a.en: By holding one member (sun, carrier or annulus) with brakes/clutches.

explain_simple.en: Lock one part, the others give a new ratio.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: In a planetary set: hold annulus, drive sun → reduction (low gear). Lock any two members → direct drive. Hold carrier → reverse.

why.en: These rules give all basic ratios.

recall_q.en: Holding the planet carrier in an epicyclic set gives?

explain_simple.en: Carrier held = reverse; two locked = direct.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Torque converter: like a fluid coupling with a third member, the stator (reactor), which multiplies torque (up to about 2–2.5 times) at low speed.

why.en: The stator redirects oil back to the impeller to add push.

recall_q.en: Which member of a torque converter multiplies torque?

explain_simple.en: A fluid coupling plus a stator.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Torque converter members: impeller (pump, connected to engine), turbine (connected to gearbox), stator (on a one-way clutch).

why.en: The one-way clutch lets the stator freewheel at coupling speed.

recall_q.en: On what is the stator mounted?

explain_simple.en: The stator only locks one way.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Coupling point: speed at which the turbine almost matches the impeller and the stator starts to freewheel. Converter then acts as a fluid coupling.

why.en: Torque multiplication ends there.

recall_q.en: Point where torque converter starts acting as a fluid coupling?

explain_simple.en: When torque boost ends.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Lock-up clutch in modern torque converters mechanically joins impeller and turbine at cruising speed.

why.en: Removes slip and saves fuel.

recall_q.en: Why is a lock-up clutch fitted in a torque converter?

explain_simple.en: Lock it solid when cruising.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Fluid coupling vs torque converter: coupling has 2 members and no torque multiplication; converter has 3 members (with stator) and multiplies torque.

why.en: Common comparison question.

recall_q.en: How many elements in a basic torque converter?

explain_simple.en: Two for coupling, three for converter.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Automatic transmission (AT): torque converter + epicyclic gear sets + hydraulic/electronic controls that shift gears without driver action.

why.en: Driver only selects P, R, N, D.

recall_q.en: Main parts of a conventional automatic transmission?

recall_a.en: Torque converter, planetary gear sets, hydraulic/electronic control.

explain_simple.en: Converter plus planet gears, shifted by computer.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Automatic selector positions: P (park — locks output), R (reverse), N (neutral), D (drive), L/2 (low).

why.en: P uses a parking pawl to lock the gearbox.

recall_q.en: What locks the output shaft in Park?

explain_simple.en: P locks the wheels through the gearbox.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Engine can be started only in P or N in automatics (neutral safety switch).

why.en: Prevents the car moving on starting.

recall_q.en: In which positions can an automatic car be started?

explain_simple.en: Start only in Park or Neutral.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: AMT (automated manual transmission): a normal manual gearbox where an ECU and actuators work the clutch and gear shifts.

why.en: Cheap automatic used in many Indian small cars.

recall_q.en: Gearbox that is a manual box with automatic clutch and shift actuators?

explain_simple.en: A manual box shifted by a robot.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: DCT (dual clutch transmission): two clutches, one for odd and one for even gears, giving very fast shifts.

why.en: Next gear is pre-selected on the other shaft.

recall_q.en: In DCT, why are there two clutches?

recall_a.en: One for odd gears, one for even gears, for fast shifts.

explain_simple.en: Next gear is always ready.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: CVT (continuously variable transmission): gives endless ratios between limits using two variable-width pulleys and a belt or chain.

why.en: Engine can stay at its best speed.

example.en: Gearless scooters use a CVT with a rubber V-belt.

recall_q.en: What transmission do gearless scooters use?

explain_simple.en: Pulleys change size smoothly; no steps.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: In a scooter CVT, centrifugal rollers push the drive pulley halves together as speed rises, making the belt ride higher and the ratio taller.

why.en: Automatic change with speed.

recall_q.en: What changes the drive pulley size in a scooter CVT?

explain_simple.en: Spinning rollers push the pulley closed.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Two-wheeler transmissions: primary drive (engine to clutch, by gears or chain), gearbox (constant mesh, sequential), final drive (chain, belt or shaft).

why.en: Each stage reduces speed.

recall_q.en: Most common final drive in motorcycles?

explain_simple.en: Engine → gears → chain → wheel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Chain drive: cheap, efficient (about 98%), but needs lubrication and tension adjustment. Belt drive: quiet and clean. Shaft drive: little maintenance, heavier.

why.en: Each has trade-offs.

recall_q.en: Final drive needing regular tension adjustment?

explain_simple.en: Chains need oil and tightening.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Gear selector mechanism: gear lever moves selector rods (rails), which move selector forks that slide synchro sleeves or gears.

why.en: This transfers the driver's hand motion into the box.

recall_q.en: Part that slides the synchro sleeve?

explain_simple.en: Lever → rod → fork → sleeve.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Interlock mechanism prevents two gears from being engaged at the same time.
