why.en: Two gears at once would lock the gearbox.

recall_q.en: What stops two gears engaging together?

explain_simple.en: One gear at a time only.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Detent (locating) mechanism: spring-loaded balls in notches hold the selector rod in each gear position.

why.en: Prevents jumping out of gear.

recall_q.en: What holds the selected gear in position?

explain_simple.en: Spring balls click into place.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Jumping out of gear causes: worn detents, worn dog teeth or synchro, weak springs, misaligned engine mounts.

why.en: Gear is not held firmly.

recall_q.en: Name one cause of a gear slipping out.

recall_a.en: Worn detent spring/ball or worn dog teeth.

explain_simple.en: Worn locks let gears pop out.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Transfer case (4WD vehicles) splits power between front and rear axles and often gives a low range.

why.en: Extra grip and low ratio for off-road.

recall_q.en: Unit that sends drive to both axles in 4WD?

explain_simple.en: Shares power front and back.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

text.en: Question: First gear ratio is 3.5:1 and final drive is 4:1. Find overall ratio.
Overall ratio = gearbox ratio × final drive ratio.
Engine turns 14 times for one wheel turn; torque at wheel ≈ 14 × engine torque (ignoring losses).

summary.en: Torque multiplies by the same ratio.

recall_q.en: Gear 3.5:1 and final drive 4:1 give overall ratio?

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

title.en: Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics

points.en: Sliding mesh (double de-clutch) → constant mesh (dog clutch) → synchromesh (cone).
Progressive (bikes) vs selective (cars).
Epicyclic: sun, planets, carrier, annulus; hold carrier = reverse.
Torque converter = impeller + turbine + stator (torque ×2).
AT, AMT, DCT, CVT (scooters); interlock and detents.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Propeller shaft carries power from the gearbox to the rear axle (differential) in front-engine rear-drive vehicles.

why.en: Gearbox and axle are far apart.

recall_q.en: Shaft connecting gearbox to differential?

explain_simple.en: The long shaft under the vehicle.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Propeller shaft is a hollow steel tube, balanced to avoid vibration. Long shafts are made in two parts with a centre bearing.

why.en: Hollow gives strength with less weight; long shafts whirl.

recall_q.en: Why are long propeller shafts split with a centre bearing?

explain_simple.en: Two short shafts shake less than one long one.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Slip joint (sliding spline joint) lets the propeller shaft change length as the rear axle moves up and down.

why.en: Axle movement changes the distance to the gearbox.

recall_q.en: What allows change in propeller shaft length?

explain_simple.en: A sliding spline lets the shaft stretch.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Universal joint (Hooke's joint) allows the shaft to drive at an angle that keeps changing.

why.en: Gearbox and axle are not in line, and the axle moves.

recall_q.en: What joint allows a shaft to transmit power at an angle?

explain_simple.en: A cross-shaped joint lets the shaft bend.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Hooke's joint parts: two yokes and a cross (spider) with needle roller bearings.

why.en: The cross lets the yokes swing in two planes.

recall_q.en: Central part of a Hooke's joint?

explain_simple.en: Two forks joined by a cross.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A single Hooke's joint at an angle does not give constant speed: the output speeds up and slows down twice per turn.

why.en: Geometry of the cross causes speed fluctuation.

recall_q.en: Does a single Hooke's joint give uniform output speed?

explain_simple.en: It wobbles in speed at an angle.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Using two Hooke's joints with yokes in the same plane and equal angles cancels the speed variation.

why.en: The second joint undoes the first joint's error.

recall_q.en: How is speed fluctuation of Hooke's joint cancelled?

recall_a.en: Two joints in phase with equal angles.

explain_simple.en: Two joints balance each other.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Other universal joints: flexible (rubber) joint, cross-type, ring-type.

why.en: Flexible joints suit small angles and absorb vibration.

recall_q.en: Joint with rubber discs for small angles?

explain_simple.en: A rubber coupling that bends a little.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Constant velocity (CV) joint gives the same output speed as input at any angle.

why.en: Front wheels steer and move, so large angles occur.

recall_q.en: Which joint is used at front-wheel-drive axles?

explain_simple.en: A joint that keeps speed steady at big angles.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: CV joint types: Rzeppa (ball type, outer wheel end), tripod (inner, plunging), Bendix-Weiss, Tracta, double Cardan.

why.en: Rzeppa allows large steering angles.

recall_q.en: Ball-type CV joint used at the wheel end?

explain_simple.en: Rzeppa has balls in grooves.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: CV joints are covered by rubber boots filled with grease. A torn boot lets dirt in and the joint fails (clicking on turns).

why.en: Dirt and lost grease ruin the joint.

recall_q.en: Clicking noise on sharp turns in a FWD car suggests?

explain_simple.en: Click on turns = CV joint.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Hotchkiss drive: the leaf springs carry the driving thrust and torque reaction from the axle to the frame. Uses an open propeller shaft with two UJs and a slip joint.

why.en: Simple; common in trucks and buses.

recall_q.en: In Hotchkiss drive, what takes the driving thrust?

explain_simple.en: Springs push the vehicle along.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Torque tube drive: the propeller shaft runs inside a rigid tube fixed to the axle. The tube takes torque reaction and drive thrust. Needs only one UJ and no slip joint.

why.en: The tube pivots at the gearbox end.

recall_q.en: Drive with one UJ and the shaft inside a tube?

explain_simple.en: Shaft in a tube that pushes the vehicle.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Torque tube drive allows coil springs, since springs need not carry thrust.

why.en: The tube does that job.

recall_q.en: Which drive allows coil springs to be used: Hotchkiss or torque tube?

explain_simple.en: Tube takes the push, so springs can be coils.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Torque reaction: when the propeller shaft drives the crown wheel, the axle casing tends to turn the opposite way.

why.en: Newton's third law.

recall_q.en: Tendency of axle casing to rotate opposite to wheels is called?

explain_simple.en: The axle tries to twist back.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Driving thrust: force from the driving wheels that pushes the vehicle forward, passed to the frame by springs or radius rods.

why.en: Wheels push on axle, axle pushes frame.

recall_q.en: Force that moves the vehicle forward from the axle is?

explain_simple.en: The push from the wheels.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Front wheel drive (FWD): engine, gearbox and differential in one unit (transaxle) driving front wheels through CV-jointed drive shafts.

why.en: No propeller shaft; more cabin space.

recall_q.en: Combined gearbox and differential in FWD cars is called?

explain_simple.en: Gearbox and diff together at the front.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: FWD advantages: more space, flat floor, good traction (engine weight on driving wheels), cheaper. Disadvantages: torque steer, heavier steering, more wear on front tyres.

why.en: Front wheels steer and drive.

recall_q.en: Give one advantage of FWD.

recall_a.en: More space / good traction / lower cost.

explain_simple.en: Roomy and grippy.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Final drive: crown wheel and pinion give a fixed speed reduction (about 3.5:1 to 6:1) and turn the drive by 90°.

why.en: Engine speed is too high for wheels.

recall_q.en: Two jobs of the final drive?

recall_a.en: Fixed speed reduction and turn drive through 90°.

explain_simple.en: Slow it down and turn the corner.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Differential lets the outer wheel turn faster than the inner wheel on a turn, while driving both.

why.en: The outer wheel covers a longer path.

recall_q.en: Why is a differential needed?

recall_a.en: Let driving wheels turn at different speeds on turns.

explain_simple.en: Outer wheel can spin faster on a bend.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Differential parts: pinion, crown wheel, differential cage (case), two sun (side) gears, two or four planet (star) pinions on a spider.

why.en: Planet pinions both drive and let side gears differ in speed.

recall_q.en: Gears connected to the axle half-shafts?

explain_simple.en: Crown wheel turns cage; planets turn side gears.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: On straight roads, planet pinions do not rotate on their own pins; the whole cage turns as one unit.

why.en: Both wheels need the same speed.

recall_q.en: Do planet pinions spin on their pins on a straight road?

explain_simple.en: On straight road, everything turns together.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Sum of the two wheel speeds = 2 × crown wheel (cage) speed. If one wheel stops, the other turns at twice cage speed.

why.en: Differential gear rule.

recall_q.en: One wheel is jacked up and spinning; the other is stopped. Speed of the spinning wheel?

explain_simple.en: One stops, the other goes double.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Drawback of a normal differential: if one wheel is on mud or ice, it spins and the other gets almost no torque.

why.en: Torque is shared equally, limited by the slipping wheel.

recall_q.en: Main drawback of an open differential?

recall_a.en: Loses traction if one wheel slips.

explain_simple.en: One wheel in mud spins; car does not move.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Limited slip differential (LSD) and differential lock reduce or stop wheel spin so the gripping wheel gets torque.

why.en: Useful for off-road and heavy vehicles.

recall_q.en: Device that prevents one wheel spinning freely?

explain_simple.en: It forces both wheels to help.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Rear axle types by support: semi-floating, three-quarter floating, fully floating.

why.en: They differ in which loads the half-shaft carries.

recall_q.en: Three types of rear axle by half-shaft support?

explain_simple.en: How much load the shaft carries.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Semi-floating axle: the half-shaft carries driving torque, bending and vehicle weight; bearing is between shaft and casing. Used in cars.

why.en: Simple and light.

recall_q.en: Rear axle type used in cars where shaft carries weight too?

explain_simple.en: Shaft does all the work.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Fully floating axle: the half-shaft carries only driving torque; wheel hub runs on two bearings on the axle casing. Used in trucks and buses.

why.en: Shaft can be removed without removing the wheel; vehicle can stand on it.

recall_q.en: Axle where half-shaft carries only torque?

explain_simple.en: Casing takes weight; shaft only turns.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Three-quarter floating: one bearing between hub and casing; shaft carries torque and side loads but not weight.

why.en: In-between design.

recall_q.en: Axle with a single bearing between hub and casing?

explain_simple.en: Middle option.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Axle casing types: banjo type (one-piece with central bulge) and split (carrier) type.

why.en: Banjo is common and easy to service.

recall_q.en: Axle casing with central bulge for the differential?

explain_simple.en: Shaped like a banjo.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Tandem axle: two rear axles close together on heavy trucks to share load. Lift axles can be raised when empty.

why.en: Spreads weight on roads.

recall_q.en: Two rear axles close together on a truck are called?

explain_simple.en: Two axles share the heavy load.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

title.en: Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles

points.en: Propeller shaft: hollow, slip joint, Hooke's joints (2 in phase).
CV joints (Rzeppa, tripod) for FWD; transaxle.
Hotchkiss (springs take thrust) vs torque tube (tube takes thrust, 1 UJ).
Differential: outer wheel faster; LSD stops wheel spin.
Semi-floating (cars), ¾, fully floating (trucks).

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Wheel types: spoked (wire) wheel, pressed steel disc wheel, light alloy cast wheel, composite wheel.

why.en: Each balances cost, weight and strength.

recall_q.en: Name the four types of wheels.

explain_simple.en: Wire, steel disc, alloy, composite.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Spoked wheel: hub joined to rim by tensioned wire spokes. Light and strong; used on bicycles and some motorcycles. Needs tubes.

why.en: Spoke holes in the rim stop it holding air.

recall_q.en: Why do spoked wheels usually need tubes?

recall_a.en: Spoke holes in the rim leak air.

explain_simple.en: Holes in the rim, so a tube is needed.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Pressed steel disc wheel: rim and disc pressed from steel and welded. Cheap, strong; used on most budget cars and trucks.

why.en: Easy mass production.

recall_q.en: Most common wheel on trucks and budget cars?

explain_simple.en: Cheap strong steel wheel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Alloy cast wheel (aluminium or magnesium alloy): light, good looking, better heat removal from brakes, reduces unsprung weight.

why.en: Lighter wheels improve ride and handling.

recall_q.en: Advantage of alloy wheels?

recall_a.en: Light, better cooling of brakes, looks.

explain_simple.en: Light and cool.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Composite wheel: made of materials like carbon fibre or a steel rim with alloy centre.

why.en: Very light and stiff.

recall_q.en: What is a composite wheel?

recall_a.en: Wheel made of combined materials like carbon fibre or steel/alloy.

explain_simple.en: Wheel built from mixed materials.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Rim types: drop centre (well base) rim for cars, flat base/divided rims for heavy vehicles.

why.en: The well lets the tyre bead drop in for fitting.

recall_q.en: Rim with a central well for fitting the tyre?

explain_simple.en: A dip in the middle to fit the tyre.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Tyre jobs: carry the vehicle weight, grip the road for driving, braking and steering, and absorb small road shocks.

why.en: The tyre is the only contact with the road.

recall_q.en: Give two functions of a tyre.

explain_simple.en: Hold, grip and cushion.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Tyre parts: tread, shoulder, sidewall, carcass (plies), bead (with steel wire), breaker/belt, inner liner.

why.en: Each layer has its own job.

recall_q.en: Part of the tyre that grips the rim?

explain_simple.en: The bead locks onto the rim.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Tread is the part touching the road; its pattern clears water and gives grip. Sidewall carries markings and flexes.

why.en: Grooves push water out to avoid aquaplaning.

recall_q.en: Part of a tyre in contact with the road?

explain_simple.en: The patterned rubber on the road.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Cross-ply (bias ply) tyre: cords run diagonally (about 30–40°) bead to bead, crossing each other in layers.

why.en: Stiff sidewalls; used in older vehicles and some heavy vehicles.

recall_q.en: Tyre in which plies cross diagonally?

explain_simple.en: Criss-cross layers.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Radial ply tyre: carcass cords run at 90° across from bead to bead, with steel or textile belts under the tread.

why.en: Flexible sidewalls and stiff tread.

recall_q.en: In a radial tyre, at what angle do the carcass cords run?

explain_simple.en: Cords run straight across.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Radial tyres: better grip, longer life, less rolling resistance (better fuel economy), cooler running. Cross-ply: cheaper, stronger sidewalls, harsher ride.

why.en: The tread stays flat on the road in radials.

recall_q.en: Which tyre gives better fuel economy: radial or cross-ply?

explain_simple.en: Radials last longer and save fuel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Belted bias tyre: cross-ply carcass with belts under the tread. Between cross-ply and radial.

why.en: A compromise design.

recall_q.en: Tyre with bias plies plus belts under the tread?

explain_simple.en: Cross-ply with belts.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Never mix radial and cross-ply tyres on the same axle.

why.en: Different handling causes instability.

recall_q.en: Can radial and cross-ply tyres be fitted on the same axle?

explain_simple.en: Same type on each axle.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Tubeless tyre: no inner tube; an airtight inner liner and tight bead seal hold air on a sealed rim with a valve fixed to the rim.

why.en: Air leaks slowly when punctured.

recall_q.en: What holds air in a tubeless tyre?

recall_a.en: Inner liner and bead seal against the rim.

explain_simple.en: Tyre and rim seal air themselves.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Tubeless advantages: slow air loss on puncture, cooler running, lighter, easy repair. Drawback: needs an airtight rim.

why.en: No tube to burst suddenly.

recall_q.en: Main safety advantage of tubeless tyres?

recall_a.en: Slow loss of air on puncture (no sudden burst).

explain_simple.en: Punctures leak slowly.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Tread patterns: rib (grooves around the tyre — steering wheels, good on highways), lug (cross bars — driving wheels, traction), rib-lug (mixed), block (off-road/snow), directional, asymmetric.

why.en: Pattern suits the job.

recall_q.en: Tread pattern for front steering wheels on highways?

explain_simple.en: Ribs for steering, lugs for pulling.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Minimum tread depth: 1.6 mm (tread wear indicators show this).

why.en: Below it, wet grip falls sharply.

recall_q.en: Legal minimum tyre tread depth?

explain_simple.en: Below 1.6 mm, change the tyre.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Aquaplaning: tyre rides on a film of water and loses contact with the road.

why.en: Tread cannot clear water fast enough at speed.

recall_q.en: Tyre riding on a water film is called?

explain_simple.en: Tyre surfing on water.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Under-inflation: both shoulders wear, tyre heats up, more fuel used, heavy steering, risk of burst.

why.en: Tyre flexes too much.

recall_q.en: Both edges of tread worn more than the centre means?

explain_simple.en: Low air wears the edges.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Over-inflation: centre of tread wears, less grip, hard ride, more damage from impacts.

why.en: Only the middle touches the road.

recall_q.en: Centre of tread worn more means?

explain_simple.en: Too much air wears the middle.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Check tyre pressure when cold, as given on the door label or manual.

why.en: Hot tyres show higher pressure.

recall_q.en: When should tyre pressure be checked?

explain_simple.en: Check before driving.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Nitrogen inflation: leaks more slowly and has no moisture, so pressure stays steadier.

why.en: Nitrogen molecules pass through rubber more slowly.

recall_q.en: Advantage of nitrogen in tyres?

explain_simple.en: Pressure stays right longer.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Factors affecting tyre life and performance: inflation pressure, load, speed, wheel alignment, wheel balance, road surface, driving habits, temperature, brakes.

why.en: Each adds heat or uneven wear.

recall_q.en: Name three factors that affect tyre performance.

recall_a.en: Pressure, load, speed, alignment, balance, road, driving.

explain_simple.en: Air, load, speed and alignment.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Wheel balancing: weights added to the rim so the wheel spins without vibration. Static and dynamic balance.

why.en: Unbalance causes shake and uneven wear.

recall_q.en: Purpose of wheel balancing?

recall_a.en: Prevent vibration and uneven tyre wear.

explain_simple.en: Small weights stop the wheel shaking.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Tyre rotation: moving tyres between positions at set intervals so they wear evenly.

why.en: Front and rear tyres wear differently.

recall_q.en: Why are tyres rotated?

explain_simple.en: Swap places to wear evenly.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Tyre size 195/65 R15 91H: 195 mm width, 65% aspect ratio, R = radial, 15-inch rim, 91 = load index, H = speed rating (210 km/h).

why.en: Read size code from the sidewall.

recall_q.en: In 195/65 R15, what is 65?

explain_simple.en: Width / height% / Radial / rim inches.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Aspect ratio = section height ÷ section width × 100. Low-profile tyres have low aspect ratio.

why.en: Lower sidewall gives sharper handling, harder ride.

recall_q.en: Formula for aspect ratio?

explain_simple.en: How tall the sidewall is compared to width.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: DOT/date code on the sidewall: last four digits show week and year of manufacture (e.g. 2324 = 23rd week of 2024).

why.en: Old tyres harden even if tread is good.

recall_q.en: In date code 2324, what is the year?

explain_simple.en: Week then year.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Retreading: putting new tread on a worn tyre casing. Common for trucks and buses. Retreaded tyres are not allowed on front wheels of buses.

why.en: Saves cost, but front tyres are safety critical.

recall_q.en: Process of adding new tread to a worn tyre?

explain_simple.en: New tread on old body.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Standing waves form in an under-inflated tyre at high speed, causing heat build-up and possible blowout.

why.en: The tyre cannot recover its shape fast enough.

recall_q.en: Wave-like deformation of tyre at high speed is called?

explain_simple.en: The tyre ripples and overheats.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: TPMS (tyre pressure monitoring system) warns the driver of low tyre pressure. Mandatory in new cars in India (M1 category) from 2022.

why.en: Low pressure is a big safety risk.

recall_q.en: What does TPMS do?

explain_simple.en: A dashboard warning for flat tyres.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Wheels: spoked, steel disc, alloy cast, composite.
Tyre parts: tread, sidewall, carcass, bead, belt.
Radial (90°, better economy) vs cross-ply (diagonal).
Rib for steering, lug for traction; min tread 1.6 mm.
Under-inflation wears edges, over-inflation centre; 195/65 R15 code.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: The charging system recharges the battery and supplies electricity to all loads when the engine runs.

why.en: The battery alone would soon go flat.

recall_q.en: Why is a charging system needed?

recall_a.en: Recharge battery and power loads while running.

explain_simple.en: It refills the battery.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Charging system parts: generator (dynamo or alternator), regulator, battery, ammeter or warning lamp, wiring.

why.en: Generator makes power; regulator controls it.

recall_q.en: Name the parts of the charging system.

explain_simple.en: Generator, controller, battery.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Dynamo (DC generator): armature rotates inside a stationary magnetic field; a commutator and brushes collect DC output.

why.en: The commutator converts AC in the armature to DC.

recall_q.en: In a dynamo, which part rotates?

explain_simple.en: Coils spin inside magnets.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Dynamo parts: yoke (frame), field poles and coils, armature, commutator, carbon brushes, end covers, pulley.

why.en: Commutator and brushes wear and need service.

recall_q.en: Part of a dynamo that converts AC to DC?

explain_simple.en: Commutator straightens the current.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Dynamos give little or no charge at idle and cannot run at high speed. They are heavy for their output.

why.en: Commutator sparks and armature fly apart at high rpm.

recall_q.en: Main drawback of a dynamo?

recall_a.en: No charging at idle; low output; cannot run fast.

explain_simple.en: Weak at idle, can't spin fast.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Alternator (AC generator): a rotor (field magnet) rotates inside a stationary stator (output windings). Diodes rectify AC to DC.

why.en: Output is taken from fixed windings, so no heavy commutator.

recall_q.en: In an alternator, which part rotates?

explain_simple.en: Magnet spins inside fixed coils.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Alternator parts: rotor (claw-pole field), stator (3-phase star or delta windings), slip rings and brushes (carry small field current), rectifier (diode pack), regulator, fan, pulley.

why.en: Slip rings carry only small field current, so brushes last long.

recall_q.en: What carries current to the alternator rotor?

explain_simple.en: Small current through slip rings.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Alternator uses 6 diodes (3-phase bridge rectifier) to change AC to DC. Diodes also stop battery current flowing back.

why.en: No cut-out relay needed.

recall_q.en: How many diodes in a basic alternator rectifier?

explain_simple.en: Six diodes change AC to DC.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Alternator advantages over dynamo: charges at idle, lighter, higher output, higher speed, less maintenance, no cut-out needed.

why.en: That is why all modern vehicles use alternators.

recall_q.en: Give two advantages of alternator over dynamo.

recall_a.en: Charges at idle, lighter, higher output, less maintenance.

explain_simple.en: Alternator: stronger, lighter, works at idle.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Never disconnect the battery while the alternator is running, and never reverse battery polarity.

why.en: Voltage spikes and reverse current destroy the diodes.

recall_q.en: Why must battery not be disconnected with engine running?

explain_simple.en: It can burn the alternator's diodes.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Regulator controls generator output voltage (about 13.8–14.4 V in a 12 V system) by controlling field current.

why.en: Too high overcharges and boils the battery; too low undercharges.

recall_q.en: Charging voltage in a 12 V system?

explain_simple.en: Regulator keeps voltage about 14 V.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Dynamo regulator has three units: cut-out (stops battery discharging into dynamo), voltage regulator, current regulator.

why.en: Dynamo needs all three.

recall_q.en: Purpose of the cut-out in a dynamo regulator?

recall_a.en: Prevent battery discharging through the dynamo.

explain_simple.en: A one-way switch for the dynamo.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Alternator needs only a voltage regulator. No cut-out (diodes block reverse flow) and no current regulator (stator limits current itself).

why.en: Self-limiting by stator reactance.

recall_q.en: Why does an alternator not need a current regulator?

recall_a.en: It limits its own current (stator reactance).

explain_simple.en: The alternator caps its own current.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Types of regulators: electromechanical (vibrating contact), electronic (transistor), integrated circuit (IC) built into the alternator, ECU-controlled.

why.en: Electronic types have no moving parts.

recall_q.en: Type of regulator in modern alternators?

explain_simple.en: A small chip inside the alternator.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Charging warning lamp glows with ignition on and engine off, and goes out when the alternator charges. If it stays on while running, charging has failed.

why.en: It shows the difference between battery and alternator voltage.

recall_q.en: Charging light stays on while driving — what does it mean?

explain_simple.en: Red battery light on = no charging.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Lead-acid battery: 12 V has 6 cells of about 2.1 V each. Electrolyte is dilute sulphuric acid.

why.en: Cells in series add voltage.

recall_q.en: How many cells in a 12 V lead-acid battery?

explain_simple.en: Six 2-volt cells make 12 V.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Specific gravity of battery acid: about 1.26–1.28 when fully charged, about 1.12 when discharged. Checked with a hydrometer.

why.en: Acid is used up during discharge.

recall_q.en: Instrument to check battery acid specific gravity?

explain_simple.en: Heavier acid = fuller battery.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Battery capacity is given in ampere-hours (Ah), e.g. 35 Ah.

why.en: Shows how much charge it can store.

recall_q.en: Unit of battery capacity?

explain_simple.en: How many amps for how many hours.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Battery plates: positive = lead peroxide (PbO₂), negative = spongy lead (Pb). Both change to lead sulphate on discharge.

why.en: Chemical change stores and releases energy.

recall_q.en: Material of positive plates in a lead-acid battery?

explain_simple.en: Brown lead peroxide (+), grey sponge lead (−).

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Sulphation: hard lead sulphate forms on plates if a battery stays discharged, reducing capacity.

why.en: Hard crystals do not convert back.

recall_q.en: Hardening of lead sulphate on idle battery plates is called?

explain_simple.en: A flat battery left long gets ruined.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Topping up a conventional battery is done with distilled water only, not acid.

why.en: Only water evaporates during charging.

recall_q.en: What is used to top up a battery?

explain_simple.en: Add pure water, not acid.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Maintenance-free (MF) batteries use calcium-lead grids, lose very little water and are sealed.

why.en: Calcium reduces gassing.

recall_q.en: Grid alloy in maintenance-free batteries?

explain_simple.en: Sealed and needs no water.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Negative earth system: battery negative is connected to the vehicle body. Almost all vehicles use negative earth.

why.en: Less corrosion and standard for electronics.

recall_q.en: Which battery terminal is earthed in most vehicles?

explain_simple.en: Minus goes to the body.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: When removing a battery, disconnect the negative (earth) terminal first; connect it last.

why.en: Avoids short circuit if the spanner touches the body.

recall_q.en: Which battery terminal is removed first?

explain_simple.en: Minus off first, minus on last.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Dynamo: armature rotates, commutator; no charge at idle.
Alternator: rotor rotates, stator fixed, 6 diodes rectify.
Dynamo regulator: cut-out + voltage + current; alternator: voltage only.
Charging voltage ~14 V; warning lamp on = not charging.
Battery 6 cells, SG 1.28 full; distilled water; negative earth.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Starter motor cranks the engine until it can run on its own.

why.en: An engine cannot start itself; it needs to be turned to begin the cycle.

recall_q.en: Function of a starter motor?

recall_a.en: Crank the engine to start it.

explain_simple.en: It spins the engine to start.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Starting system parts: battery, ignition/starter switch, solenoid (relay), starter motor, drive pinion, flywheel ring gear, heavy cables.

why.en: High current flows only through short, thick cables.

recall_q.en: Name the parts of a starting system.

recall_a.en: Battery, switch, solenoid, starter motor, pinion, ring gear.

explain_simple.en: Key → solenoid → motor → flywheel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Starter motor is a DC series-wound motor.

why.en: Series motors give very high torque at zero speed.

recall_q.en: Type of motor used as a starter?

explain_simple.en: Series motor = big starting torque.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Starter motor draws a very high current (about 150–400 A for cars, more for trucks).

why.en: Engine compression resists cranking.

recall_q.en: Why are starter cables thick?

explain_simple.en: Huge current needs fat wires.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Starter motor parts: yoke, field coils, armature, commutator, brushes, end frames, drive mechanism with pinion.

why.en: Similar to a dynamo but built for torque.

recall_q.en: Where does the brush rub in a starter motor?

explain_simple.en: Brushes feed current to the spinning armature.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Gear ratio between starter pinion and flywheel ring gear is about 10:1 to 20:1.

why.en: Gives high cranking torque from a small motor.

recall_q.en: Typical starter pinion to ring gear ratio?

explain_simple.en: Small gear turns big gear for torque.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Starter drive engages the pinion with the ring gear for cranking and disengages it once the engine starts.

why.en: A running engine would spin the starter too fast and wreck it.

recall_q.en: Why must the starter pinion disengage after starting?

recall_a.en: To avoid over-speeding the starter motor.

explain_simple.en: The engine would spin the starter to pieces.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Starter drive types: Bendix (inertia) drive (inboard and outboard), overrunning (roller) clutch drive, axial (sliding armature), pre-engaged drive.

why.en: Each engages and protects in a different way.

recall_q.en: Name four types of starter drives.

recall_a.en: Bendix, overrunning clutch, axial (sliding armature), pre-engaged.

explain_simple.en: Different ways to push the gear in.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Bendix drive: pinion sits on a screwed sleeve on the armature shaft. When the motor spins, the pinion's inertia makes it run along the thread into mesh.

why.en: Pinion is heavy on one side; it lags and screws forward.

recall_q.en: What makes the pinion move into mesh in a Bendix drive?

recall_a.en: Inertia of the pinion on a helical sleeve.

explain_simple.en: The pinion screws itself forward.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: When the engine starts, the ring gear spins the pinion faster, screwing it back out of mesh. A drive spring cushions the shock.

why.en: The thread works in reverse.

recall_q.en: How does a Bendix pinion disengage?

recall_a.en: Engine spins it faster and it screws back.

explain_simple.en: The engine throws the pinion back.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Inboard Bendix: pinion moves towards the motor to engage. Outboard Bendix: pinion moves away from the motor.

why.en: Depends on how the starter is mounted relative to the flywheel.

recall_q.en: In outboard Bendix drive, which way does the pinion move to engage?

explain_simple.en: Inboard moves in; outboard moves out.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Overrunning (roller) clutch drive: a one-way roller clutch lets the pinion freewheel if the engine drives it, protecting the armature.

why.en: Rollers lock one way and slip the other.

recall_q.en: What protects the armature in an overrunning clutch drive?

explain_simple.en: A one-way clutch lets the pinion spin free.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Pre-engaged starter: a solenoid first pushes the pinion into mesh using a shift lever, then closes the main contacts to spin the motor. Uses an overrunning clutch.

why.en: Pinion meshes before turning, so less gear wear.

recall_q.en: In a pre-engaged starter, what pushes the pinion into mesh?

explain_simple.en: Mesh first, spin second.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Pre-engaged starter is the most common in modern vehicles.

why.en: Smooth, positive engagement and long life.

recall_q.en: Most common starter drive in modern cars?

explain_simple.en: Modern cars use pre-engaged starters.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Axial (sliding armature) starter: the whole armature slides forward by magnetic force to mesh the pinion. Used in large diesel engines.

why.en: Gives full engagement before full power.

recall_q.en: Starter where the armature moves along its axis to engage?

explain_simple.en: The whole motor shaft slides forward.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Starter solenoid has a pull-in winding (moves plunger) and a hold-in winding (keeps it in).

why.en: Pull-in needs more current; hold-in saves current once engaged.

recall_q.en: Two windings in a starter solenoid?

explain_simple.en: One pulls, one holds.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Gear reduction starter has a small high-speed motor with internal reduction gears.

why.en: Lighter and draws less current for the same torque.

recall_q.en: Advantage of a gear reduction starter?

explain_simple.en: Small fast motor with gears inside.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Do not crank for more than about 10–15 seconds at a time.

why.en: Starter overheats and battery drains.

recall_q.en: Maximum cranking time at once?

explain_simple.en: Short tries only.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Starter only clicks: low battery, loose terminals, faulty solenoid contacts. Starter spins but engine does not turn: drive/pinion failure.

why.en: Symptoms point to the faulty part.

recall_q.en: Starter spins but engine does not crank — likely fault?

explain_simple.en: Spinning without cranking = drive problem.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Starter: DC series motor, high torque, 150–400 A.
Pinion : ring gear ≈ 15:1.
Bendix inertia drive (inboard/outboard).
Overrunning clutch; pre-engaged (solenoid + lever) most common.
Axial (sliding armature) for big diesels; crank ≤15 s.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Ignition system produces a high-voltage spark at the spark plug at the right moment to ignite the mixture in a petrol engine.

why.en: Petrol needs a spark to burn.

recall_q.en: Function of the ignition system?

recall_a.en: Produce a timed high-voltage spark at the plug.

explain_simple.en: It lights the fire at the right time.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Ignition types: battery (coil) ignition, magneto ignition, electronic ignition (transistorised, capacitor discharge), computer controlled, distributor-less (DLI).

why.en: From old mechanical to modern electronic.

recall_q.en: Name three types of ignition systems.

explain_simple.en: Coil, magneto, electronic.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Spark plug needs about 10,000–30,000 volts (modern systems up to 40,000 V).

why.en: Compressed mixture resists sparking.

recall_q.en: Voltage needed at the spark plug?

explain_simple.en: Very high voltage to jump the gap.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Coil ignition circuit: primary circuit (battery, switch, ballast resistor, primary winding, contact breaker, condenser) and secondary circuit (secondary winding, distributor, HT leads, plugs).

why.en: Low voltage primary creates high voltage secondary.

recall_q.en: Is the contact breaker in the primary or secondary circuit?

explain_simple.en: Low voltage side and high voltage side.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Ignition coil is a step-up transformer: primary has few turns of thick wire (about 200–300); secondary has many turns of thin wire (about 20,000).

why.en: Turns ratio steps voltage up.

recall_q.en: Which coil winding has more turns?

explain_simple.en: Many turns make high voltage.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: High voltage is induced when the primary current is suddenly broken and the magnetic field collapses.

why.en: Fast change in magnetic field induces high voltage (mutual induction).

recall_q.en: When is high voltage produced in the coil?

recall_a.en: When primary current is broken (field collapses).

explain_simple.en: Cut the current suddenly and a big spark comes.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Contact breaker (CB) points open and close the primary circuit, worked by a cam on the distributor shaft.

why.en: Opening the points triggers the spark.

recall_q.en: What opens the contact breaker points?

explain_simple.en: A cam flicks the points open.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: CB point gap is about 0.35–0.45 mm. Points are made of tungsten.

why.en: Tungsten resists arcing and wear.

recall_q.en: Material of contact breaker points?

explain_simple.en: Tough tungsten tips.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Cam angle (dwell angle): number of degrees of distributor cam rotation during which the points stay closed.

why.en: Longer dwell lets the coil build up full current.

recall_q.en: Define dwell angle.

recall_a.en: Cam angle during which CB points remain closed.

explain_simple.en: How long the points stay shut.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Larger point gap → smaller dwell angle. Smaller gap → larger dwell.

why.en: A wider gap means the points open earlier and close later.

recall_q.en: If point gap increases, what happens to dwell angle?

explain_simple.en: Wider gap, less closed time.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Condenser (capacitor) is connected across the CB points. It stops arcing at the points and makes the primary current collapse faster.

why.en: Faster collapse gives higher secondary voltage.

recall_q.en: Two functions of the condenser in coil ignition?

recall_a.en: Prevent arcing at points and speed up field collapse.

explain_simple.en: It saves the points and boosts the spark.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Faulty condenser: burnt, pitted points and weak spark.

why.en: Arcing eats the point surfaces.

recall_q.en: Burnt and pitted CB points suggest which fault?

explain_simple.en: Bad condenser burns the points.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Distributor sends high voltage to each spark plug in firing order, and houses the CB points, cam, condenser and advance mechanisms.

why.en: One coil serves all cylinders.

recall_q.en: Part that sends spark to each plug in order?

explain_simple.en: It shares sparks among cylinders.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Distributor rotor turns inside the cap and passes HT current to the cap's side terminals, one for each cylinder.

why.en: Rotor points to each plug lead in turn.

recall_q.en: Rotating arm inside the distributor cap is called?

explain_simple.en: A spinning pointer sends the spark.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Distributor runs at camshaft speed (half crankshaft speed) in four-stroke engines.

why.en: Each plug fires once every two crank turns.

recall_q.en: Speed of the distributor shaft?

explain_simple.en: Same speed as the camshaft.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Spark advance: the spark must come earlier at higher speed, because the burn takes nearly the same time but the piston moves faster.

why.en: Peak pressure should come just after TDC.

recall_q.en: Why must the spark be advanced at high speed?

recall_a.en: To give time for burning before piston passes TDC.

explain_simple.en: Faster engine → spark earlier.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Centrifugal advance: weights in the distributor fly out with speed and turn the cam forward, advancing the spark.

why.en: It follows engine speed.

recall_q.en: Advance mechanism that depends on engine speed?

explain_simple.en: Spinning weights move the spark earlier.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Vacuum advance: a diaphragm connected to manifold vacuum turns the CB base plate, advancing the spark at part load (high vacuum).

why.en: Lean part-load mixture burns slowly and needs more advance.

recall_q.en: Advance mechanism that depends on engine load?

explain_simple.en: Light load → more advance by vacuum.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Too much advance causes knocking and overheating. Too little (retarded) causes power loss, overheating and high fuel use.

why.en: Burn timing is wrong either way.

recall_q.en: Effect of over-advanced ignition?

explain_simple.en: Too early = knock; too late = weak.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Ignition timing is checked with a stroboscopic timing light aimed at marks on the crank pulley.

why.en: The flash freezes the moving mark.

recall_q.en: Instrument used to check ignition timing?

explain_simple.en: A flashing light shows the timing mark.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Ballast resistor in the primary circuit reduces coil current at normal running and is bypassed during cranking for a stronger spark.

why.en: Battery voltage drops while cranking.

recall_q.en: Why is the ballast resistor bypassed during starting?

recall_a.en: To give full voltage to the coil for a strong spark.

explain_simple.en: More voltage for starting.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Spark plug parts: terminal, insulator (ceramic), metal shell with threads, centre electrode, side (ground) electrode, gasket.

why.en: Insulator stops HT current leaking to the shell.

recall_q.en: Material of spark plug insulator?

explain_simple.en: Ceramic body, metal threads, two electrodes.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Spark plug gap is usually about 0.6–1.1 mm.

why.en: Too small: weak spark; too large: misfire.

recall_q.en: Typical spark plug gap?

explain_simple.en: Less than a millimetre or so.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Hot plug: long insulator nose, runs hot, used in low-speed, cool engines. Cold plug: short nose, loses heat fast, used in high-speed, high-compression engines.

why.en: Plug must stay hot enough to burn off carbon but not cause pre-ignition.

recall_q.en: Which plug suits a high-speed, high-compression engine?

explain_simple.en: Hot engine, cold plug. Cool engine, hot plug.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Spark plug reading: light tan/grey = normal; black sooty = rich mixture; oily = oil burning; white blistered = overheating/lean.

why.en: Plug colour shows engine condition.

recall_q.en: Black sooty spark plug shows?

explain_simple.en: Black = too much fuel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Spark plug types: standard, projected nose, resistor type (reduces radio interference), platinum/iridium tip (long life), multi-electrode.

why.en: Iridium plugs last much longer.

recall_q.en: Purpose of a resistor spark plug?

explain_simple.en: Stops crackling in the radio.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Magneto ignition makes its own current using magnets; no battery is needed.

why.en: Used where no battery exists: small bikes, outboard engines, aircraft.

recall_q.en: Does magneto ignition need a battery?

explain_simple.en: It makes its own electricity.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Magneto gives a weak spark at low speed (starting) and a strong spark at high speed. Coil ignition is the opposite: strong at low speed.

why.en: Magneto output depends on speed.

recall_q.en: Which ignition gives a better spark at starting: coil or magneto?

explain_simple.en: Magneto is weak at start, strong at speed.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Low tension magneto: produces low voltage; a separate coil steps it up near the plug. High tension magneto: has both windings inside and gives high voltage directly.

why.en: Differ in where voltage is stepped up.

recall_q.en: Magneto that gives high voltage directly?

explain_simple.en: HT magneto does it all inside.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Rotating armature magneto: windings rotate between fixed magnets. Rotating magnet magneto: magnets rotate, windings fixed (more common).

why.en: Fixed windings are more reliable.

recall_q.en: More common magneto type?

explain_simple.en: Spin the magnet, keep the coils still.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Flywheel magneto: magnets are cast in the flywheel. Used in scooters, mopeds and small engines.

why.en: Compact and simple.

recall_q.en: Magneto with magnets in the flywheel?

explain_simple.en: The flywheel is the magnet.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Electronic ignition replaces CB points with a transistor switch triggered by a sensor (magnetic pick-up, Hall effect or optical).

why.en: No point wear, accurate timing, stronger spark.

recall_q.en: What replaces CB points in electronic ignition?

explain_simple.en: Electronics switch the coil instead of points.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Transistorised coil ignition (TCI): points carry only a tiny trigger current; a transistor switches the coil current. Fully electronic versions use a pulse generator.

why.en: Points last longer or are not needed at all.

recall_q.en: In transistor-assisted ignition, what does the transistor switch?

explain_simple.en: Transistor does the heavy switching.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Capacitor discharge ignition (CDI): a capacitor is charged to about 400 V and discharged into the coil primary by a thyristor (SCR).

why.en: Very fast rise of voltage, strong spark at high speed.

example.en: Used in motorcycles and scooters.

recall_q.en: Ignition used in most two-wheelers?

explain_simple.en: A charged capacitor fires the coil.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Pulse generators: magnetic (inductive) pick-up — reluctor and coil; Hall-effect sensor — voltage changes when a vane passes; optical — light beam interrupted.

why.en: They tell the module when to fire.

recall_q.en: Sensor that produces voltage when a magnetic vane passes a semiconductor?

explain_simple.en: Sensors tell the computer when to spark.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Computer controlled (programmed/mapped) ignition: ECU sets spark timing from sensors (crank position, speed, load/MAP, coolant temperature, knock sensor) using a stored map.

why.en: Gives exact timing for every condition; no mechanical advance.

recall_q.en: What replaces centrifugal and vacuum advance in computer ignition?

recall_a.en: ECU timing map using sensor inputs.

explain_simple.en: A computer chooses the best spark time.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Knock sensor (piezoelectric) on the block detects knocking; the ECU retards timing to stop it.

why.en: Allows running close to the knock limit safely.

recall_q.en: Sensor that detects engine knock?

explain_simple.en: It hears knocking and the ECU delays the spark.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Distributor-less ignition (DLI / DIS): no distributor. Separate coils are triggered by the ECU using a crankshaft position sensor.

why.en: No rotor or cap to wear; stronger, accurate spark.

recall_q.en: Ignition system without a distributor?

explain_simple.en: Each coil fired directly by computer.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Wasted spark DLI: one coil fires two cylinders at once — one on compression (useful) and one on exhaust (wasted).

why.en: Pairs of cylinders reach TDC together.

recall_q.en: In a wasted spark system, how many plugs does one coil fire?

explain_simple.en: One spark used, one wasted.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Coil-on-plug (COP / direct ignition): a separate coil sits directly on each spark plug. No HT leads.

why.en: Least energy loss and interference.

recall_q.en: System with an individual coil on each spark plug?

explain_simple.en: Every plug has its own coil.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Crankshaft position sensor (CKP) tells the ECU crank angle and speed; camshaft position sensor (CMP) tells which cylinder is on compression.

why.en: Needed for spark and injection timing.

recall_q.en: Sensor giving crank angle and engine speed?

explain_simple.en: It tells the computer where the crank is.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: HT leads (ignition cables) are resistance or suppression cables (carbon core) to reduce radio interference.

why.en: Sparks create electrical noise.

recall_q.en: Why are HT leads made of carbon-core resistance wire?

explain_simple.en: Cuts electrical noise.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Coil = step-up transformer; spark when primary is broken.
CB points (tungsten), dwell angle, condenser stops arcing.
Centrifugal advance (speed), vacuum advance (load).
Magneto: LT/HT, rotating magnet/armature; weak at start.
Electronic, CDI (bikes), computer, DLI (wasted spark, COP).

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 came into force on 1 July 1989. It replaced the old Motor Vehicles Act, 1939.

why.en: It is the main law for drivers, vehicles, permits, traffic and insurance in India.

recall_q.en: MV Act 1988 came into force on?

explain_simple.en: Act of 1988, working from July 1989.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: The MV (Amendment) Act, 2019 brought big changes: much higher fines, Golden Hour care, Good Samaritan protection, a Motor Vehicle Accident Fund and stricter rules on juveniles.

why.en: Road deaths were very high; the law needed stronger teeth.

recall_q.en: Which amendment raised MV Act fines sharply?

recall_a.en: MV (Amendment) Act, 2019 (in force mostly from 1 September 2019).

explain_simple.en: 2019 amendment = big fines.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Rules under the Act: Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 (CMVR) made by the Centre, and Kerala Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 (KMVR) made by the State.

why.en: The Act gives the frame; rules give the details.

recall_q.en: Name the central and Kerala rules under the MV Act.

explain_simple.en: Act = frame; CMVR and KMVR = details.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Main chapters of the MV Act: II licensing of drivers, III licensing of conductors, IV registration, V permits (control of transport vehicles), VII construction and equipment, VIII traffic control.

why.en: PSC often asks which chapter covers which subject.

recall_q.en: Which chapter of the MV Act deals with registration?

explain_simple.en: II driver, III conductor, IV registration, V permit.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: More chapters: XI insurance against third-party risks, XII Claims Tribunals, XIII offences, penalties and procedure, XIV miscellaneous.

why.en: Fines sit in Chapter XIII; claims go to tribunals under Chapter XII.

recall_q.en: Offences and penalties are in which chapter of the MV Act?

explain_simple.en: XI insurance, XII tribunal, XIII fines.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A driver must carry the driving licence, registration certificate, insurance certificate and PUC certificate. Transport vehicles also need permit and fitness certificate.

why.en: Officers can ask for these documents at any time (Section 130).

recall_q.en: Documents to carry while driving a private car?

recall_a.en: DL, RC, insurance certificate, PUC certificate.

explain_simple.en: Licence, RC, insurance, PUC.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Documents can now be shown in electronic form through DigiLocker or mParivahan. These are valid like the paper copies.

why.en: Rule 139 CMVR allows electronic documents.

recall_q.en: Are DL and RC in DigiLocker valid for checking?

recall_a.en: Yes, electronic copies in DigiLocker/mParivahan are valid.

explain_simple.en: Phone copy in DigiLocker is fine.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Duty after an accident (Section 134): the driver must get medical help for the injured, take them to hospital if possible, and inform police and insurer.

why.en: Quick care saves lives in the golden hour.

recall_q.en: Section on duty of driver in case of accident and injury?

explain_simple.en: Accident: help the injured, tell police.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Golden Hour is the first one hour after a serious injury. Treatment in this time gives the best chance of survival. The 2019 amendment defined it.

why.en: Fast treatment prevents death from bleeding and shock.

recall_q.en: What is the Golden Hour?

recall_a.en: The first 60 minutes after a traumatic injury.

explain_simple.en: First hour after accident is most important.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A Good Samaritan (Section 134A) is a person who helps an accident victim in good faith. They cannot be harassed or held liable.

why.en: People hesitated to help because of police and court troubles.

recall_q.en: Which section protects Good Samaritans?

explain_simple.en: Helpers are protected by law.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Conductor licence is covered by Chapter III (Sections 29 to 38). A conductor of a stage carriage must hold a conductor licence.

why.en: Conductors handle passengers and tickets, so they must be trained.

recall_q.en: Who needs a conductor licence?

recall_a.en: Conductor of a stage carriage (Chapter III).

explain_simple.en: Bus conductor needs a licence.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Duties of a conductor: issue tickets, not allow overloading, help passengers board safely, keep the bus orderly, and not smoke or misbehave.

why.en: Passenger safety and fair fare collection.

recall_q.en: Give two duties of a bus conductor.

recall_a.en: Issue tickets; prevent overcrowding; safe boarding.

explain_simple.en: Tickets, safety, no overloading.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Learner's licence test checks knowledge of traffic rules, signs and driver duties. Driving test checks real driving skill (test of competence).

why.en: First knowledge, then skill.

recall_q.en: What does a learner's licence test check?

recall_a.en: Knowledge of traffic rules, signs and duties.

explain_simple.en: LL test = rules; DL test = driving.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Every motor vehicle must be registered before use in a public place (Section 39). The registering authority issues a Registration Certificate (RC).

why.en: Registration links the vehicle to an owner.

recall_q.en: Section making registration compulsory?

explain_simple.en: No registration, no road.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A non-transport vehicle's registration is valid for 15 years from the date of issue. After that it can be renewed for 5 years at a time.

why.en: Old vehicles must be checked again.

recall_q.en: Validity of RC for a new private car?

recall_a.en: 15 years; renewal for 5 years each time.

explain_simple.en: Private car RC = 15 years.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Transport vehicles need a fitness certificate (Section 56). A new transport vehicle gets fitness for 2 years, then it is renewed every year.

why.en: Buses and lorries run a lot and wear faster.

recall_q.en: First fitness certificate validity for a new transport vehicle?

recall_a.en: 2 years, then 1 year at a time.

explain_simple.en: New bus: 2 years fit, then yearly.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Road signs are of three types: mandatory (regulatory), cautionary (warning) and informatory.

why.en: Each type has its own shape so drivers know it at a glance.

recall_q.en: Three types of road signs?

explain_simple.en: Must do, be careful, for your information.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Mandatory signs are mostly circular. Cautionary signs are triangles pointing up with a red border. Informatory signs are rectangles (often blue or green).

why.en: Shape tells the type even from far away.

recall_q.en: Shape of a cautionary (warning) sign?

explain_simple.en: Circle = order, triangle = warning, rectangle = info.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Two mandatory signs have special shapes: STOP is an octagon (8 sides, red), and GIVE WAY is an inverted triangle (point down).

why.en: These are so important that they look different from all other signs.

recall_q.en: Shape of the STOP sign and the GIVE WAY sign?

recall_a.en: STOP: octagon. GIVE WAY: inverted triangle.

explain_simple.en: 8-sided stop; upside-down triangle give way.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Red-bordered circle = prohibition (do not do). Blue filled circle = compulsory (you must do), like compulsory left turn or compulsory cycle track.

why.en: PSC traps: blue circle is not information; it is an order.

recall_q.en: A blue circular sign means?

explain_simple.en: Red ring = don't; blue circle = must.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Traffic lights: red means stop, amber means stop if safe (light is about to change), green means go if the way is clear.

why.en: Amber is not a signal to speed up.

recall_q.en: What does a steady amber light mean?

recall_a.en: Stop before the line unless it is unsafe to stop.

explain_simple.en: Amber = get ready to stop.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Flashing amber: slow down and go with caution. Flashing red: stop fully, then go when safe.

why.en: Used at night or at junctions with low traffic.

recall_q.en: Meaning of flashing red signal?

recall_a.en: Stop completely, then proceed when safe.

explain_simple.en: Flashing red = like a stop sign.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Road markings: broken white centre line = you may cross to overtake if safe; solid line = do not cross; double solid yellow = never cross.

why.en: Solid lines are placed where overtaking is dangerous.

recall_q.en: Can you cross a solid centre line to overtake?

explain_simple.en: Broken = may cross; solid = don't.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Number plate colours: private white with black letters; transport yellow with black; self-drive rental black with yellow; electric vehicles green.

why.en: Colour shows the use of the vehicle at a glance.

recall_q.en: Colour of number plate for a self-drive rental car?

explain_simple.en: White private, yellow taxi, black rental, green EV.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Electric vehicle plates: private EV has green plate with white letters; commercial EV has green plate with yellow letters.

why.en: PSC trap: the letter colour changes, not the plate.

recall_q.en: Letters on a commercial EV number plate are which colour?

explain_simple.en: Green EV plate: white = private, yellow = commercial.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: High Security Registration Plates (HSRP) are aluminium plates with chromium hologram, laser-coded number and snap lock. They are compulsory for all vehicles.

why.en: They stop fake plates and help trace stolen vehicles.

recall_q.en: What is HSRP?

recall_a.en: Tamper-proof aluminium plate with hologram and laser code.

explain_simple.en: Hard-to-copy number plate.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: The BH (Bharat) series number lets a vehicle move between states without re-registration. It is for defence staff, government staff and private firms in four or more states.

why.en: People who transfer often need not re-register.

recall_q.en: Purpose of BH series registration?

recall_a.en: No re-registration when moving to another state.

explain_simple.en: BH = one number for all of India.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Kerala MVD is headed by the Transport Commissioner. Field offices are Regional Transport Offices (RTO) and Sub RTOs. MVIs and AMVIs do inspection and enforcement.

why.en: This is the department an AMVI works in.

recall_q.en: Head of the Kerala Motor Vehicles Department?

explain_simple.en: Transport Commissioner on top, RTOs below.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook
