learn.en: Wings of the MVD: administration, licensing and registration, technical (vehicle inspection), enforcement (road checks, Safe Kerala squads), and road safety.

why.en: Each wing does one main job.

recall_q.en: Which MVD wing does road checking?

explain_simple.en: Enforcement wing checks on the road.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Permits are granted by the State Transport Authority (STA) and Regional Transport Authority (RTA), set up under Section 68.

why.en: They control how many buses and lorries run on each route.

recall_q.en: Which authorities grant permits?

explain_simple.en: STA and RTA give permits.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Vehicle categories: L = two and three wheelers, M = passenger vehicles, N = goods vehicles. M1 is a car with up to 8 seats plus driver.

why.en: Category decides the rules and tests for a vehicle.

recall_q.en: Category letter for goods vehicles?

explain_simple.en: L light 2/3-wheel, M people, N goods.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: PSC trap: Kerala's state code on number plates is KL, and KL-01 is Thiruvananthapuram RTO.

why.en: Often asked as a one-mark general question.

recall_q.en: Which RTO has the code KL-01?

explain_simple.en: KL-01 = Thiruvananthapuram.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

title.en: MV Act basics, signs and the MVD

points.en: MV Act 1988, in force 1 July 1989; big amendment 2019.
Chapters: II driver, III conductor, IV registration, V permits, XIII offences.
Signs: circle order, triangle warning, rectangle info; STOP octagon.
Plates: white private, yellow transport, black rental, green EV.
Carry DL, RC, insurance, PUC; DigiLocker copies valid.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: The Indian Roads Congress (IRC), set up in 1934, makes the standards for road design in India.

why.en: All width, slope and curve values in exams come from IRC.

recall_q.en: Which body sets road design standards in India?

explain_simple.en: IRC writes the road rule book.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Road classes (Nagpur Road Plan, 1943): National Highways, State Highways, Major District Roads, Other District Roads and Village Roads.

why.en: Class decides width, speed and who maintains the road.

recall_q.en: Five classes of roads by the Nagpur plan?

recall_a.en: NH, SH, MDR, ODR, Village roads.

explain_simple.en: National, State, District (major, other), Village.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Carriageway is the part of the road that vehicles use. Shoulders are the strips beside it for stopped vehicles and support.

why.en: Shoulders protect the edge and give space in emergencies.

recall_q.en: Part of the road used by moving vehicles?

explain_simple.en: Carriageway = driving part.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: IRC widths: single lane 3.75 m; two-lane road without raised kerb 7.0 m; with raised kerbs 7.5 m; intermediate lane 5.5 m.

why.en: Width must fit the widest legal vehicle with safe clearance.

recall_q.en: IRC width of a two-lane carriageway without kerbs?

explain_simple.en: One lane 3.75 m, two lanes 7 m.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Maximum legal width of a motor vehicle is 2.6 m. Maximum height for normal vehicles is about 3.8 m.

why.en: Road lanes and bridges are designed for these sizes.

recall_q.en: Maximum permitted width of a vehicle?

explain_simple.en: Vehicle not wider than 2.6 m.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Formation width (roadway) = carriageway + shoulders. Right of way (land width) is the full land taken for the road, including space for future widening.

why.en: PSC asks the difference between these widths.

recall_q.en: Width of land acquired for a road is called?

explain_simple.en: Roadway = road + shoulders; right of way = all land.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Camber (cross slope) is the slope given across the road, high in the middle and low at the edges.

why.en: It drains rainwater off the road surface quickly.

recall_q.en: Main purpose of camber?

recall_a.en: Drain rainwater from the road surface.

explain_simple.en: Middle high so water runs off.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Camber values: concrete and high-type bituminous 1.7 to 2%; thin bituminous 2 to 2.5%; WBM and gravel 2.5 to 3%; earth roads 3 to 4%.

why.en: Rougher surfaces hold water, so they need more slope.

recall_q.en: Which surface needs the steepest camber?

explain_simple.en: Smooth road small slope; rough road big slope.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Camber shapes: parabolic (curved), straight line, or straight with a rounded crown. Heavy rain areas need more camber.

why.en: Parabolic suits fast cars; straight is easy to build.

recall_q.en: Name two camber shapes.

explain_simple.en: Curved or straight slope.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Super elevation (banking) means raising the outer edge of the road on a curve.

why.en: It balances the centrifugal force that pushes vehicles outward on a curve.

recall_q.en: Why is super elevation provided?

recall_a.en: To counter centrifugal force on curves.

explain_simple.en: Outer edge higher so vehicles don't slide out.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: IRC design super elevation: e = V² / (225 R), with V in km/h and R in metres. This assumes 75% of design speed and no friction.

why.en: Friction is left as a safety margin for mixed traffic.

recall_q.en: IRC formula for super elevation?

explain_simple.en: Speed squared over 225 times radius.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Full equilibrium equation on a curve: e + f = V² / (127 R). IRC takes the side friction f as 0.15.

why.en: Banking and tyre friction together hold the vehicle.

recall_q.en: Value of lateral friction f used by IRC?

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Maximum super elevation: 7% in plain and rolling terrain, 10% in hill roads (not snow-bound), 7% in snow-bound areas.

why.en: Too much banking makes slow vehicles slide inward.

recall_q.en: Maximum super elevation on plain roads?

explain_simple.en: Plain 7%, hills 10%.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

text.en: Question: Design speed 80 km/h, curve radius 500 m. Find super elevation.
e = 0.057, that is 5.7%. It is below 7%, so it is accepted.

summary.en: e = V²/(225R), V in km/h, R in m.
If e is above 7%, limit it to 7%.

recall_q.en: V = 80 km/h, R = 500 m. Super elevation?

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Gradient is the rise or fall of the road along its length. It is written as 1 in N or as a percent.

why.en: Steep gradients slow heavy vehicles and strain brakes downhill.

recall_q.en: What is gradient?

recall_a.en: Rate of rise or fall along the road length.

explain_simple.en: How steep the road goes up or down.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Types of gradient: ruling (normal design limit), limiting (used where ruling is too costly), exceptional (short stretches only) and minimum (for drainage).

why.en: Each is used in a different situation.

recall_q.en: Gradient that is normally adopted in design?

explain_simple.en: Ruling = normal; limiting = harder; exceptional = rare.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Plain terrain: ruling gradient 3.3% (1 in 30), limiting 5% (1 in 20), exceptional 6.7% (1 in 15).

why.en: Common numerical fact in PSC.

recall_q.en: Ruling gradient in plain terrain?

explain_simple.en: Plains: 1 in 30, 1 in 20, 1 in 15.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Mountainous terrain: ruling gradient 5% (1 in 20), limiting 6% (1 in 16.7), exceptional 7% (1 in 14.3).

why.en: Hills allow steeper roads to save length.

recall_q.en: Ruling gradient in mountainous terrain?

explain_simple.en: Mountains: ruling 5%.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Grade compensation reduces the gradient on a curve. It is (30 + R) / R percent, but not more than 75 / R percent.

why.en: A curve already adds resistance, so the slope must be eased.

recall_q.en: Formula for grade compensation on curves?

explain_simple.en: Ease the slope on a curve.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Sight distance is the length of road a driver can see ahead. It must be enough to stop or overtake safely.

why.en: You can only avoid what you can see in time.

recall_q.en: What is sight distance?

recall_a.en: Length of road visible ahead to the driver.

explain_simple.en: How far ahead the driver can see.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Stopping sight distance (SSD) = lag distance + braking distance. Lag distance = 0.278 V t; braking distance = V² / (254 f).

why.en: Car moves during reaction time, then while braking.

recall_q.en: SSD is made up of which two parts?

explain_simple.en: Thinking distance + braking distance.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: IRC uses a reaction time (perception and brake reaction) of 2.5 seconds, and friction f of 0.35 to 0.40 for SSD.

why.en: Value suits an average driver.

recall_q.en: Total reaction time used by IRC for SSD?

explain_simple.en: Driver needs 2.5 s to react.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

text.en: Question: V = 80 km/h, t = 2.5 s, f = 0.35. Find SSD.

recall_q.en: SSD at 80 km/h, t = 2.5 s, f = 0.35?

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Overtaking sight distance (OSD) = d1 + d2 + d3: distance while waiting behind, distance during the overtake, and distance the oncoming car moves.

why.en: Overtaking needs the opposite lane clear for all three.

recall_q.en: OSD is the sum of which three distances?

explain_simple.en: Wait + pass + oncoming car.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Intermediate sight distance (ISD) = 2 × SSD. For SSD, driver eye height is taken as 1.2 m and object height as 0.15 m.

why.en: Used where full OSD cannot be given.

recall_q.en: Intermediate sight distance equals?

explain_simple.en: ISD = 2 × SSD.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Extra widening on curves = mechanical widening (n l² / 2R) + psychological widening (V / 9.5√R).

why.en: Rear wheels cut inside the curve, and drivers keep away from the edge.

recall_q.en: Two parts of extra widening on curves?

explain_simple.en: Extra width on bends for wheels and nerves.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A transition curve joins a straight road to a circular curve gradually. The ideal shape is the spiral (clothoid).

why.en: Centrifugal force and banking build up slowly, not suddenly.

recall_q.en: Ideal shape of a transition curve?

explain_simple.en: Smooth entry into a bend.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Intersections are at-grade (roads meet at the same level, such as rotary or channelised junctions) or grade-separated (flyovers and interchanges).

why.en: Grade separation removes crossing conflicts.

recall_q.en: Flyover is which type of intersection?

explain_simple.en: Same level or different levels.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A four-leg junction of two two-way roads has 32 conflict points: 16 crossing, 8 merging and 8 diverging.

why.en: Crossing conflicts cause the worst crashes.

recall_q.en: Total conflict points at a 4-legged intersection?

explain_simple.en: Four-way junction = 32 danger points.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A rotary (roundabout) makes all traffic go one way around a central island. Vehicles merge and leave by weaving.

why.en: It turns crossing conflicts into gentle merges.

recall_q.en: Movement of vehicles within a rotary is called?

explain_simple.en: Roundabout: go round and weave out.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Cloverleaf, trumpet and diamond are types of grade-separated interchanges. A full cloverleaf removes all crossing conflicts.

why.en: Used on busy highways.

recall_q.en: Interchange shaped like a four-leaf clover is?

explain_simple.en: Clover, trumpet, diamond = flyover junctions.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: PCU (Passenger Car Unit) compares vehicles to one car. A car is 1 PCU; bigger or slower vehicles have higher PCU values.

why.en: Road capacity is counted in PCU.

recall_q.en: PCU value of a passenger car?

explain_simple.en: Count traffic as car-equivalents.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Lane 3.75 m; two-lane 7.0 m; vehicle width 2.6 m.
Camber drains water: 1.7–2% concrete up to 3–4% earth.
Super elevation e = V²/225R, max 7% plains.
Plain ruling gradient 1 in 30; 32 conflict points.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Third-party insurance is compulsory for every motor vehicle in a public place (Section 146). Driving without it is an offence.

why.en: Victims of an accident must get compensation.

recall_q.en: Which insurance is compulsory under the MV Act?

explain_simple.en: Third-party cover is a must.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: The three parties: first party is the owner, second party is the insurance company, third party is any other person hurt or whose property is damaged.

why.en: Third party is the outsider the law protects.

recall_q.en: Who is the third party in motor insurance?

recall_a.en: Any other person (not insurer or insured) who suffers loss.

explain_simple.en: Third party = other people.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Policy types: liability only (third party), comprehensive (third party + own damage) and standalone own damage.

why.en: Comprehensive also pays for damage to your own vehicle.

recall_q.en: Which policy covers both own damage and third-party liability?

explain_simple.en: TP only, or TP + own damage.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Third-party property damage cover is limited to ₹7.5 lakh. Third-party death and injury cover has no upper limit.

why.en: Human life cannot be capped.

recall_q.en: Limit for third-party death claims?

explain_simple.en: Property limited; life not limited.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Compulsory personal accident cover for the owner-driver is ₹15 lakh.

why.en: Owner is not a third party, so needs separate cover.

recall_q.en: Compulsory PA cover for owner-driver?

explain_simple.en: Owner-driver gets 15 lakh accident cover.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: IRDAI (Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India) regulates insurers and licenses surveyors.

why.en: It protects policy holders.

recall_q.en: Who licenses insurance surveyors?

explain_simple.en: IRDAI controls insurance.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A motor claim above ₹50,000 must be assessed by a surveyor licensed by IRDAI (Insurance Act, Section 64UM).

why.en: Big claims need an independent expert check.

recall_q.en: Claims above what amount need a licensed surveyor?

explain_simple.en: Big claim = licensed surveyor.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Kinds of survey: spot survey (at the accident site), final survey (estimates loss at the garage), re-inspection (checks repairs before payment).

why.en: Each step checks that the claim is real and fair.

recall_q.en: Survey done after repairs before settlement?

explain_simple.en: Spot, final, re-inspection.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: IDV (Insured Declared Value) is the current market value of the vehicle. It is the most the insurer pays for total loss or theft.

why.en: Premium and total-loss payment both depend on IDV.

recall_q.en: What is IDV?

recall_a.en: Insured Declared Value: maximum sum insured.

explain_simple.en: IDV = what your vehicle is worth now.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: IDV = manufacturer's listed price minus age depreciation: up to 6 months 5%, 6 months–1 year 15%, 1–2 years 20%, 2–3 years 30%, 3–4 years 40%, 4–5 years 50%.

why.en: Older vehicles are worth less.

recall_q.en: Depreciation for IDV on a 2½-year-old car?

explain_simple.en: Older car, lower IDV.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: For vehicles older than 5 years, IDV is fixed by agreement between the insurer and the owner.

why.en: Fixed tables do not fit very old vehicles.

recall_q.en: How is IDV fixed for a 7-year-old vehicle?

explain_simple.en: Very old car: agree on value.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

text.en: Question: Listed price ₹8,00,000. Car is 2 years 4 months old. Find IDV.

recall_q.en: Price ₹8 lakh, age 2 years 4 months. IDV?

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Depreciation on parts: rubber, nylon, plastic parts, tyres, tubes and batteries 50%; fibreglass parts 30%; glass parts nil.

why.en: Owner gets new parts, so a share of the cost is borne by them.

recall_q.en: Depreciation on glass parts in a claim?

explain_simple.en: Rubber 50%, fibre 30%, glass 0%.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Metal parts depreciation by age: under 6 months nil, 6 months–1 year 5%, 1–2 years 10%, 2–3 years 15%, 3–4 years 25%, 4–5 years 35%, 5–10 years 40%, over 10 years 50%.

why.en: Metal parts last long, so depreciation rises slowly.

recall_q.en: Depreciation on metal parts for a 3½-year-old car?

explain_simple.en: Metal parts: older, more cut.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Zero depreciation is an add-on cover. With it, the insurer pays the full cost of replaced parts without deducting depreciation.

why.en: It reduces what the owner pays from pocket.

recall_q.en: Which add-on removes depreciation deduction?

explain_simple.en: Zero dep = full part cost paid.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Constructive total loss (CTL): when repair cost plus salvage handling exceeds 75% of IDV, the vehicle is treated as a total loss.

why.en: Repairing would cost nearly as much as the vehicle.

recall_q.en: Repair cost above what percent of IDV makes it a total loss?

explain_simple.en: Repair too costly = total loss.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Salvage is the value of the damaged vehicle or parts left after the loss. It goes to the insurer or is deducted from the claim.

why.en: The owner should not gain from the loss.

recall_q.en: Value of damaged parts left after a loss is?

explain_simple.en: Salvage = what the wreck is still worth.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: No Claim Bonus (NCB) is a discount on the own-damage premium for claim-free years: 20%, 25%, 35%, 45%, then 50% after five years.

why.en: It rewards careful drivers.

recall_q.en: Maximum NCB?

explain_simple.en: No claim = cheaper next year.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: NCB belongs to the owner, not the vehicle. It can be moved to a new vehicle. It is lost when a claim is made.

why.en: PSC trap: NCB is not lost when you sell the car.

recall_q.en: Does NCB go with the vehicle on sale?

recall_a.en: No, it stays with the owner.

explain_simple.en: NCB follows the person.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Compulsory deductible (excess) is the fixed amount the owner pays in every own-damage claim, such as ₹1,000 for private cars up to 1,500 cc.

why.en: It stops very small claims.

recall_q.en: What is compulsory deductible?

recall_a.en: Fixed part of each claim borne by the owner.

explain_simple.en: You pay the first small part.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Factors in assessing loss: cause matches the accident story, extent of damage, repair or replace, depreciation, salvage, policy conditions and valid DL and permit.

why.en: The surveyor must find a fair and true amount.

recall_q.en: Give three factors a surveyor checks.

recall_a.en: Cause, extent of damage, depreciation, salvage, policy terms.

explain_simple.en: Is it true, how much, what deductions.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A claim can be refused if the driver had no valid licence, was drunk, or the vehicle was used for a purpose not covered, such as hire use under a private policy.

why.en: These break the policy conditions.

recall_q.en: Give one reason an own-damage claim can be refused.

recall_a.en: No valid DL, drunk driving, or misuse of vehicle.

explain_simple.en: Break the rules, lose the claim.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Insurance principles: utmost good faith, insurable interest, indemnity, subrogation, contribution and proximate cause.

why.en: Every claim decision rests on these.

recall_q.en: Name the principle that says insurance only puts you back where you were.

explain_simple.en: Insurance repairs loss, gives no profit.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Subrogation: after paying the claim, the insurer gets the owner's right to recover money from the person who caused the loss.

why.en: The owner cannot be paid twice.

recall_q.en: Insurer taking the insured's right to recover is called?

explain_simple.en: Insurer steps into your shoes.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Claim steps: tell the insurer quickly, file FIR if needed (theft, injury), survey, approval, repair, re-inspection, payment.

why.en: Late notice can weaken the claim.

recall_q.en: First step after an accident for an insurance claim?

explain_simple.en: Tell insurer first.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Theft claim needs FIR, all keys, RC, and a non-traceable report from police. It is settled on IDV.

why.en: Proof that the vehicle is really lost.

recall_q.en: Police document needed to settle a theft claim?

explain_simple.en: Theft: FIR, keys, police untraced report.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Premium depends on IDV, engine cc, age, zone (city), NCB, add-ons and voluntary deductible. Third-party premium rates are fixed by IRDAI.

why.en: More risk and higher value mean higher premium.

recall_q.en: Who fixes third-party premium rates?

explain_simple.en: Bigger, costlier car pays more.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

points.en: TP insurance compulsory (Sec 146); TP life cover unlimited.
IDV = price − age depreciation (5% to 50%).
Rubber, tyres 50%; fibre 30%; glass nil.
Surveyor needed above ₹50,000; CTL above 75% of IDV.
NCB 20% to 50%; stays with owner.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Electronic fuel injection (EFI) sprays fuel through injectors that an electronic control unit (ECU) controls. It replaced the carburettor.

why.en: The ECU meters fuel exactly for every condition.

recall_q.en: What replaced the carburettor in modern petrol engines?

explain_simple.en: Computer-controlled fuel spray.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Advantages of EFI: better mileage, lower emissions, easy cold start, more power, smooth running and no carburettor icing.

why.en: Exact fuel quantity means less waste.

recall_q.en: Give two advantages of EFI over carburettor.

recall_a.en: Better economy, lower emissions, easy cold start.

explain_simple.en: Less fuel, less smoke, easy start.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Throttle body injection (TBI) is single-point injection: one or two injectors placed at the throttle body, feeding all cylinders.

why.en: It is cheap and simple, like an electronic carburettor.

recall_q.en: Single-point injection is also called?

explain_simple.en: One injector for all cylinders.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: MPFI (multi-point fuel injection) has one injector for each cylinder, spraying into the intake port just before the inlet valve.

why.en: Each cylinder gets equal fuel.

recall_q.en: Where does an MPFI injector spray fuel?

recall_a.en: Into the intake port, just before the inlet valve.

explain_simple.en: One injector per cylinder, at the port.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: MPFI injection timing: simultaneous (all at once), group or batch (in groups) and sequential (each injector in firing order).

why.en: Sequential gives the best control.

recall_q.en: Which MPFI type fires injectors in firing order?

explain_simple.en: Sequential = one by one, in order.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: GDI (gasoline direct injection) sprays petrol directly into the combustion chamber at high pressure (about 50–200 bar).

why.en: It allows lean stratified burning and higher compression.

recall_q.en: In GDI, fuel is injected into?

explain_simple.en: Petrol sprayed straight into the cylinder.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Fuel supply in EFI: electric fuel pump in the tank → filter → fuel rail → injectors. A pressure regulator keeps about 3 bar.

why.en: Steady pressure means fuel quantity depends only on opening time.

recall_q.en: Where is the electric fuel pump usually fitted?

explain_simple.en: Pump in tank pushes fuel to injectors.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: An injector is a solenoid valve. The ECU opens it for a few milliseconds; this time is called pulse width. Longer pulse width gives more fuel.

why.en: Fuel quantity is controlled by time.

recall_q.en: What decides the quantity of fuel from an injector?

explain_simple.en: Open longer = more fuel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: The ECU (ECM) is the brain. It reads sensors (inputs), decides, and drives actuators (outputs) like injectors and ignition coils.

why.en: Input → process → output.

recall_q.en: Sensors are ECU inputs or outputs?

explain_simple.en: Sensors tell; ECU thinks; actuators act.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Open loop: ECU uses fixed maps without O2 feedback (cold start, full throttle). Closed loop: ECU corrects fuel using the oxygen sensor.

why.en: Closed loop keeps the mixture near 14.7:1 for the catalyst.

recall_q.en: Which sensor makes closed-loop control possible?

explain_simple.en: Closed loop = ECU checks exhaust and corrects.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Stoichiometric air-fuel ratio for petrol is 14.7:1 by mass. Lambda (λ) = actual AFR ÷ 14.7. λ = 1 is ideal; above 1 lean; below 1 rich.

why.en: The three-way catalyst works best at λ = 1.

recall_q.en: λ greater than 1 means the mixture is?

explain_simple.en: λ 1 = perfect, more = lean, less = rich.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

text.en: Question: A petrol engine runs at AFR 16:1. Find λ and say rich or lean.
λ is above 1, so the mixture is lean.

recall_q.en: AFR 16:1 petrol. λ and type?

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: MAF sensor (mass air flow) measures air entering the engine. Hot-wire type: incoming air cools a heated wire; more current needed means more air.

why.en: ECU must know the air mass to add the right fuel.

recall_q.en: Working principle of a hot-wire MAF sensor?

recall_a.en: Air cools a heated wire; current to keep it hot shows air mass.

explain_simple.en: More air cools the wire more.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: MAP sensor (manifold absolute pressure) measures pressure (vacuum) in the intake manifold. ECU uses it with rpm to estimate engine load (speed-density method).

why.en: Cheaper than a MAF sensor.

recall_q.en: What does the MAP sensor measure?

explain_simple.en: Manifold vacuum shows load.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Throttle position sensor (TPS) is a potentiometer on the throttle shaft. It tells the ECU how much the throttle is open.

why.en: Sudden opening needs extra fuel (acceleration enrichment).

recall_q.en: TPS is which type of sensor?

explain_simple.en: TPS tells how far you pressed.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Coolant temperature sensor is an NTC thermistor: its resistance falls as temperature rises. A cold engine gets a richer mixture.

why.en: Cold fuel vaporises poorly.

recall_q.en: Resistance of an NTC coolant sensor when the engine heats up?

explain_simple.en: Hotter = less resistance.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Intake air temperature (IAT) sensor is also an NTC thermistor. Cold air is denser, so the ECU adds more fuel.

why.en: Fuel must match the air mass.

recall_q.en: Why does the ECU need intake air temperature?

explain_simple.en: Cold air needs more fuel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Oxygen (lambda) sensor sits in the exhaust. The zirconia type makes 0.1 to 0.9 V: high voltage (about 0.9 V) means rich, low (about 0.1 V) means lean.

why.en: It tells the ECU if burning was rich or lean.

recall_q.en: Zirconia O2 sensor output for a rich mixture?

explain_simple.en: Rich = high voltage.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Crankshaft position sensor (CKP) gives engine speed and piston position. If it fails, there is no spark or injection, so the engine will not start.

why.en: Timing of spark and fuel depends on it.

recall_q.en: Failure of which sensor causes a no-start in EFI?

explain_simple.en: No CKP signal, no start.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Camshaft position sensor (CMP) tells which cylinder is on its compression stroke. It is needed for sequential injection.

why.en: Crank turns twice per cycle; cam tells which turn.

recall_q.en: Which sensor identifies cylinder 1 for sequential injection?

explain_simple.en: Cam sensor says which cylinder is next.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Knock sensor is a piezoelectric sensor on the block. When it detects knocking, the ECU retards the ignition timing.

why.en: Knock can break pistons.

recall_q.en: ECU response to a knock signal?

explain_simple.en: Knock heard, spark delayed.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Hall effect and inductive (magnetic) sensors are used for crank, cam and wheel speed. Inductive sensors make AC voltage; Hall sensors give a digital square wave.

why.en: Both turn rotation into electric pulses.

recall_q.en: Which sensor type gives a square-wave digital output?

explain_simple.en: Hall = on/off pulses.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Actuators in EFI: injectors, idle air control valve, ignition coils, fuel pump relay, electronic throttle motor, EGR valve and canister purge valve.

why.en: These carry out the ECU's orders.

recall_q.en: Name two actuators in an EFI system.

recall_a.en: Injectors, idle air control valve, ignition coil.

explain_simple.en: Actuators do the work.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Idle air control (IAC) valve lets a little air bypass the closed throttle to keep idle speed steady when AC or lights are switched on.

why.en: Extra load would otherwise stall the engine.

recall_q.en: Function of the IAC valve?

recall_a.en: Control idle speed by bypass air.

explain_simple.en: Keeps idle steady.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Drive-by-wire (electronic throttle control): the accelerator pedal has a sensor, and a motor opens the throttle. There is no cable.

why.en: Allows cruise control and traction control.

recall_q.en: In drive-by-wire, what opens the throttle?

recall_a.en: An electric motor controlled by the ECU.

explain_simple.en: Pedal sends signal, motor opens throttle.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: If a sensor fails, the ECU uses default values (limp home mode) and lights the MIL (check engine light).

why.en: The driver can still reach a workshop.

recall_q.en: What is limp home mode?

recall_a.en: Safe reduced running using default values after a fault.

explain_simple.en: Runs weakly so you get home.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: OBD (on-board diagnostics) stores fault codes (DTCs like P0301). A scan tool reads them through the 16-pin OBD-II connector. OBD-II is compulsory with BS-VI.

why.en: Fast and accurate fault finding.

recall_q.en: Fault codes are read through which port?

explain_simple.en: Plug scanner, read fault code.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: CRDI (common rail direct injection) is the diesel system where a high-pressure pump keeps fuel in a common rail. ECU-controlled injectors spray it into each cylinder.

why.en: Injection pressure is the same at any engine speed.

recall_q.en: Full form of CRDI?

explain_simple.en: One high-pressure pipe feeds all injectors.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: CRDI pressure is very high: about 1,350 to 2,000 bar or more. Very fine spray burns cleaner.

why.en: Fine droplets mix quickly with air.

recall_q.en: Typical CRDI rail pressure?

explain_simple.en: Very high pressure, very fine spray.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: CRDI parts: low-pressure feed pump, high-pressure pump, common rail, rail pressure sensor, pressure control valve, solenoid or piezo injectors, ECU.

why.en: Each keeps pressure and timing exact.

recall_q.en: Which sensor tells the ECU the rail pressure?

explain_simple.en: Pump, rail, sensor, injectors.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: CRDI can inject several times per cycle: pilot (small, before), main, and post injection.

why.en: Pilot injection reduces diesel knock and noise; post helps DPF cleaning.

recall_q.en: Why is pilot injection used?

recall_a.en: To reduce diesel knock and noise.

explain_simple.en: A little fuel first, then the main shot.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Piezo injectors open faster than solenoid injectors, so they allow more precise and more injections per cycle.

why.en: Piezo crystals change size instantly with voltage.

recall_q.en: Which injector type responds fastest?

explain_simple.en: Piezo = fastest injector.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Older diesel systems: inline pump, rotary (distributor) pump and unit injector. In these, pressure rises with engine speed.

why.en: CRDI fixed this weakness.

recall_q.en: Name one older diesel injection pump type.

explain_simple.en: Old pumps: inline, rotary.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: PSC trap: the term 'MPFI' is for petrol engines; 'CRDI' is for diesel engines. Both are electronically controlled injection.

why.en: Options often mix these up.

recall_q.en: CRDI is used in petrol or diesel engines?

explain_simple.en: MPFI petrol, CRDI diesel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

title.en: Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI

points.en: TBI single point; MPFI port per cylinder; GDI into cylinder.
Injector quantity = pulse width; fuel pressure about 3 bar.
Sensors: MAF, MAP, TPS, ECT (NTC), O2, CKP, CMP, knock.
λ = AFR/14.7; closed loop uses O2 sensor.
CRDI: rail 1,350–2,000 bar; pilot, main, post injection.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Main pollutants from petrol engines are CO, HC and NOx. Diesel engines give mainly NOx and particulate matter (PM or soot).

why.en: Petrol engines run near ideal mixture; diesels run lean with smoke.

recall_q.en: Main pollutants from a diesel engine?

explain_simple.en: Petrol: CO, HC, NOx. Diesel: NOx, soot.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Sources of HC in a petrol car without controls: exhaust about 60%, crankcase blow-by about 20%, evaporation from tank and carburettor about 20%.

why.en: Each source needs its own control device.

recall_q.en: What share of HC comes from crankcase blow-by?

explain_simple.en: Exhaust 60, crankcase 20, evaporation 20.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Carbon monoxide (CO) forms from incomplete burning with a rich mixture. It is colourless, odourless and poisonous; it binds with haemoglobin in blood.

why.en: Blood then cannot carry oxygen.

recall_q.en: CO is mainly formed by a rich or lean mixture?

explain_simple.en: Too much fuel makes CO.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Hydrocarbons (HC) are unburnt fuel. They come from rich mixture, misfire, and fuel left near cold cylinder walls (quench layer).

why.en: HC causes smog and eye irritation.

recall_q.en: Give one cause of high HC emission.

explain_simple.en: Unburnt fuel comes out as HC.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: NOx (oxides of nitrogen) forms at very high combustion temperature with extra oxygen. High compression and slightly lean mixtures increase NOx.

why.en: Nitrogen in air reacts only when very hot.

recall_q.en: Main cause of NOx formation?

recall_a.en: High combustion temperature with excess oxygen.

explain_simple.en: Too hot burning makes NOx.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: In diesels there is a NOx–PM trade-off: cooler burning cuts NOx but raises soot, and hotter burning cuts soot but raises NOx.

why.en: That is why diesels need both EGR/SCR and a DPF.

recall_q.en: Reducing NOx in a diesel usually increases which pollutant?

explain_simple.en: Less NOx, more soot; less soot, more NOx.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: PCV (positive crankcase ventilation) valve sends blow-by gases from the crankcase back into the intake manifold to be burnt.

why.en: It stops crankcase HC from going into the air.

recall_q.en: Purpose of the PCV valve?

recall_a.en: Burn crankcase blow-by gases by sending them to the intake.

explain_simple.en: Crankcase gas goes back to burn.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: EVAP system: an activated charcoal canister stores fuel vapour from the tank. When the engine runs, the purge valve sends the vapour to the intake to burn.

why.en: Stops evaporative HC loss.

recall_q.en: Material in an EVAP canister?

explain_simple.en: Charcoal catches petrol vapour.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: EGR (exhaust gas recirculation) sends a small part of exhaust gas (about 5–15%) back into the intake.

why.en: Inert gas lowers peak combustion temperature, so NOx falls.

recall_q.en: EGR mainly reduces which pollutant?

explain_simple.en: Some exhaust back in, flame cooler, less NOx.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: EGR is closed at idle and at full throttle. It works at part load and cruising.

why.en: At idle it causes rough running; at full throttle power is needed.

recall_q.en: Is EGR active at idle?

explain_simple.en: EGR works when cruising.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A three-way catalytic converter changes CO to CO₂, HC to CO₂ and water, and NOx to nitrogen, all at once.

why.en: Three pollutants, one device.

recall_q.en: Three pollutants controlled by a three-way catalyst?

explain_simple.en: Turns three bad gases into safe ones.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Catalysts used: platinum and palladium for oxidation (CO, HC); rhodium for reduction of NOx.

why.en: Rhodium is the PSC answer for NOx reduction.

recall_q.en: Which metal in a catalytic converter reduces NOx?

explain_simple.en: Pt, Pd burn; Rh reduces NOx.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Catalytic converter body is a ceramic honeycomb (cordierite) or metal monolith with an alumina washcoat holding the precious metals.

why.en: Honeycomb gives a large surface in a small space.

recall_q.en: Material of the honeycomb in a catalytic converter?

explain_simple.en: Honeycomb gives big surface.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A catalytic converter starts working above about 250–300 °C (light-off temperature). It needs λ close to 1.

why.en: Cold starts give most of the pollution.

recall_q.en: What is light-off temperature?

recall_a.en: Temperature at which the catalyst starts working (about 250–300 °C).

explain_simple.en: Catalyst works only when hot.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Leaded petrol poisons the catalytic converter. Misfire overheats and melts it. Leaded petrol was banned in India from 2000.

why.en: Lead coats the catalyst so gases can't touch it.

recall_q.en: What fuel additive poisons a catalytic converter?

explain_simple.en: Lead kills the catalyst.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A two-way (oxidation) catalyst controls only CO and HC. Diesels use a diesel oxidation catalyst (DOC).

why.en: Diesel exhaust has too much oxygen to reduce NOx in a normal catalyst.

recall_q.en: Two-way catalyst controls which pollutants?

explain_simple.en: Two-way: CO and HC only.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Afterburner (thermal reactor) burns leftover CO and HC in the hot exhaust manifold with extra air supplied by air injection.

why.en: A second burning cleans the exhaust.

recall_q.en: What does an afterburner do?

recall_a.en: Burns remaining CO and HC in the exhaust with added air.

explain_simple.en: Burns leftovers in the exhaust.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Diesel particulate filter (DPF) traps soot. It cleans itself by burning the soot (regeneration) at high temperature.

why.en: Soot harms lungs.

recall_q.en: Process of burning soot in a DPF is called?

explain_simple.en: Filter traps soot, then burns it.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: SCR (selective catalytic reduction) sprays urea solution (AdBlue or DEF, 32.5% urea) into the exhaust. It forms ammonia, which turns NOx into nitrogen and water.

why.en: Best NOx control for BS-VI diesels.

recall_q.en: Liquid used in an SCR system?

explain_simple.en: Urea cleans NOx.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Diesel smoke colours: black = incomplete burning (overload, faulty injector, rich); blue = lube oil burning; white = unburnt fuel at cold start or water in fuel.

why.en: Colour tells the fault.

recall_q.en: Blue smoke from the exhaust indicates?

explain_simple.en: Black fuel, blue oil, white cold/water.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Diesel smoke is measured with a smoke meter. Hartridge type measures light absorption (opacity); Bosch type uses filter paper blackening.

why.en: PUC test for diesels checks smoke density.

recall_q.en: Hartridge smoke meter works on?

explain_simple.en: Smoke blocks light; meter measures it.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Diesel PUC test is a free acceleration smoke test. Result is the light absorption coefficient k in m⁻¹.

why.en: Quick, needs no load.

recall_q.en: Unit of smoke density in diesel PUC test?

explain_simple.en: Rev it fast, measure smoke.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Exhaust gas analysers use NDIR (non-dispersive infrared) to measure CO, CO₂ and HC in petrol vehicles.

why.en: Each gas absorbs infrared at its own wavelength.

recall_q.en: Principle of a petrol exhaust gas analyser?

explain_simple.en: Infrared light finds the gases.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Lab methods: FID (flame ionisation detector) for HC and chemiluminescence for NOx.

why.en: Higher accuracy for type approval tests.

recall_q.en: NOx is measured in labs by?

explain_simple.en: FID for HC, chemiluminescence for NOx.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: PUC limits for BS-IV and later petrol 4-wheelers: idle CO 0.3% and HC 200 ppm; at high idle CO 0.2% and λ 1 ± 0.03.

why.en: Check current Rule 115 CMVR values before the exam.

recall_q.en: Idle CO limit for BS-IV petrol car in PUC test?

explain_simple.en: BS-IV car: CO 0.3% at idle.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Bharat Stage (BS) norms are India's emission standards, based on European (Euro) norms. They are set by the central government under CMVR.

why.en: Each new stage cuts the allowed pollution.

recall_q.en: Bharat Stage norms are based on?

explain_simple.en: BS = India's version of Euro norms.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Timeline: BS-I (India 2000) in 2000, BS-IV across India from April 2017, BS-V skipped, BS-VI across India from 1 April 2020.

why.en: PSC asks which stage was skipped and the BS-VI date.

recall_q.en: Which Bharat Stage was skipped?

explain_simple.en: Jumped from BS-IV to BS-VI in 2020.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: BS-VI fuel has only 10 ppm sulphur, against 50 ppm in BS-IV fuel.

why.en: Low sulphur is needed for DPF and SCR to work.

recall_q.en: Sulphur content in BS-VI fuel?

explain_simple.en: BS-VI fuel: 10 ppm sulphur.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: BS-VI Phase 2 (April 2023) added Real Driving Emission (RDE) tests and on-board monitoring of emissions.

why.en: Lab results must match real roads.

recall_q.en: What did BS-VI phase 2 add?

recall_a.en: Real Driving Emission (RDE) testing and on-board monitoring.

explain_simple.en: Test on real roads too.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: PUC (Pollution Under Control) certificate shows that the vehicle passed the emission test. Driving without a valid PUC is an offence.

why.en: Regular checks keep old vehicles in limits.

recall_q.en: Full form of PUC?

explain_simple.en: PUC = passed smoke test.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Noise is measured with a sound level meter in dB(A). Pressure horns and multi-tone horns are banned; changing the silencer to make noise is an offence.

why.en: Noise harms hearing and health.

recall_q.en: Unit of vehicle noise measurement?

explain_simple.en: Noise measured in decibels.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Cleaner fuels: CNG and LPG give less CO and PM. Ethanol blending (E20, 20% ethanol in petrol) cuts imports and emissions.

why.en: Fuel choice also controls pollution.

recall_q.en: What does E20 mean?

explain_simple.en: E20 = 20% ethanol.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

title.en: How a three-way catalytic converter cleans exhaust

text.en: Exhaust with CO, HC and NOx enters the hot honeycomb.

explain.en: It must be above light-off temperature.

text.en: Rhodium takes oxygen from NOx, leaving nitrogen (N₂).
That oxygen, with platinum or palladium, burns CO to CO₂ and HC to CO₂ and water.
The O2 sensor helps the ECU keep λ near 1, so both reactions can happen.

summary.en: Oxidation: CO, HC → CO₂, H₂O (Pt, Pd).

recall_q.en: Why must λ stay near 1 for a three-way catalyst?

recall_a.en: So oxidation of CO/HC and reduction of NOx both happen.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

points.en: PCV crankcase HC; EVAP charcoal canister; EGR cuts NOx.
Three-way catalyst: Pt, Pd oxidise; Rh reduces NOx.
Diesel: DOC, DPF (soot), SCR with urea (NOx).
Smoke: black fuel, blue oil, white cold or water.
BS-IV 2017, BS-V skipped, BS-VI 1 April 2020.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Active safety systems help avoid a crash (ABS, ESC, traction control). Passive safety systems protect people during a crash (seat belt, airbag, crumple zone).

why.en: PSC often asks to classify a system as active or passive.

recall_q.en: Is an airbag an active or passive safety system?

explain_simple.en: Active avoids crash; passive protects in crash.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: ABS (anti-lock braking system) stops the wheels from locking during hard braking, so the driver can still steer.

why.en: A locked wheel slides and cannot steer.

recall_q.en: Main benefit of ABS?

recall_a.en: Keeps steering control by preventing wheel lock.

explain_simple.en: Brake hard and still steer.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: ABS parts: wheel speed sensors, ABS ECU, and the hydraulic modulator (valves and a pump). The modulator releases and reapplies pressure many times a second.

why.en: This pulsing keeps the wheel just short of locking.

recall_q.en: Which ABS part changes brake pressure?

explain_simple.en: Sensors watch, ECU decides, modulator pulses.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: With ABS the brake pedal pulses during hard braking. The driver should keep pressing firmly, not pump the pedal.

why.en: The system does the pumping.

recall_q.en: How should a driver brake hard in an ABS car?

recall_a.en: Press firmly and hold; do not pump.

explain_simple.en: Press hard, keep pressing.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: ABS is compulsory for two-wheelers above 125 cc, and CBS (combined braking system) for two-wheelers up to 125 cc, from April 2019.

why.en: Two-wheeler skids caused many deaths.

recall_q.en: Which braking system is compulsory for two-wheelers up to 125 cc?

explain_simple.en: Above 125 cc ABS; up to 125 cc CBS.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: EBD (electronic brake force distribution) shares braking force between front and rear wheels according to load. It works with ABS.

why.en: A loaded rear can take more braking.

recall_q.en: What does EBD do?

recall_a.en: Distributes brake force to each wheel by load.

explain_simple.en: Right braking for each wheel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Traction control stops the drive wheels from spinning when accelerating. It cuts engine torque or brakes the spinning wheel, using ABS wheel sensors.

why.en: Spinning wheels lose grip.

recall_q.en: Traction control works during braking or acceleration?

explain_simple.en: Stops wheel spin when you speed up.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: ESC (electronic stability control, also ESP) stops skids. Using steering angle, yaw rate and lateral acceleration sensors, it brakes single wheels to keep the car on its path.

why.en: It corrects understeer and oversteer.

recall_q.en: Which sensor tells ESC how fast the car is turning about its vertical axis?

explain_simple.en: ESC stops the car from spinning out.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A three-point seat belt holds the chest and hips. Its inertia reel locks when the car slows suddenly.

why.en: It stops the body flying forward.

recall_q.en: What locks a seat belt in a sudden stop?

explain_simple.en: Belt locks on sudden stop.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Seat belt pretensioner pulls the belt tight at the start of a crash, often with a small explosive charge. Load limiter then lets out a little belt to reduce chest injury.

why.en: Tight early, gentle later.

recall_q.en: Function of a seat belt pretensioner?

recall_a.en: Tightens the belt instantly in a crash.

explain_simple.en: Belt snaps tight in a crash.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Airbags are SRS (supplementary restraint system). They work along with the seat belt, not instead of it.

why.en: Without a belt, the body can hit the opening airbag hard.

recall_q.en: Full form of SRS?

explain_simple.en: Airbag helps the belt, doesn't replace it.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Airbag working: crash sensor (accelerometer) → airbag ECU → igniter → gas generator fills the bag in about 30 milliseconds.

why.en: The bag must be full before the head moves forward.

recall_q.en: About how fast does an airbag inflate?

explain_simple.en: Faster than a blink.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Older airbags used sodium azide to make nitrogen gas. A clock spring (spiral cable) connects the steering wheel airbag while the wheel turns.

why.en: Wires cannot twist with the steering wheel otherwise.

recall_q.en: Gas used to inflate an airbag?

explain_simple.en: Nitrogen fills the bag.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Driver airbag is compulsory in cars from July 2019. Front passenger airbag is compulsory for new cars from 2021.

why.en: Front crashes are most common.

recall_q.en: Front passenger airbag became compulsory from?

explain_simple.en: Driver 2019, passenger 2021.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Never fit a rear-facing child seat in front of an active passenger airbag. Children should sit in the rear seat.

why.en: The opening airbag can hit the child seat with great force.

recall_q.en: Where should a rear-facing child seat never be placed?

recall_a.en: Front seat with an active airbag.

explain_simple.en: Kids in the back.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Since July 2019 new cars must have: driver airbag, seat belt reminder, speed alert, rear parking sensors and a manual override for central locking.

why.en: Basic safety for all cars.

recall_q.en: Name two features made compulsory in cars from July 2019.

recall_a.en: Driver airbag, seat belt reminder, speed alert, parking sensors.

explain_simple.en: Airbag, belt beeper, speed beeper, reverse sensor.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Speed alert system: beeps once above 80 km/h, beeps often above 100 km/h, and beeps continuously above 120 km/h.

why.en: Warns the driver of high speed.

recall_q.en: Speed above which the speed alert beeps continuously?

explain_simple.en: 80 beep, 100 more, 120 nonstop.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Parking sensors are ultrasonic sensors in the bumper. The beep gets faster as an object gets closer. A reverse camera shows the area behind.

why.en: Small objects behind are hard to see.

recall_q.en: Type of sensor used for parking sensors?

explain_simple.en: Sound waves bounce back from objects.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Cruise control keeps a set speed without pressing the accelerator. Adaptive cruise control uses radar to keep a safe gap to the car ahead.

why.en: Reduces fatigue on highways.

recall_q.en: What extra does adaptive cruise control do?

recall_a.en: Keeps a safe distance using radar.

explain_simple.en: Cruise holds speed; adaptive also keeps gap.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Cruise control turns off when the driver presses the brake or clutch.

why.en: The driver must always be in control.

recall_q.en: How is cruise control cancelled?

recall_a.en: Press brake (or clutch) or the cancel switch.

explain_simple.en: Touch brake, cruise stops.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Power windows, power seats and power mirrors use small DC motors. Power seats may have memory positions; power windows may have anti-pinch.

why.en: Comfort with one button.

recall_q.en: What drives a power window?

recall_a.en: A small DC motor and regulator.

explain_simple.en: Small motors move glass, seats and mirrors.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Rain-sensing wiper: an infrared light beam is reflected inside the windscreen. Raindrops change the reflection, and the wipers start and adjust speed.

why.en: Driver need not adjust wipers.

recall_q.en: Principle of a rain sensor?

recall_a.en: Change in infrared light reflection by water on glass.

explain_simple.en: Water changes light, wiper starts.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Automatic climate control keeps a set cabin temperature using cabin, outside and sun-load sensors. It controls blower speed, blend door and compressor.

why.en: Comfort without manual changes.

recall_q.en: Name one sensor used in automatic climate control.

recall_a.en: Cabin temperature, ambient or sun-load sensor.

explain_simple.en: Set the temperature, car keeps it.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Car AC cycle: compressor → condenser (gives out heat) → receiver-drier → expansion valve → evaporator (absorbs cabin heat) → compressor.

why.en: Heat is moved from inside to outside.

recall_q.en: Which AC part absorbs heat from the cabin?

explain_simple.en: Evaporator cools inside; condenser heats outside.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Car AC refrigerant is R-134a; newer cars use R-1234yf, which harms the climate much less.

why.en: Old R-12 damaged the ozone layer.

recall_q.en: Common car AC refrigerant?

explain_simple.en: R-134a in most cars.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Noise control: sound insulation and damping sheets, rubber engine mounts, good silencers, sealed doors and active noise cancellation.

why.en: Less noise means less driver tiredness.

recall_q.en: Give two methods of vehicle noise control.

recall_a.en: Insulation, rubber mounts, silencer, active noise cancellation.

explain_simple.en: Block, absorb or cancel the noise.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Remote keyless entry (RKE) locks and unlocks doors by a radio signal from the key fob. Smart keys (passive entry) unlock when the key is near.

why.en: Convenience and security.

recall_q.en: How does a key fob communicate with the car?

explain_simple.en: Press button, radio unlocks car.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: An immobiliser has a transponder chip in the key. The engine ECU allows starting only if the chip's code matches.

why.en: A copied key or hot-wiring will not start the engine.

recall_q.en: Part in the key that works with an immobiliser?

explain_simple.en: Wrong key chip, no start.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: GPS finds position using signals from satellites. At least 4 satellites are needed for a 3D position. India's own system is NavIC.

why.en: Used for navigation and vehicle tracking.

recall_q.en: Minimum satellites for a 3D GPS fix?

explain_simple.en: Four satellites tell where you are.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Vehicle location tracking devices (VLTD) with emergency buttons are compulsory in public service vehicles (AIS-140) from 2019.

why.en: Passenger safety, especially women.

recall_q.en: Standard for vehicle tracking devices in buses and taxis?

explain_simple.en: Buses must have GPS tracker and panic button.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Speed governors (speed limiting devices) are needed in transport vehicles: usually 80 km/h; 60 km/h for dumpers and tankers; 40 km/h for school buses.

why.en: Heavy vehicles at high speed cause deadly crashes.

recall_q.en: Speed limit set by speed governor in school buses?

explain_simple.en: Most 80, tankers 60, school bus 40.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: TPMS (tyre pressure monitoring system) warns when a tyre's pressure is low.

why.en: Low pressure causes blowouts and poor mileage.

recall_q.en: What does TPMS monitor?

explain_simple.en: Warns of a soft tyre.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: ADAS (advanced driver assistance systems) includes automatic emergency braking (AEB), lane keep assist, blind spot warning and adaptive cruise.

why.en: Cameras and radar help prevent crashes.

recall_q.en: Which ADAS feature brakes by itself before a collision?

explain_simple.en: Car brakes if you don't.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

points.en: Active: ABS, EBD, traction control, ESC. Passive: belt, airbag.
ABS: sensors, ECU, modulator; >125 cc bikes ABS, ≤125 cc CBS.
Airbag fills in about 30 ms; SRS works with belt.
Speed alert 80/100/120; governor 80, tanker 60, school bus 40.
Immobiliser transponder; GPS 4 satellites; AIS-140 trackers.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A battery electric vehicle (BEV) runs only on a battery and electric motor. Main parts: battery, motor, controller (inverter), charger and BMS.

why.en: No engine, no fuel tank, no exhaust.

recall_q.en: Name three main parts of an electric vehicle.

explain_simple.en: Battery feeds motor through controller.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: EV benefits: zero tailpipe emission, low running cost, fewer moving parts, quiet running, full torque from zero speed and regenerative braking.

why.en: Electric motors are simple and efficient.

recall_q.en: Give two benefits of EVs.

recall_a.en: No tailpipe emission, low running cost.

explain_simple.en: Clean, cheap to run, quiet.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: EV challenges: high purchase cost, range anxiety, long charging time, few chargers, battery cost and disposal, and load on the power grid.

why.en: These slow down EV adoption.

recall_q.en: What is range anxiety?

recall_a.en: Fear that the battery will run out before reaching a charger.

explain_simple.en: Worry about running out of charge.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Most EVs use lithium-ion batteries. Common types are NMC (nickel manganese cobalt) and LFP (lithium iron phosphate).

why.en: Lithium-ion stores much energy for its weight.

recall_q.en: Most common battery type in EVs?

explain_simple.en: EVs use lithium-ion batteries.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: LFP batteries are safer and last more cycles but store less energy per kg. NMC stores more energy but costs more and is less heat-stable.

why.en: Choice depends on cost, safety and range.

recall_q.en: Which battery type is safer: LFP or NMC?

explain_simple.en: LFP safe and long life; NMC more range.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Battery capacity is measured in kilowatt-hours (kWh). More kWh means more range.

why.en: Energy stored decides distance.

recall_q.en: Unit of EV battery capacity?

explain_simple.en: Bigger kWh, longer drive.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

text.en: Question: A 30 kWh battery car uses 150 Wh per km. Find range.
Change to the same unit: 30 kWh = 30,000 Wh.

summary.en: Range = battery energy ÷ energy per km.
Keep units the same (Wh with Wh).

recall_q.en: 30 kWh battery, 150 Wh/km. Range?

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

text.en: Question: A 30 kWh battery is charged from empty with a 7.5 kW AC charger. Find time.
Time = 4 hours (a little more in real life because of losses).

summary.en: Real time is longer due to losses.

recall_q.en: 30 kWh with 7.5 kW charger takes about?

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: BMS (battery management system) watches each cell's voltage and temperature, finds the state of charge (SOC), balances cells and protects against overcharge and overheating.

why.en: Lithium cells are damaged or catch fire if abused.

recall_q.en: What does SOC mean?

recall_a.en: State of charge (how full the battery is).

explain_simple.en: BMS is the battery's guard.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Thermal runaway is when a lithium cell overheats, which makes it hotter still, leading to fire. Cooling systems and BMS prevent it.

why.en: Cause of EV and scooter fires.

recall_q.en: Uncontrolled heating that can cause a battery fire is called?

explain_simple.en: Heat makes more heat, then fire.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: AIS-156 sets battery safety tests for L-category (two and three wheeler) EVs. It was tightened in 2022–23 after e-scooter fires.

why.en: To stop battery fires.

recall_q.en: Which AIS standard covers EV battery safety for two-wheelers?

explain_simple.en: AIS-156 = scooter battery safety.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: EV motors: BLDC (brushless DC) in scooters, PMSM (permanent magnet synchronous motor) in most cars, and induction motors in some cars.

why.en: Brushless motors need little maintenance.

recall_q.en: Motor commonly used in electric scooters?

explain_simple.en: Scooters BLDC, cars mostly PMSM.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: A hub motor sits inside the wheel hub and drives the wheel directly. It is common in electric scooters.

why.en: No chain, belt or gearbox needed.

recall_q.en: Motor fitted inside the wheel is called?

explain_simple.en: Motor inside the wheel.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: The inverter changes battery DC into AC for the motor and controls its speed. A DC-DC converter lowers high voltage to 12 V for lights and accessories.

why.en: The motor runs on AC; accessories run on 12 V.

recall_q.en: Which part converts battery DC to AC for the motor?

explain_simple.en: Inverter: DC to AC.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: EVs usually have a single-speed reduction gear and no clutch or multi-speed gearbox.

why.en: Electric motors give high torque over a wide speed range.

recall_q.en: Does a typical EV have a multi-speed gearbox?

explain_simple.en: One gear is enough for an EV.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Regenerative braking uses the motor as a generator while slowing down. It charges the battery and reduces brake wear.

why.en: Energy that would become heat is saved.

recall_q.en: What is regenerative braking?

recall_a.en: Motor acts as generator during braking to charge the battery.

explain_simple.en: Braking charges the battery.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: AC charging uses the car's on-board charger to change AC to DC. DC fast charging sends DC directly to the battery, bypassing the on-board charger.

why.en: DC chargers are big and fast; on-board chargers are small.

recall_q.en: In DC fast charging, which part is bypassed?

explain_simple.en: AC slow via car's charger; DC fast direct.

cards.source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

learn.en: Common charging standards in India: CCS2 for DC fast charging of cars, Type 2 for AC; older Bharat AC-001 and DC-001 standards; CHAdeMO in a few vehicles.

why.en: Plug type must match the charger.

recall_q.en: Main DC fast charging connector for cars in India?

explain_simple.en: CCS2 is the common fast-charge plug.
